### Patterns

- `createNewTileEntity(world, meta)`: `if(meta >= 12) return new TileEntityMachineX(); if(meta >= 6) return new TileEntityProxyCombo().inventory().power().fluid(); return null;`. `BlockDummyable.overrideTileMeta` (with `setOverride()`/`resetOverride()`) is an unused static hook: nothing calls the setters and no `createNewTileEntity` reads the field (B-052). To use it, the block's `createNewTileEntity` must read it explicitly. It only affects TEs created during that server-side setBlock call, not TEs reloaded from NBT or created on the client.
- Placement: `onBlockPlaced` stores the clicked face as temporary meta. `onBlockPlacedBy` handles EntityPlayer placers only. Facing comes from yaw (`i==0->2, 1->5, 2->3, 3->4`) only when the top or bottom face was clicked; otherwise facing = the clicked face. Then `dir = getDirModified(facing)`, `o = -getOffset()`, and the core goes at `(x + facing.offsetX * o, y + getHeightOffset(), z + facing.offsetZ * o)`, with two exceptions. A bottom-face click lowers it by U+D (`oy -= dim[0] + dim[1]`). A side-face click replaces ox/oz with `x/z + face.offset * rotate(getDimensions(), dir)[opposite face]`, so the footprint starts at the clicked cell. Next, `checkRequirement` failing refunds the item and aborts. On the server only, the core is set with `getMetaForCore(...)`, then `IPersistentNBT.restoreData`, then `fillSpace`. Hooks: `getDirModified` (5 overrides, 3 more callers in custom `onBlockPlacedBy`s), `getHeightOffset` (16), `getMetaForCore` (PylonLarge, must return 12-15), `isLegacyMonoblock` (MachinePress, MachineEPress).
- XL multiblocks override `checkRequirement`/`fillSpace` with extra `MultiblockHandlerXR` calls and `makeExtra` on ports; `getAllDimensions()` (rows of 6, or 9 with fwd/up/lat offsets) and `getAABBExtras()` drive ONLY the client placement wireframe, which rotates with `facing` while the real footprint uses `getDirModified(facing)`; keep them in sync by hand.
- Break/drops: breaking a dummy removes its neighbour toward the core (`breakBlock`). Breaking the core triggers no `breakBlock` cascade, but every removal synchronously notifies its neighbours, and their `destroyIfOrphan` removes the rest recursively in the same tick. This runs server only, is skipped while `safeRem` is set, and leaves dummies whose 3x3x3 neighbourhood is not fully loaded. `breakBlock` spills any `ISidedInventory` at the broken position. Drops come from `onBlockHarvested` (`harvestBlock` only adds stats), and creative mode drops nothing.
- Persistent NBT: TE `writeNBT` must build a child compound and `nbt.setTag(IPersistentNBT.NBT_PERSISTENT_KEY, data)`; `readNBT` reads `nbt.getCompoundTag(NBT_PERSISTENT_KEY)`; block overrides `getDrops(...) { return IPersistentNBT.getDrops(world, x, y, z, this); }` and implements `IPersistentInfoProvider`; non-Dummyable blocks call `restoreData` in `onBlockPlacedBy` and override `onBlockHarvested`/`harvestBlock` as `MachineBattery` does.
- GUI: `standardOpenBehavior` works on the server side. It finds the core and opens at core coordinates (a proxy TE is not an IGUIProvider), and returns true while sneaking and on the client without opening anything. FML opens a server-side GUI only if `provideContainer` returns non-null, so container-less screens must call `FMLNetworkHandler.openGui` on the client at the core coordinates (see RadioTelex, RadioAUTOCAL). IDs are passed through unchanged: 0 by convention, -1 for the Electrolyser's last selected tab, and 14 blocks pass the clicked `side` (this works only because those TEs ignore the ID).
- Registration: fluent chain in `ModBlocks.initializeBlock()` ending in `setBlockTextureName`; `register(x)` for ItemBlockBase; nested `public static class TileEntityX` inside the Block file is accepted (MachineCapacitor, Floodlight, BlockPWR, FluidPump, CableDiode, BlockCablePaintable) but still needs a `TileMappings` entry.
- Rendering: BlockDummyable is invisible; TESR bound in `ClientProxy` with `IItemRendererProvider`; each TESR's rotation (any fixed pre-rotation plus the meta switch) is tuned to its model. RenderChemicalPlant applies a fixed 90 degrees before its switch (switch 0 at meta 12, net 90), while RenderSawmill has no pre-rotation (net 0 at meta 13). Copy the TESR that belongs to the model you reuse.
- `IBomb.explode(world, x, y, z)` returns `BombReturnCode`: `DETONATED`, `TRIGGERED`, `LAUNCHED` (success; `wasSuccessful()`), `ERROR_MISSING_COMPONENT`, `ERROR_INCOMPATIBLE` (target implements `IBomb` but refuses, e.g. a locked blast door), `ERROR_NO_BOMB` (used by the caller when the block is not an `IBomb`), `UNDEFINED` (no feedback); `ItemDetonator` reports `getUnlocalizedMessage()` (`bomb.*` lang keys) through `ChatBuilder`. Det cord: blocks implement `IDetConnectible.canConnectToDetCord(world, x, y, z, dir)` (default true); `IDetConnectible.isConnectible(...)` is the static probe. Fluid ducts: right-clicking `FluidDuctBase` with an `IItemFluidIdentifier` (`ItemFluidIDMulti` etc.) calls `id.getType(world, x, y, z, stack)` and re-types the `TileEntityPipeBaseNT` via `setType`.

### How-to

- Rectangular multiblock: block `extends BlockDummyable`; `createNewTileEntity` as above; `getDimensions()` in the SOUTH frame; `getOffset()`; `fillSpace(world, x, y, z, dir, o) { super.fillSpace(...); x += dir.offsetX * o; z += dir.offsetZ * o; makeExtra(world, px, py, pz); ... }` (copy `LaunchPad`/`MachineCoker`; `MachineChemicalPlant`'s `x -= dir.offsetX` is the same thing for offset 1); `onBlockActivated` -> `standardOpenBehavior(..., 0)`; TE implements `IGUIProvider` (e.g. `TileEntityMachineChemicalPlant` L271-272); `TileMappings.writeMappings()` put; `ModBlocks` init (copy `machine_chemical_plant` ~L2499) + `register`; TESR in `ClientProxy`; lang `tile.machine_x.name`. A `.desc` tooltip (`$` line breaks, shown with LSHIFT) also needs the block to `implements ITooltipProvider` with `addInformation(...) { this.addStandardInfo(stack, player, list, ext); }`, as in MachineCoker, and to be registered with `register(x)` (ItemBlockBase). Exemplar `blocks/machine/MachineChemicalPlant.java` (it has no tooltip).
- Irregular multiblock: override `checkRequirement`/`fillSpace` with matching extra `MultiblockHandlerXR.checkSpace`/`fillSpace` calls (same origin, dims and dir in both). `fillSpace` never writes a box's origin and points every other cell of the box at it, overwriting what is there. Each extra box must therefore be centred on the core or on a cell an earlier box already filled (MachineCoker, relative to the core: (x, y+1, z) and (x+-2, y+1, z+-2)). A box that only touches the body leaves orphans, and a box that contains the core off-centre overwrites the core. `getDimensions()` also sets the wall/ceiling placement offsets. If `fillSpace` calls super (MachineCoker) it must stay the main body, so side-face placement ignores the extra boxes. If it does not (MachineChungus), make it the bounding envelope. Add `getAllDimensions()` rows for the preview; `getAABBExtras` and `getHeightOffset` are optional. Exemplar `MachineCoker.java`.
- Rotated hitbox: add `AxisAlignedBB` entries to `this.bounding` in the ctor and `this.maxY = 0.999D`. The rotation passed to `getAABBRotationOffset` is `dir.getRotation(UP)`, so author boxes with -X as the machine's forward (as if core meta were 14/WEST) and verify in-game against `MachineSawmill`. Exemplar `MachineCentrifuge.java`.
- Single-block machine with GUI, two routes. (a) Extend `BlockContainer` and write it by hand: yaw -> meta (`i==0->2, 1->5, 2->3, 3->4`) in `onBlockPlacedBy`; `onBlockActivated` -> `FMLNetworkHandler.openGui(player, MainRegistry.instance, 0, world, x, y, z)`; spill the inventory in `breakBlock`, then call `super`. Exemplar `MachineBattery.java` (deprecated, creative-hidden family; ctor `(Material, long maxPower)`). (b) Extend `BlockMachineBase(Material, guiID)`, which already opens `guiID` and spills ISidedInventory, and set `rotatable = true` in the ctor or it never writes a facing meta. Exemplar `MachineDiesel.java`. In both routes the TE implements `IGUIProvider` (GUIHandler checks the TE first, then the Block) and needs a `TileMappings` entry.
- Cable/pipe block: extend `BlockContainer`, own `renderID`, bounds via `Library.canConnect`/`canConnectFluid`; ducts extend `FluidDuctBase` for identifier-item typing. Exemplar `FluidDuctStandard.java`.
- Crane: extend `BlockCraneBase`, `createNewTileEntity` -> `TileEntityCraneBase` subclass, register 13 `iconDirectional*` icons, `IEnterableBlock`. Exemplar `CraneInserter.java`.
- Conveyor: extend `BlockConveyorBendable`, no TE, drop `ModItems.conveyor_wand`. Exemplar `BlockConveyor.java`.
- Explosive: `BlockTNTBase` (icons `_side/_top/_bottom`), `BlockDetonatable(mat, encouragement, flammability, popFuse, detonateOnCollision, detonateOnShot)`, or `BlockChargeBase`; implement `IFuckingExplode.explodeEntity`; register nukes with the 2-arg form (no tooltips) or `ItemBlockBase.class` (charges do). Exemplar `BlockTNTBase.java`.
- Redstone/detonator on a multiblock: `IBomb.explode` finds the core and delegates; `onNeighborBlockChange` forwards to the core then calls `super` (orphan cleanup). Exemplar `LaunchPad.java`.

### Gotchas

- `makeExtra` silently no-ops when the target is not this block or meta > 5: wrong port coordinates give a machine with no working ports and no error.
- Port flags and the proxy class persist: each proxy saves `inv/power/conductor/fluid/metal/heat` in NBT (TileEntityProxyCombo.java:415-442), and Combo and Dyn have separate TileMappings ids. Changing the flags, or switching Combo to Dyn, in `createNewTileEntity` only affects ports placed afterwards. Machines already in a world keep their old ports until broken and re-placed, or until a migration rewrites the proxies.
- `safeRem`/`overrideTileMeta` are static globals: an exception inside `fillSpace`/`makeExtra` leaves `safeRem = true`.
- `BlockDummyable.positions`/`internalPlayers` are unsynchronized instance scratch state shared by client and server in single-player.
- Owner's pack: ntmrba 1.3's `AccessorBlockDummyable` (`@Invoker`, required mixin config) pins `getMetaForCore(World, int, int, int, EntityPlayer, int)` (L317), `getDirModified(ForgeDirection)` (L327) and `checkRequirement(World, int, int, int, ForgeDirection, int)` (L331). Renaming them or changing their parameters crashes the game when `BlockDummyable` loads; add an overload instead.
- Owner's pack: ntmrba's `MixinTileEntityPylonBase` merges unannotated `validate()` (`func_145829_t`), `invalidate()` (`func_145843_s`) and `onChunkUnload()` into `TileEntityPylonBase`, each calling the superclass version and then updating ntmrba's client wire list. `TileEntityPylonBase` declares none of them today; one added there is silently replaced by the mixin copy at runtime (server logic included, since single-player shares the class), so put pylon lifecycle work in `TileEntityCableBaseNT` or in a differently named helper. With `OPTIMIZE_WIRES` on, ntmrba also draws wires from its own list instead of `RenderPylonBase.renderLinesGeneric`, so edits there do not show in the pack.
- Custom `fillSpace` with a different origin/dir creates dummy chains pointing at the box origin; any gap = orphan self-deletion.
- `TileEntityProxyBase.cachedPosition` is written only by `TileEntityCustomMachine.checkStructure` (L409), persisted in NBT, and checked before `findCore`/`IProxyController`. A core swapped in place needs no action, because `getTE()` re-reads the position on every call and ProxyCombo's cached `tile` refreshes once the old TE is invalid. The cache clears itself only when a lookup finds no TE (or a proxy) there. Nothing clears it when the structure check fails, so ports keep delegating to their last controller, or to any non-proxy TE that takes the controller's position before the next lookup.
- `MachineSawmill` (L125-146), `MachineStirling` (L97-117) and `MachineHeatBoiler` (L84-104) find the core again after `super.onBlockPlacedBy` from yaw only (`x + dir.offsetX * o`, no `getHeightOffset`), so wall and ceiling placement put the core elsewhere and the item-damage-1 variants (bladeless, cogless, exploded) lose that state.
- `BlockDummyable.getSettings` (L609-616) and `infoForDisplay` (L627-634) use the `findCore` result without a null check (`pasteSettings` at L621 has one), so the copy tool on an orphaned dummy throws an NPE; `infoForDisplay` also passes the dummy's x/y/z to the core TE instead of `pos[]`.
- World-gen: `Component.placeCore` ignores `getDirModified` and `getMetaForCore` (javadoc at `world/gen/component/Component.java:833`), and NBT structures rotate core/extra metas as horizontal facings through `BlockDummyable.transformMeta` (L636-656), which is wrong for PylonLarge's 45-degree metas.
- `BlockCraneBase.onBlockActivated` returns false when holding `ItemTooling`/`ItemConveyorWand`; `PneumoTube` checks `ToolType.SCREWDRIVER` first.
- `FluidDuctStandard.getPickBlock` returns `ModItems.fluid_duct` with the fluid ID as damage; `BlockCustomMachine` encodes config index as damage >= 100.
- `DummyOldBase` implements `IEnergyConnectorBlock`/`IFluidConnectorBlock`/`IDummy`; `DummyBlockBlast` extends `BlockContainer` directly.
- Smells: only 3 TODOs (`pile/BlockGraphiteDrilledBase.java:178,222`, `MachineSolar.java:17`); item-spill code (the `nextInt(21) + 10` loop) duplicated in 50 block classes (27 machine, 13 bomb, 6 network, plus BlockDummyable, 2 generic and 1 turret; 53 files codebase-wide); `FluidDuctStandard` has a large commented-out `getItem` with debug prints; `drawPlacementHighlight` is ~250 lines of tessellator code in the Block class.

---

## 5. Tile entities: base classes and common machines

### Purpose

`com/hbm/tileentity/` holds the hierarchy every machine builds on (`TileEntityLoadedBase` -> `TileEntityMachineBase` -> `TileEntityMachinePolluting`, plus proxies), the plug-in interfaces (`IGUIProvider`, `IBufPacketReceiver`, `IConfigurableMachine`, `IUpgradeInfoProvider`, `IControlReceiver` (`interfaces/`), `IPersistentNBT`, `IFluidCopiable`, `IConditionalInvAccess`, `IRepairable`) and `TileMappings`. `machine/` has 189 top-level files (290 recursive). Energy/fluid behaviour is inherited from the `api.hbm` default-method interfaces and driven from `updateEntity`.

### Key files

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `com/hbm/tileentity/TileEntityLoadedBase.java` | Root: `isLoaded` (set false ONLY in `onChunkUnload`), `muffled`/`tilted`, `markChanged()`, `createAudioLoop()`/`rebootAudio()`/`getVolume()`, `serialize`/`deserialize`, `networkPackNT(range)` (BufPacket, precompiled on main thread, dedupe against `lastPackedBuf` except every 20th tick, queued via `PacketThreading`), `checkTilt` (one floor block per 20 ticks). |
| `TileEntityMachineBase.java` | Abstract `ISidedInventory` base: `slots[]`, `getName()`, NBT `items`, default deny-all side access, `breatheAir()` (atmosphere check; TODO consume from tanks), deprecated `handleButtonPacket`, `isUseableByPlayer` (`getDistanceSq <= 128`). Imports Forge's `FluidTank` for `getGaugeScaled`, not HBM's. |
| `TileEntityMachinePolluting.java` | + `IFluidStandardSender` (deprecated shim) with three smoke tanks; `pollute(...)`, `sendSmoke()`. |
| `TileEntityInventoryBase.java`, `TileEntityTickingBase.java` | Non-ticking inventory base (default `getAccessibleSlotsFromSide` = `{0}`), ticking base without inventory. |
| `TileMappings.java` | `writeMappings()` -> private `put(Class, String... names)` (extra names = alternative ids for `registerTileEntityWithAlternatives`); collects `IConfigurableMachine` classes into `configurables`; `Compat.blacklistAccelerator(clazz)` (Torcherino). |
| `IUpgradeInfoProvider.java`, `inventory/UpgradeManagerNT.java`, `items/machine/ItemMachineUpgrade.java` | Upgrades: `public UpgradeManagerNT upgradeManager = new UpgradeManagerNT(this);` + `upgradeManager.checkSlots(slots, first, last)` each tick (`last` is inclusive), then `getLevel(UpgradeType)`. Never pair the deprecated no-arg constructor (used by the ElectricFurnace exemplar) with the 3-arg `checkSlots`: `owner` is null, `checkSlotsInternal` returns immediately and every level stays 0 without error. The TE must implement `IUpgradeInfoProvider`, whose `getValidUpgrades()` filters and caps the levels. Rescans happen only when a slot's ItemStack reference changes (`ItemStack` has no `equals`, so `Arrays.equals` compares identity). The mutex logic (`LM_SMELTER/SHREDDER/CENTRIFUGE/CRYSTALLIZER`, `mutexType` never reset, strict `>`, so after any rescan a same- or lower-ordinal mutex upgrade is ignored, B-056) is currently unreachable: no upgrade item carries an LM_* type and no TE accepts one. |
| `inventory/fluid/tank/FluidTank.java` | HBM tank: `loadTank/unloadTank/setType`, `serialize/deserialize`, `renderTank`/`renderTankInfo`; `withPressure`/`setTankType` are no-ops when unchanged. `writeToNBT(nbt, key)` writes `<key>`, `<key>_max`, `<key>_type`, `<key>_p`. `readFromNBT` replaces the constructor capacity with the saved `<key>_max` when it is > 0, so capacity changes in code or config do not reach existing tiles unless `changeTankSize` is called afterwards. It clamps the fill to that saved value, so a missing `_max` zeroes the fill (B-055). Type (name-compat, then id) and pressure are restored too. |
| `machine/TileEntityMachineElectricFurnace.java`, `TileEntityMachineCentrifuge.java`, `TileEntityMachineDiesel.java`, `TileEntityMachineChemicalPlant.java` | Exemplars: simplest receiver (`updateConnections` every 40 ticks), IConfigurableMachine + audio + EC info, polluting provider + IControlReceiver + IFluidCopiable, multiblock core with `DirPos[] getConPos()` and tank arrays. |
| `packet/toclient/BufPacket.java`, `packet/toserver/NBTControlPacket.java`, `packet/toserver/AuxButtonPacket.java` | TE sync; GUI control (checks `hasPermission(player)`, then calls `receiveControl(player, nbt)` and `receiveControl(nbt)`); deprecated button packet: instanceof chain, and then `handleButtonPacket` for EVERY `TileEntityMachineBase`, with NO permission, distance or GUI check. Any client can toggle machines or start bomb countdowns (`TileEntityNukeBalefire`, `TileEntityAntimatter`) at arbitrary coordinates, so never use it for new controls. Both server handlers call `getTileEntity` at the client-supplied coordinates before any check, which loads or generates the chunk if it is not loaded. |
| `sound/AudioWrapper.java`, `AudioWrapperClient.java` | Server no-op / client loop handles. |

### Patterns

- Census (machine/ top-level): 92 extend `TileEntityMachineBase`, 33 `TileEntityLoadedBase`, 23 raw `TileEntity`, 9 `TileEntityMachinePolluting`, 3 `TileEntityTickingBase`; rbmk uses `TileEntityRBMKBase` -> `ActiveBase` -> `SlottedBase`; albion `TileEntityCooledBase`.
- Sync for ticking machines is ByteBuf: override `serialize`/`deserialize` (super first, identical order) and call `networkPackNT(range)` unconditionally each server tick. Ranges in use: 15-25 for small single blocks, 50 typical, 100-150 for multiblocks, 250 for the largest. Vanilla NBT sync is also still used: 11 classes in tileentity/ (`TileEntityFoundryBase`, `TileEntityCrateBase`, `TileEntityPipeBaseNT`, `TileEntityPipelineBase`, `TileEntityPylonBase`, `TileEntityCraneBase`, `TileEntityPneumoTube`, `TileEntityDishControl`, radio torches, `TileEntityCombatDropPod`) and ~17 TEs nested in blocks/ override `getDescriptionPacket`/`onDataPacket` with an NBT `S35PacketUpdateTileEntity`. For some (foundry, crates, pipes, pylons) it is the only sync; others use it for the initial state alongside `networkPackNT`. `INBTPacketReceiver`/`networkPack(NBT)` no longer exist (only a commented-out reference in `TileEntityMachineIGenerator`, whose `updateEntity` is entirely commented out).
- Registration: `put(TileEntityX.class, "tileentity_x")` inside `TileMappings.writeMappings()` or one of its private helpers. Machines go in `putMachines()`, and OC-only tiles inside the `ocPresent` guard in `putNetwork()`. `MainRegistry` (L339-345) loops the resulting HashMap. Ids are persisted in saves and never renamed. Most are lowercase `tileentity_<name>`, but legacy ids keep typos and casing: six `tilentity_` ids (e.g. `tilentity_diFurnace`, `tilentity_objtester`), plus `tileentity_satellitereceicer`, `tileentity_nuke_Antimatter`, `tileentity_pioe_anchor`.
- GUI: TE implements `IGUIProvider`; `provideGUI` carries `@SideOnly(Side.CLIENT)` by convention (90 of 94 in machine/); block opens with ID 0.
- Control: `IControlReceiver.hasPermission(player)` (distance < 25 or `isUseableByPlayer`) + `receiveControl(nbt)` + `markChanged()`; GUI sends `NBTControlPacket`. Five tiles use the player-aware overload (`TileEntityLaunchPadRocket`, `TileEntityMachineRadarNT`, `TileEntityOrbitalStationLauncher`, `TileEntityElectrolyser`, and `BlockWandStructure.TileEntityWandStructure`). Do not extend `AuxButtonPacket` (9 classes still override `handleButtonPacket`).
- Config: `IConfigurableMachine` with `public static` fields. `MachineDynConfig.initialize()` (PreLoad, `MainRegistry` L336, right after `TileMappings.writeMappings()`) builds one throwaway dummy per class with `newInstance()` before `readIfPresent`, so constructors must be public, no-arg and side-effect free. Only that dummy's constructor sees default statics. Real tiles are built later (placement or chunk load) and see the configured values. For tiles that already exist, NBT wins over the config: `FluidTank.readFromNBT` replaces the capacity with the saved `<key>_max`, and Diesel restores `powerCap` from NBT. Changing `I:fuelCap`/`L:powerCap` therefore affects only newly placed generators unless the tile calls `tank.changeTankSize(cap)` (and resets the cap) after reading NBT.
- Audio: `createAudioLoop()` -> `MainRegistry.proxy.getLoopedSound(id, x, y, z, volume, range, pitch, keepAliveTicks)` (8-arg; the 7-arg overload is deprecated; pitch argument is dropped by the proxy, call `updatePitch`); client branch start/`rebootAudio`/`keepAlive`/`updateVolume(getVolume(1F))`; stop in `onChunkUnload` (call `super` first) and `invalidate`.
- Pollution: `PollutionHandler.incrementPollution(world, x, y, z, PollutionType.SOOT, PollutionHandler.SOOT_PER_SECOND)` once per 20 ticks, or extend `TileEntityMachinePolluting` and `pollute(...)` + `sendSmoke(...)`.
- Render culling: override `getRenderBoundingBox()` with a cached AABB and `@SideOnly getMaxRenderDistanceSquared()` (206 TEs do).

### How-to

- Single-block electric machine: `extends TileEntityMachineBase implements IEnergyReceiverMK2, IGUIProvider, IUpgradeInfoProvider`; `super(slotCount)`; `getName()` -> `"container.foo"`; `slots_io` + `isItemValidForSlot`/`canExtractItem`/`getAccessibleSlotsFromSide` (battery slot `instanceof IBatteryItem`); NBT + `serialize`/`deserialize`; server tick: `trySubscribe` per side, `power = Library.chargeTEFromItems(slots, batterySlot, power, maxPower)`, `upgradeManager.checkSlots(slots, a, b)`, work, `networkPackNT(50)`; `provideContainer`/`provideGUI`; `TileMappings` put; block `extends BlockContainer`; `ModBlocks`; `ContainerFoo`/`GUIFoo`; TESR + `ClientProxy` bind; lang; recipe. Exemplar `TileEntityMachineElectricFurnace.java`, with caveats. Do not copy its on/off block swap: `MachineElectricFurnace.updateBlockState` runs on every server tick except the one where a smelt completes. Each call does `setBlock` with meta 0 plus a second meta write, which runs `breakBlock`, removes the TE, constructs a throwaway new TE, and then re-inserts the old one, with neighbour and client block updates every tick. Swap only when the on/off state actually changes, or keep a synced flag and render it. Also do not copy its 40-tick `updateConnections` (subscribe at least every 20 ticks) or its deprecated `new UpgradeManagerNT()`.
- Multiblock core with fluid + power: `implements IEnergyReceiverMK2, IFluidStandardTransceiverMK2, IGUIProvider`; `FluidTank[] inputTanks/outputTanks`; `for(DirPos pos : getConPos()) { trySubscribe(worldObj, pos); trySubscribe(type, worldObj, pos) per input; tryProvide(tank, worldObj, pos) per output; }`; `getReceivingTanks/getSendingTanks/getAllTanks`; render bbox. Exemplar `TileEntityMachineChemicalPlant.java`. Ports are exactly the cells `getConPos()` returns: the core's `trySubscribe`/`tryProvide` check only the neighbouring cable's `canConnect`, never the machine's own. The machine's `canConnect(ForgeDirection)` (energy, default `dir != UNKNOWN`) and the separate fluid `canConnect(FluidType, ForgeDirection)` are consulted only for cable/duct attachment (`Library.canConnect`/`canConnectFluid`: render and hitbox) and for direct pushes from an adjacent provider or `CableDiode`. On a multiblock, `TileEntityProxyCombo` forwards them to the core with the direction only, not the position. Override them to match `getConPos()` so cables do not visually attach where no port exists. ChemicalPlant's hard-coded `getConPos()` (L175-190) works only because its 3x3 footprint is symmetric. For a machine with a facing, derive the ports from the core meta: `ForgeDirection dir = ForgeDirection.getOrientation(getBlockMetadata() - BlockDummyable.offset); ForgeDirection rot = dir.getRotation(ForgeDirection.UP);` then `new DirPos(xCoord + dir.offsetX * n + rot.offsetX * m, y, zCoord + dir.offsetZ * n + rot.offsetZ * m, <direction pointing from the machine out to that cell>)`. Exemplar `oil/TileEntityMachineCatalyticReformer.java:133-145`. The machine block next to each port cell should be a `makeExtra` proxy (area 4). Without one the subscription still works, but cables will not visually attach there and adjacent providers cannot push in directly.
- Configurable numbers: see area 1; exemplar `TileEntityMachineCentrifuge.java`.
- GUI button: `IControlReceiver` + `PacketDispatcher.wrapper.sendToServer(new NBTControlPacket(data, te.xCoord, te.yCoord, te.zCoord))` from `mouseClicked` (or `GuiInfoContainer.clickSendFlag`). Exemplar `TileEntityMachineDiesel.java`.
- Loop sound: `NTMSounds` constant + `sounds.json`; `AudioWrapper audio`; `createAudioLoop()`; client branch gated on a synced running flag; `onChunkUnload() { super.onChunkUnload(); stop }` and `invalidate()`. Exemplar `TileEntityMachineCentrifuge.java`. Note that Centrifuge, Diesel and ChemicalPlant (all exemplars in this section) skip `super.onChunkUnload()` (B-061); always add it when copying them.
- Smoke-tank pollution: extend `TileEntityMachinePolluting(slotCount, bufferMb)`; `getSendingTanks()` returns `getSmokeTanks()` + own outputs; call `pollute(fluidType, FluidReleaseType.BURN, amount)` at a fixed rate (Diesel: every 5 ticks), then `sendSmoke(x+dx, y+dy, z+dz, dir)` per side. NOTE: `amount` is currently ignored (`TileEntityMachinePolluting.java:56-57` calls `pollute(entry.getKey(), entry.getValue())`; the `* amount` was dropped upstream in 7532f57f7). Each call therefore adds one mB's worth of the fluid's `FT_Polluting` burn map, i.e. ceil(value*100) mB of smoke per type, whatever is passed. Scale by call frequency or call `pollute(PollutionType, float)` directly. The static `FT_Polluting.pollute(world, x, y, z, type, release, mB)` does multiply by mB. The base class saves smoke tanks to NBT as `smoke0..2` but does not put them in `serialize`, and Diesel's own `serialize` (`TileEntityMachineDiesel.java:221-228`) writes only its fuel tank, so the client never sees the smoke fill; a GUI that shows smoke must serialize the tanks itself. Exemplar `TileEntityMachineDiesel.java`.

### Gotchas

- `super.onChunkUnload()` is the only place `isLoaded` becomes false; 25 of ~50 `TileEntityLoadedBase` overrides skip it (B-061). 1.7.10 calls `onChunkUnload()`, never `invalidate()`, on unload, so such a tile is not dropped by `NodeNet.isBadLink` on the next net tick. It stays a receiver/provider until its 3000 ms wall-clock subscription expires (a network merge re-stamps it, `NodeNet.java:48-49`), and `TileAccessCache` returns it for up to 60 ticks for direct pushes. During that window the net moves power or fluid into or out of a tile whose chunk has already been saved and unloaded.
- `networkPackNT` dedupes identical buffers except every 20th tick; `TileEntityLoadedBase` does not override `getDescriptionPacket`, so a freshly loaded client sees state only after that resend. `serialize()` must be deterministic.
- `MachineDynConfig` swallows every error. A missing public no-arg ctor silently drops the machine from `hbmMachines.json` (B-059). A malformed file (anything Gson's lenient parser rejects) throws into the empty outer catch (L88): ALL machines silently keep their defaults and the file is not rewritten. An exception inside one machine's `readIfPresent` leaves that machine partly configured, and the rewrite then replaces the user's bad entry with the current values.
- Subscriptions expire after 3000 ms of wall-clock time, not ticks, so call `trySubscribe`/`tryProvide` at least every 20 ticks. `ElectricFurnace.updateConnections` runs every 40 ticks. On its own it sees a new cable within 40 ticks, because its own cached null (`TileAccessCache`, 20 ticks) expires before its next probe. If another tile caches a null for the same cell just before the cable is placed, the delay can approach ~60 ticks. Below ~13.3 TPS the 40-tick refresh also exceeds the 3000 ms timeout, so the furnace drops off its net for part of each cycle.
- `BlockDummyable.breakBlock` already spills `ISidedInventory` contents of the core; only single-block `BlockContainer` machines need their own spill.
- `TileEntityMachineCentrifuge.provideExtraInfo` writes both `setBoolean` and `setInteger` under `B_ACTIVE`.
- Tiles do not chunkload; `ChunkLoaderManager`/`IChunkLoader` are entity-side (missiles, shells, drones, planes).
- ElectricFurnace-style on/off block swapping (static `keepInventory` + `world.setBlock`) breaks `findCore` if copied into a BlockDummyable.
- Smells: `TileEntityMachineAssemblyFactory.java:48` TODO base class; `TileEntityMachineWarController.java:40-58` auto-generated stubs; `TileEntityReactorResearch.java:51` TODO fix reactor control; `TileEntityFEL.java:70` @Spaghetti; `IRTGUser.java` three `@Untested @Beta` overloads; 22 classes (including the ElectricFurnace and Centrifuge exemplars and the bases `TileEntityOilDrillBase`/`TileEntityMachineCompressorBase`) still use the deprecated `new UpgradeManagerNT()` + `checkSlots(this, slots, a, b)`. Only 7 use `new UpgradeManagerNT(this)` + `checkSlots(slots, a, b)` (e.g. `TileEntityMachineChemicalPlant`). When migrating, change the constructor and the `checkSlots` call together (see the Upgrades row in Key files).

---

## 6. Tile entities: RBMK, fusion, Albion, bombs, turrets, deco

### Purpose

Server-side simulation tiles for the big set pieces: RBMK (per-column heat + tick-batched neutron streams + gamerule "dials"), fusion torus and peripherals (UNINOS GenNode klystron/plasma nets), Albion particle accelerator (a `Particle` walking `IParticleUser` tiles), assembly nukes and launch pads (`IBomb`/`IRadarCommandReceiver`), `BulletConfig`-driven turrets, deco tiles, plus research/breeding/ZIRNOX/PWR reactors. Machine tiles follow the area-5 skeleton and mostly expose OC `@Callback`s and ROR hooks. Assembly nukes, the custom nuke, landmine, crashed bomb, `TileEntityFusionTorusStruct`, `TileEntityFusionCollector`, `TileEntityZirnoxDestroyed` and the deco tiles (all but `TileEntityLanternBehemoth`) are plain `TileEntity` subclasses without BufPacket sync, OC or ROR.

### Patterns

- One-shot events piggyback on `BufPacket`: set a flag, `networkPackNT`, clear it; `serialize` writes a boolean discriminator (`TileEntityTurretTauon.shot`, `Maxwell.shot`, `Richard.isTurretPacket`, `PWRController.isPrinting`). This works because `networkPackNT` compiles the buffer synchronously (`TileEntityLoadedBase.java:91-93`) before `PacketThreading` sends it; its dedup check (L102) drops a packet identical to the last one sent unless `worldTime % 20 == 0`, so a one-shot packet that equals the previous one is lost.
- Client interpolation via `sync*` fields and a countdown set in `deserialize`: `turnProgress` in the autoloader, `sync` in launch pad large. The crane console declares `turnProgress` but never assigns it, so it snaps to `sync*` every tick. Turrets set `turnProgress = 2` but never read it; they copy `syncRotation*` into `rotation*` each client tick.
- RBMK lid state lives in block metadata; `RBMKBase.onScrew` must call `node.removeLid()` or the cached neutron node goes stale; unlidded columns leak radiation.
- Fusion transport: `UniNodespace.getNode(world, x, y, z, Provider.THE_PROVIDER)` else `new GenNode(provider, BlockPos).setConnections(DirPos)` + `createNode`; `node.net.addReceiver/addProvider(this)` every tick; `destroyNode` in `invalidate()`. Klystron/Plasma nets have empty `update()` and no purge; `provideKyU` guards with `isLoaded() && !isInvalid()`.
- Registration: launch pads, landmine, balefire, antimatter, compact launcher, launch table and crashed bomb are `put` in the `writeMappings()` body (L101-197); `putBombs()` only holds assembly nukes, custom nuke, charges; RBMK in `putRBMK()`, fusion in `putFusion()` (incl. `TileEntityFusionKlystronCreative`), turrets in `putTurrets()`.
- OC: `@Optional.InterfaceList(...)`, `SimpleComponent, CompatHandler.OCComponent`, `@Callback(direct = true) @Optional.Method(modid = "OpenComputers")`; see area 18 for the `methods()`/`invoke()` semantics.
- Tilt: `checkTilt(TiltType.CONFIG, true)` + `getFloorCount()/getFloorPosFromIndex()` (torus: 6x6 = 36 samples at 2-block spacing over 11x11; ZIRNOX: 3x3 = 9 samples via `standardFloor5x5` over its 5x5 footprint).
- RBMK gamerule dials (`RBMKDials`, created on server start, refreshed on `/gamerule`, read through typed getters): `dialPassiveCooling`, `dialPassiveCoolingInner`, `dialColumnHeatFlow`, `dialDiffusionMod`, `dialHeatProvision`, `dialColumnHeight`, `dialBoilerHeatConsumption`, `dialControlSpeed`, `dialControlSurgeMod`, `dialReactivityMod`, `dialModeratorEfficiency`, `dialAbsorberEfficiency`, `dialAbsorberHeatConversion`, `dialReflectorEfficiency`, `dialFluxRange`, `dialOutgasserSpeedMod`, `dialReasimBoilers`, `dialReasimBoilerSpeed`, `dialReasimRange`, `dialDisableDepletion`, `dialDisableXenon`, `dialDisableMeltdowns`, `dialEnableMeltdownOverpressure`, `dialEnablePermaScrap`, `dialSaveDials`. Per-rod flux weighting by neutron type is the private `TileEntityRBMKRod.fluxFromType(NType)`.

### How-to

- New RBMK column: extend `TileEntityRBMKBase` (passive) or `TileEntityRBMKSlottedBase(slots)` (GUI); `getConsoleType()` (add a `ColumnType` at the END with a free texture offset; extend `RBMKColumn.getFancyStats` if it shows stats); `onMelt(reduce)` with `spawnDebris`; keep `super.updateEntity()` at the end. If neutrons interact: add an `RBMKType` constant, return it from `getRBMKType()`, and add a branch for it in `RBMKNeutronStream.runStreamInteraction` (RBMKNeutronHandler.java:312-364). The existing branches cast to their own TE classes, and the `IRBMKFluxReceiver` branch dispatches only ROD and OUTGASSER, so implementing `IRBMKFluxReceiver` alone does nothing. `makeNode` needs no change: it copies `getRBMKType()`/`hasLid()` into the node. A column that only moderates returns the existing `RBMKType.MODERATOR` (as `TileEntityRBMKModerator` does); overriding `isModerated()` adds moderation only to a column whose type is not `OTHER`, because `OTHER`/null nodes are skipped before that check (L297-310). Block: extend `RBMKBase` (or `RBMKPipedBase` for piped columns) and copy `blocks/machine/rbmk/RBMKOutgasser.java`. (`RBMKRod.java` is rod-specific: `renderIDRods` with extra `_inner`/`_fuel` icons, meltdown in `breakBlock`, rod insertion.) `createNewTileEntity` returns the TE for `meta >= this.offset` and a `TileEntityProxyCombo` with the needed capabilities for `hasExtra(meta)`. `onBlockActivated` -> `openInv`. Override `getRenderType()` to return `renderIDPassive`. `RBMKPipedBase` already returns `renderIDControl`, and `renderIDRods` works only for `RBMKRod` subclasses because `RenderRBMKRod` casts to it. Without the override the block inherits `BlockDummyable.getRenderType() == -1` and is invisible. Textures in `textures/blocks/rbmk/`: `<name>_top/_side/_cover_top/_cover_side/_glass_top/_glass_side` (+ `_pipe_top/_pipe_side` for piped). `ModBlocks` next to `rbmk_rod` (~L2390; existing columns use the 2-arg `GameRegistry.registerBlock`, ~L3578-3597). `putRBMK()` id `tileentity_rbmk_*`. A TESR (ClientProxy `//RBMK` ~L466) is only needed for animated parts; passive columns have none. Exemplar `TileEntityRBMKOutgasser.java`.
- New RBMK fuel: `ItemRBMKPellet` + `ItemRBMKRod(pellet)` builder chain in `ModItems` (~L3423/~L3479). Build the rod after `rbmk_fuel_empty` (~L3478): the rod constructor calls `setContainerItem(ModItems.rbmk_fuel_empty)`, and grid disassembly (`RBMKFuelCraftingHandler`) relies on that to hand back the empty rod. `ItemRBMKRod(pellet)` adds the rod to `ItemRBMKRod.craftableRods`, which feeds the fuel-pool recipe and NEI disassembly. Register both items (the Californium pellets `rbmk_pellet_lecf/mecf/hecf`, ModItems.java:3459-3461, are constructed but never registered and have no rods). The billet recipe is `RodRecipes.addRBMKRod(billet, rod)` (`DictFrame` or `Item` overload, crafting/RodRecipes.java:258-263); add the call to the list at L91-126 or make it from fork code. Texture `items/<unloc>.png`, lang `item.<unloc>.name`. Hazards in `HazardRegistry.registerItems()` through the private helpers `registerRBMKPellet(pellet, base, dep[, linear[, blinding, digamma]])` and `registerRBMKRod(rod, base, dep[, blinding | linear])` (rods also get `HOT`); without them the fuel carries no radiation/heat hazard and shows no hazard tooltip.
- New dial: an `RBMKKeys` constant whose default is boxed the way the getter and `GameRuleHelper` cast it (`1.0`, not `1`, for a double dial; otherwise `refresh()` and client reads throw ClassCastException); a line in `refresh()` (without it the first server read throws `NullPointerException("Cannot find gamerule ... after creation")`, RBMKDials.java:142-144); a typed getter. If stream code reads the dial, add a package-private static to `RBMKNeutronHandler` and assign it in the per-world loop of `NeutronHandler.onServerTick` (L34-42).
- New turret: extend `TileEntityTurretBaseNT`/`BaseArtillery`; `static List<Integer> configs` from `XFactory*.<bullet>.id`; `getAmmoList()`; tuning getters (`getDecetorRange` etc, typos are API); `updateFiringTick()` with `getFirstConfigLoaded()`, `cachedCasingConfig = conf.casing`, `spawnBullet`, `conusmeAmmo`; block extends `TurretBaseNT`; `putTurrets()`; TESR (~L257). Exemplar `TileEntityTurretChekhov.java`.
- Fusion consumer: `implements IFusionPowerReceiver` (`receivesFusionPower()` false for neutron-only). Each server tick, copy the buffer to its `*Sync` field and zero it. If `plasmaNode == null || plasmaNode.expired`, set `d = getOrientation(meta - 10).getOpposite()` and look up `UniNodespace.getNode(world, x + d.offsetX*n, y + 2, z + d.offsetZ*n, PlasmaNetworkProvider.THE_PROVIDER)`, where n is the distance to the consumer's front block (Boiler 4, MHDT 6, Breeder/Collector 2; `TileEntityFusionPlasmaForge` also uses 5, but along `getRotation(UP)` for a receiver node and the opposite side for a provider node, TileEntityFusionPlasmaForge.java:152-157/232-243). If no node exists, create `new GenNode(provider, pos).setConnections(new DirPos(x + d.offsetX*(n+1), y + 2, z + d.offsetZ*(n+1), d))` and call `UniNodespace.createNode`. Call `plasmaNode.net.addReceiver(this)` when `hasValidNet()`. `destroyNode` goes in `invalidate()` (server only). `receiveFusionPower` runs inside the torus's tick, so do the work there or buffer it. Then `putFusion()` and a TESR (~L485). Exemplar `TileEntityFusionBoiler.java`.
- Albion component: extend `TileEntityCooledBase(slots)` + `IParticleUser` (`canParticleEnter` checks `new BlockPos(this).offset(beamlineDir, -entry)` and direction; `onEnter` may `particle.crash(PAState.X)`; `getExitPos`); block like `blocks/machine/albion/BlockPAQuadrupole`; `TileMappings` (~L207-213); TESR (~L282). Exemplar `TileEntityPAQuadrupole.java`.
- Launchable missile: `ItemMissile(form, tier[, fuel])`. `fuel` is final and defaults to `form.defaultFuel`; `fuelCap` defaults to `fuel.defaultCap` and can be changed with `setFuelCap`; `notLaunchable()` opts out. Register the item as usual. The entity extends `EntityMissileBaseNT` with a public constructor `(World, float, float, float, int, int)`, is registered with `addEntity` in `EntityMappings` (e.g. L84), and gets a renderer in `ClientProxy` (e.g. L737-742). Then add `missiles.put(new ComparableStack(item), Entity.class)` in `TileEntityLaunchPadBase.registerLaunchables()` (called at MainRegistry.java:337).
- Custom nuke ingredient: `entries.put(new ComparableStack(item), new CustomNukeEntry(type, value[, MULT]))` in `registerBombItems()`; caps in `blocks/bomb/NukeCustom.explodeCustom`.
- RTTY mini panel: `TileEntityLoadedBase` + `IGUIProvider` (null container, `GuiScreen`) + `IControlReceiver` + OC; inner `XUnit[]` with per-index NBT/ByteBuf; `RTTYSystem.listen`/`broadcast`; block extends `RBMKMiniPanelBase`. Register the TE with `put(..., "tileentity_rbmk_*")` in `TileMappings.putRBMK()` and the block with `register(x)` in `ModBlocks` (~L3598-3606; `register` gives `ItemBlockBase`, which keeps the panel's `ITooltipProvider` tooltip). Bind the TESR under ClientProxy `//RBMK` (~L472-478). Mark `provideGUI` `@SideOnly(Side.CLIENT)`; the exemplar omits it (`TileEntityRBMKGauge.java:184`). Exemplar `TileEntityRBMKGauge.java`.
- Assembly nuke: plain `TileEntity` + `ISidedInventory` + `IGUIProvider` with `isReady()`/`clearSlots()`; block `BlockContainer implements IBomb` (copy `blocks/bomb/NukeBoy.java`); `EntityNukeExplosionMK5.statFac` + `EntityNukeTorex`; `putBombs()`; TESR (~L241).

### Gotchas

- Flux that `spreadFlux` emits in tick N is delivered (`receiveFlux`) at ServerTickEvent START of tick N+1 and burned in that tick's `updateEntity`, a one-tick lag from emission to burn. `lastFluxQuantity` is the displayed value. `NeutronNodeWorld.removeEmptyWorlds` drops a `StreamWorld` (and its node cache) when it has no streams, i.e. when no reactor in that dimension emitted a stream the previous tick. Stream iterators share a mutable `BlockPos`: `NeutronStream.getBlocks` keeps its counter `i` and `posInstance` in stream instance fields (NeutronStream.java:50-73), so two iterators over one stream are not independent. `RBMKNeutronHandler` statics (`columnHeight`, `fluxRange` and the three efficiencies) are package-private. `NeutronHandler` reassigns them for each world inside its loop, just before that world's streams and `cleanNodes` run (NeutronHandler.java:34-47). They are valid only inside that loop iteration, so no other code should read them. The control-rod tail check in `runStreamInteraction` tests the origin node (dead branch, issue #1933). Each non-column position a stream crosses deposits radiation at the ORIGIN column when it is open or only partly blocked (`irradiateFromFlux(pos, hits)` with `pos` = origin, RBMKNeutronHandler.java:285/289, B-070). A fully blocked position (hits == columnHeight) ends the stream without irradiating anything. The reflector branch casts the origin to `TileEntityRBMKRod` (L355); today only `TileEntityRBMKRod`/`TileEntityRBMKRodReaSim` create RBMK streams.
- `RBMKDials` getters on the client log an error and return the default.
- The dial cache is keyed by `World` object. Only the overworld is created at server start (MainRegistry.java:737), and `/gamerule` refreshes only the sender's world (ModEventHandler.java:1595). In every other dimension, including NTM: Space bodies, the first dial read finds no cache entry and "self-heals" with `setOrCreateGameRule(key, default)` (RBMKDials.java:146). That call overwrites an existing value. Secondary dimensions share the overworld's `GameRules` through `DerivedWorldInfo`, so that dial's saved value reverts to its default. Other worlds' caches keep the old value until they are refreshed or the server restarts. Worlds are never removed from the cache (`ModEventHandler.onUnload`, L835-836, clears only `NeutronNodeWorld`), so an unloaded dimension leaks, and when it loads again as a new World object it repeats the reset. Because `createDials` fills the cache before writing defaults (RBMKDials.java:64-69), a new world caches `dialEnablePermaScrap` (default true) as false (`getGameRuleBooleanValue` of a missing rule, L97), so RBMK and ZIRNOX debris despawns (`EntityRBMKDebris.java:109`, `EntityZirnoxDebris.java:127`) until the next restart or `/gamerule`; numeric dials fall back to their defaults there. With `dialSaveDials` false the cache keeps the pre-reset values until the next restart or `/gamerule` while the saved rules are back at their defaults.
- `TileEntityRBMKControlAuto`: NBT without a `function` key sets `function = null` (L91-94; the field defaults to `LINEAR`, L23). `serialize` then skips the int that `deserialize` always reads (L117/L127), so every client read underflows (`BufPacket` catches and logs it, BufPacket.java:58-63). `getSettings` throws an NPE (L177), and so does `updateEntity`'s `switch(this.function)` (L57) on the server whenever the heat is between the bounds; with Forge's default `removeErroringTileEntities = false` (ForgeModContainer.java:63) that crashes the server.
- Fusion torus zeroes `klystronEnergy` after use and klystrons write into it directly: one-tick ordering lag by design. Forgetting `destroyNode` leaves zombie net members. The torus counts at most one receiver per plasma net when it picks `getOuputIntensity` (`break`, TileEntityFusionTorus.java:163), but the payout loop (L203-213) pays every `IFusionPowerReceiver` on each net the full `plasmaEnergy * outputIntensity`, so receivers sharing one port net do not split it.
- PA: every beamline block must be a `BlockDummyable` whose core is `IParticleUser` or the run derails. A coil below `quadMin` makes the quadrupole draw 10x. In a dipole, momentum below `diMin` and `distanceTraveled` below `diDistMin` (minimum side length) each multiply the draw by 10 (100x together). An inline dipole pass resets the multiplier to 1 and skips the `diMax` check. Otherwise, momentum above `quadMax`/`diMax` crashes with `CRASH_OVERSPEED`.
- Pads: tank types re-type from the loaded missile each tick (`setFuel`). `FluidTank.setTankType` empties a tank whenever its type changes, so loading a missile with a different fuel pair voids each mismatched tank. Solid-fuel missiles leave the tanks unchanged. Rocket pad rebuilds tanks and places/removes tower blocks; redstone edge needs the block's `onNeighborBlockChange` to call `updateRedstonePower`.
- Turrets: rotations in radians; `getHorizontalOffset` hard-codes 2x2 offsets; ammo slots accept anything (`isItemValidForSlot` true); damaged variants ignore the whitelist; `TurretArty.methods()` omits `getPos`, `TurretHIMARS` adds `addCoords` without listing it.
- `TileEntityRBMKHeater` uses `modid = "opencomputers"` (L32), which never matches, so FML strips that `SimpleComponent` declaration. This is harmless: OC's coremod has already injected the Environment implementation and `CompatHandler.OCComponent` still supplies `SimpleComponent` (B-326, area 18 Gotchas). Changing the modid to `"OpenComputers"` is annotation hygiene (Phase 4).
- Smells: `TileEntityTurretFritz.java:160` TODO duplicated connections; `TileEntityCompactLauncher`/`LaunchTable.sendCommandEntity` pass `posX` for both x and z; `TileEntityLaunchPadRocket.getDestination` inverted `hasDrive()`; `TileEntityLaunchPadLarge` checks `erector == 1F` twice; `TileEntityNukeCustom.destruct()` passes x as z; `TileEntityNukeBoy.isReady` uses `slots[01]` (octal); `TileEntityRBMKConsole.getName()` returns null; `EntityAntimatter.java` in `tileentity/bomb` is a 0-byte file; `TileEntityRBMKSlottedBase` and `getOutputPos` (Boiler:140, Cooler:83, Heater:94, Outgasser:63) are admitted copy-paste; `GameRuleHelper.parseDouble`/`parseInt` pass the empty value instead of the key to `addGameRule` (util/GameRuleHelper.java:29-30, 44-45), so the first missing numeric dial creates a gamerule named `""`.

## 7. Energy/fluid networks (UNINOS) and packet threading

### Purpose

UNINOS (`com/hbm/uninos`) is the graph engine behind every wire-like system: HE cables, fluid ducts (one graph per `FluidType`), pneumatic tubes, and single-purpose nets (klystron, plasma, foundry channel, rebar). Tiles push a `GenNode` into a per-World map keyed `Pair(BlockPos, INetworkProvider)`; `UniNodespace.updateNodespace()` (every `ServerTickEvent` START from `ModEventHandler.onServerTick`, BEFORE tile ticks) stitches nodes into `NodeNet`s and ticks `update()`. Machines subscribe as receivers/providers to an adjacent conductor's net (area 2). `PacketThreading` (`com/hbm/handler/threading`) moves the netty send of every `ThreadedPacket` handed to it onto one worker thread (`NTM-Packet-Thread-*`) and rejoins at tick END. Three kinds of sends go through it: TE-sync `BufPacket`s from `networkPackNT` and `ExtPropPacket` are precompiled on the main thread; the `AuxParticlePacketNT` particle sends (132 call sites) are serialized on the worker. A message that is not a `ThreadedPacket` is logged and dropped.

### Key files

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `com/hbm/uninos/UniNodespace.java` | `worlds` (World -> `UniNodeWorld`, never cleared on unload except `/ntmreapnetworks`), `activeNodeNets`, `getNode/createNode/destroyNode`, `updateNodespace()`, `checkNodeConnection`/`checkConnection`/`connectToNode`, 5-minute reaper. `UniNodeWorld.popNode` calls `node.net.destroy()`. |
| `uninos/GenNode.java`, `NodeNet.java`, `INetworkProvider.java` | Node (`positions[]`, `connections[]`, `net` null first tick, `expired`, `recentlyChanged`); abstract net (`links`, `receiverEntries`/`providerEntries` timestamp maps, `joinNetworks`, `isBadLink`; ctor self-registers in `activeNodeNets`); provider factory (must return a fresh net each call). |
| `uninos/networkproviders/PowerNetProvider.java`, `FluidNetProvider.java`, `PneumaticNetwork.java` + `Provider`, `KlystronNetwork.java`, `PlasmaNetwork.java`, `FoundryNetwork.java`, `RebarNetwork.java` | Power singleton (`Nodespace.THE_POWER_PROVIDER`), per-FluidType provider, item-tube net (raw `NodeNet`, own `receivers` map with 1000 ms timeout, `send()` every 5 ticks per compressor, range by pressure 10/25/100/250/1000, 64 mass units per transfer, NTL `accessors`/`storages`), empty-update nets. |
| `tileentity/network/TileEntityCableBaseNT.java`, `TileEntityCableSwitch.java`, `TileEntityPylonBase.java`, `TileEntitySubstation.java`, `TileEntityPipeBaseNT.java`, `TileEntityPipelineBase.java`, `TileEntityFluidValve.java`, `TileEntityFluidCounterValve.java`, `TileEntityPipeExhaust.java`, `TileEntityConverterHeRf.java`, `TileEntityConverterRfHe.java` | Conductor/duct tiles, plus the HE/RF bridge endpoints, which hold no node: `TileEntityConverterHeRf` is an `IEnergyReceiverMK2` that calls `trySubscribe` and outputs RF, and `TileEntityConverterRfHe` is an `IEnergyProviderMK2` that takes RF and calls `tryProvide`. Pylons use `DirPos(..., UNKNOWN)` at their own position plus one toward each wired pylon; `PipeBaseNT.onChunkUnload` only sets `isLoaded = false` (nodes survive unload); exhaust holds 3 FluidNodes at one position. |
| `tileentity/network/pneumatic/TileEntityPneumoTube.java`, `TileEntityPneumaticMachineBase.java`, `TileEntityPneumoStorageImporter.java`, `TileEntityPneumoStorageExporter.java`, `TileEntityPneumaticStorageBase.java`, `TileEntityPneumoStorageAccess.java` | Tube (compressor/endpoint roles, filters); access-point base `TileEntityPneumaticMachineBase` (only subclasses: importer and exporter) and the terminal `TileEntityPneumoStorageAccess` (a `TileEntityLoadedBase` copy of the base's node/cache code; `ContainerPneumoStorageAccess` drives its cache), both destroy their node on chunk unload; storage base (detaches monitors on unload but keeps its node). |
| `tileentity/network/RTTYSystem.java`, `TileEntityRadioTorchBase.java`, `TileEntityRadioTorchSender.java`, `TileEntityRadioTorchReceiver.java` | Double-buffered radio channel bus keyed (World, channel); `broadcast` next tick visible, and numeric values sent to one channel in the same tick are summed (see How-to); channels are never evicted (compare `chan.timeStamp`, `chan != null` is not "signal present"); test channel `2012-08-06` injected every tick. |
| `tileentity/network/RequestNetwork.java`, `TileEntityRequestNetwork.java`, `TileEntityDroneDock.java`, `TileEntityDroneWaypoint.java` | Drone logistics graph (leases 2000 ms; the intended 20-tick throttle is dead code so the purge runs every tick; `hasPath` uncapped over known nodes). Not nodespace-based. |
| `tileentity/machine/TileEntityMachineRadarNT.java` | Static `updateSystem()` gathers matching entities once per server tick. |
| `handler/threading/PacketThreading.java`, `packet/threading/ThreadedPacket.java`, `PrecompiledPacket.java` | Single-worker pool (`NTM-Packet-Thread-*`), `ReentrantLock lock`, `createAllAroundThreadedPacket`/`createSendToThreadedPacket`, `waitUntilThreadFinished` (50 ms per future; on a timeout it logs and clears the queue; it latches `hasTriggered` once `clearCnt > 5`, i.e. on the 6th non-empty clear since the last reset, and from then on every send runs inline on the main thread until `/ntmpackets resetState`. Only `resetState`, a clear that finds the queue already empty (a timeout on the last outstanding task) and `init()` with threading disabled and an empty queue reset `clearCnt`; a clean tick never calls `clearThreadPoolTasks`, so six overflows at any spacing latch it. A task that throws, e.g. in the post-send recompile (B-100), surfaces as an `ExecutionException` that is swallowed (`// impossible`, L155-156) and ends the wait loop; the `finally` block then drops and counts whatever is still queued. `packetThreadingErrorBypass` skips the wait entirely and drops whatever is queued). `preparePacket` compiles on the main thread only for `PrecompiledPacket`, and logs and drops any message that is not a `ThreadedPacket` (L74-77). `init()` only called from `/ntmpackets` (its validation is inverted: `max > core` resets both to 1). |
| `commands/CommandPacketInfo.java`, `CommandReapNetworks.java` | `/ntmpackets` with subcommands `info`, `resetState`, `toggleThreadingStatus`, `forceLock`, `forceUnlock`. Issued on the server thread (player, console, command block), `forceLock` only starves the worker: the lock is reentrant, and after six non-empty queue clears sends fall back to inline. Issued over RCON, it runs on the RCON client thread, because `MinecraftServer.handleRConCommand` calls `executeCommand` directly; that thread keeps the lock, and the server thread hangs at its next lock-taking send in `NetworkHandler` until `forceUnlock` arrives on the same RCON connection, and for ever if that connection closes. `forceUnlock` from a thread that does not hold the lock throws `IllegalMonitorStateException`. `/ntmreapnetworks` clears `activeNodeNets` and `worlds` (L29-36: it marks every link expired but never calls `invalidate()`/`destroy()` on the nets, so orphaned nets keep `valid = true`; TEs recover because they test `node.expired`). |
| `blocks/network/CableDiode.java`, `tileentity/machine/storage/TileEntityBatteryBase.java`, `TileEntityBatteryREDD.java`, `blocks/generic/BlockRebar.java`, `blocks/machine/FoundryChannel.java`, `tileentity/machine/fusion/TileEntityFusionKlystron.java` | Diode (`sendPowerDiode`, recursion brake, 10 pulses/tick), battery-as-conductor (node at `getPortPos()`, lookup/destroy at own xyz: REDD's ports exclude the core, so it leaks duplicate nodes), custom `transferFluid` walking `net.links`, foundry node with `NTMMaterial`, offset klystron node. |

### Patterns

- Connection rule (`checkConnection`): A connects to B iff A has a `DirPos c` at one of B's positions and B has a `DirPos r` with `r.pos - r.dir == c.pos` and `r.dir == c.dir.getOpposite()`; `skipSideCheck` is always false. Wired links use UNKNOWN on both ends (`UNKNOWN.getOpposite() == UNKNOWN`), the reverse being B's own-position UNKNOWN DirPos.
- Net formation: nodes with `!hasValidNet() || recentlyChanged` are re-checked each tick; the larger net absorbs the smaller; set `node.recentlyChanged = true` when connections change at runtime (`TileEntityPylonBase.addConnection`).
- Node keys use the provider INSTANCE, so several providers may coexist at one position; fluid nets are per `FluidType` instance (`/ntmreload` preserves instances of same-named custom fluids via `Fluids.fluidMigration`; only removed/renamed custom fluids orphan nodes).
- Tick orchestration: START: `RTTYSystem.updateBroadcastQueue`, `RequestNetwork.updateEntries`, `TileEntityMachineRadarNT.updateSystem`, `UniNodespace.updateNodespace`; END: `PacketThreading.waitUntilThreadFinished`, `NetworkHandler.flush`. A node created in `updateEntity` gets a net next tick.
- Threaded sends: a `PrecompiledPacket` handed to `PacketThreading` (`BufPacket` from `networkPackNT`, `ExtPropPacket` from `EntityEffectHandler`) is serialized on the main thread before queueing. A plain `ThreadedPacket` (`AuxParticlePacketNT`) is serialized inside `NetworkHandler`'s codec `encode` on the worker thread, so its data must be immutable after construction. After the send, the task calls `getCompiledBuffer().release()`. The send has drained the buffer, so this call recompiles it: `toBytes()` runs a second time on the worker for every queued packet (for `BufPacket` that is the TE's `serialize()`, run against live state) and the result is thrown away (B-100). An exception there surfaces as a swallowed `ExecutionException` in `waitUntilThreadFinished`, which ends that tick's join and drops the rest of the queue. Never reuse a `ThreadedPacket` instance on the threaded path. `EntityBufPacket` (`EntityRideableRocket.java:458`) and the `BufPacket`s in `BlockVolcanoV2.java:91` / `BlockAtmosphereEditor.java:154` bypass `PacketThreading`; they are serialized in `encode` on the main thread.

### How-to

- Consumer/provider/duct/cable/new network kind: see area 2. Register new TEs in `TileMappings.writeMappings()` (e.g. L497 `put(TileEntityCableBaseNT.class, "tileentity_cable", "tileentity_wirecoated")`).
- Pneumatic access point: extend `TileEntityPneumaticMachineBase(slotCount)` and call `super.updateEntity()` first. Server side, the base gets or creates the `PneumaticNode`, recreates `cache` when it has expired, and, once the node has a valid net, registers the cache with it via `addStackCache` (`TileEntityPneumaticMachineBase.java:22-46`). Then, server side, guard `if(cache != null && !cache.hasExpired)` and use `cache.addItemsAndReturnQuantity` / `consumeItemsAndReturnQuantity`. The base never calls `networkPackNT`, so call it yourself if the client needs state. Exemplars: `TileEntityPneumoStorageImporter.java` (insert) and `TileEntityPneumoStorageExporter.java` (extract, `networkPackNT(15)`). `TileEntityPneumoStorageAccess.java` does not extend the base: it is a `TileEntityLoadedBase` copy of the same node/cache code, and `ContainerPneumoStorageAccess` drives its cache. Register the TE next to the other pneumatic entries in `TileMappings.putNetwork()` (L532-538).
- Tile sync packet: override `serialize`/`deserialize`, calling `super` first on both sides with the same field order (`TileEntityLoadedBase` syncs `muffled`/`tilted` there); server side, call `networkPackNT(range)`. Exemplar: `blocks/network/CableDiode.java` (`TileEntityDiode`, serialize/deserialize L133-145, `networkPackNT(15)` L162). `TileEntityFluidCounterValve.java` skips `super` on both sides, so do not use it as a model. Custom packets: append them to `PacketDispatcher.registerPackets()`. Anything passed to `PacketThreading.create*ThreadedPacket` must extend `ThreadedPacket` (other classes are logged and dropped, `PacketThreading.java:74-77`), and must extend `PrecompiledPacket` if `toBytes` reads mutable server state. Even then, `toBytes` runs a second, discarded time on the worker after the send (B-100), so it must not throw or have side effects. Packets sent directly through `PacketDispatcher.wrapper` are serialized on the calling thread and need neither.
- RTTY: the sender calls `RTTYSystem.broadcast(worldObj, channel, value)`. Within one tick, a numeric value sent to a channel that already holds a numeric value is added to it: both are parsed as `long` and the sum is stored as a String (`RTTYSystem.java:29-38`). Non-numeric values, and numbers that fail `Long.parseLong` (e.g. `1.5`), overwrite. For numbers the javadoc's "only the last signal pushed will be used" is wrong: two senders on one channel in the same tick deliver the sum. The value becomes visible to `listen` at the next tick's START (`updateBroadcastQueue`, which stamps `getTotalWorldTime()`). Receiver: `RTTYChannel chan = RTTYSystem.listen(worldObj, channel)`; `null` means the channel has never been used, otherwise compare `chan.timeStamp` with the last stamp you processed (`TileEntityRadioTorchReceiver.java:22`). Exemplars: `TileEntityRadioTorchSender.java` / `TileEntityRadioTorchReceiver.java`.

### Gotchas

- `TileAccessCache` caches null lookups 20 ticks (new cable seen after up to 1 s); non-null entries self-expire on invalidation.
- Subscription timeouts are wall-clock: a paused/lagging server drops every subscriber; they self-heal on the next subscribe.
- `PowerNetMK2.update`/`FluidNetMK2.update` return early when either side is empty, so stale entries linger on one-sided nets.
- `TileEntityPylonBase.addConnection` NPEs when the node does not exist yet (same tick as placement).
- A `GenNode` whose `connections` were never set (`GenNode.java:10`; only `setConnections`/`setStandardConnections` set them) NPEs `UniNodespace.checkNodeConnection` on the for-each at `UniNodespace.java:99`, inside the server tick.
- `updateNodespace` connects nodes only for `MinecraftServer.getServer().worldServers` (`UniNodespace.java:61`), but `updateNetworks` ticks every net in `activeNodeNets` (L82-83), so nets of an unloaded dimension's `World` keep ticking against stale members (B-107).
- After `/ntmreapnetworks`, `UniNodespace.destroyNode(World, GenNode)` (L52-56, no null check on `worlds.get(world)`; used by the klystron and plasma-node machines) NPEs until that world has a node map again (B-094).
- Unloading the chunk of one pneumatic importer, exporter or access terminal destroys its node (`TileEntityPneumaticMachineBase.java:60-68`, `TileEntityPneumoStorageAccess.java:60-69`); `popNode` calls `net.destroy()`, and `PneumaticNetwork.destroy` (L50-56) clears every receiver, dissolves every `StackCache` and drops every storage, so the whole tube network is torn down and re-forms next tick.
- Owner's pack: bobfluidtranslator 2.1.12 (a coremod bridging NTM fluids to Forge) reads `NodeNet.receiverEntries`/`providerEntries` (`NodeNet.java:21-22`) by name with the descriptor `Ljava/util/HashMap;` (`UniversalFluidBridge.relayToReceivers`/`relayFromProviders`). Renaming or retyping them (hbm/master `0352a3e8` retypes both to `Set`) makes every Forge fill/drain/getTankInfo on an HBM fluid or exhaust duct throw `NoSuchFieldError` inside the bridge, which catches it, logs `UniversalFluidBridge#<op> failed for <class>` with a stack trace and does nothing. Keep both names and the `HashMap` type.
- `NetworkHandler.flush()` at tick END is effectively a no-op for server-to-client traffic: on the server, `FMLOutboundHandler.write` hands each packet to `NetworkDispatcher.sendProxy` -> `NetworkManager.scheduleOutboundPacket`, which `writeAndFlush`es it at once or hands it to the netty event loop (javap on forgeBin). The class comment at `NetworkHandler.java:31` that claims delayed flushing is wrong; do not assume sends are batched until tick END.
- Smells: `NodeNet.joinNetworks` raw-generics cast ("this is bullshit"); `PowerNode` rant about join failures (root cause unknown); `TileEntityPipelineBase` "copy pasted crap class"; `RequestNetwork` "this entire system sucks" with an 8-point migration plan; `TileAccessCache.publicCumRag`; `TileEntityPipeBaseNT` redeclares `public boolean isLoaded` (L121), shadowing `TileEntityLoadedBase.isLoaded` (its `onChunkUnload` calls super, so both copies stay in step, but a refactor of the base field must update both); the `PacketThreading` latch message (L204) tells admins to run `/ntmpacket resetState`, but the command is `/ntmpackets` (`CommandPacketInfo.java:21`); no TODO/@Spaghetti markers inside uninos/threading/api.

## 8. Items

### Purpose

`com/hbm/items/ModItems.java` (7192 lines; 2002 item fields at L109-2338: 1918 `public static Item` plus 84 typed `ItemEnumMulti`/`ItemRBMKRod`/`ItemRBMKPellet`) instantiates items in `initializeItem()` (L2340) / `initializeItem2()` (L4373: `ModItemsArmor.init()`, ability tools, `GunFactory.init()`, buckets) and registers them in `registerItem()` (L4906). Behaviour is dispatched from the event handlers via marker interfaces (`ArmorFSB`, `ItemArmorMod`, `IItemHUD`, `IKeybindReceiver`, `IEquipReceiver`, `IGUIProvider`, `IItemControlReceiver`, `IAnimatedItem`).

### Key files

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `items/ModItems.java`, `ModItemsArmor.java` | Registry; armor sets instantiated in `ModItemsArmor.init()` (static import of `ModItems.*`), registered back in `ModItems.registerItem()`. `excludeNEI` set; `addRemap(String, Item, meta or Enum)` registers an `ItemRemap` (no callers). |
| `items/ItemEnumMulti.java`, `ItemEnums.java`, `ItemCustomLore.java`, `ItemGenericPart.java`, `ItemRemap.java`, `BrokenItem.java`, `ItemInventory.java`, `ItemVOTVdrive.java` | Enum-meta base (`setUnlocalizedName` also sets texture; icons `<unloc>.<enum_lower>`; `stackFromEnum`), shared enums, lang-driven `.desc` tooltips (`$` split, `.desc.P11` variant), enum with own textures, rename placeholder (unused, see How-to), broken-item wrapper, NBT-backed inventory (ejects > 6000 bytes compressed), Space destination drive. |
