### Patterns

- Three-phase registration: field, instantiate (`new X().setUnlocalizedName("x").setCreativeTab(MainRegistry.partsTab).setTextureName(RefStrings.MODID + ":x")`), `GameRegistry.registerItem(x, x.getUnlocalizedName())`. The registry name is `hbm:item.x` (see naming families). Hidden items use `.setCreativeTab(null)`, which hides them from the creative menu only; NEI still lists them. To hide an item from the NEI panel, add `API.hideItem(new ItemStack(...))` in `main/NEIConfig.loadConfig()`. `ModItems.excludeNEI` only suppresses GenericRecipe entries containing the item in NEI's recipe/usage views, and only when the client config `NEI_HIDE_SECRETS` is on.
- `ModItems`/`ModItemsArmor` are currently identical to the last merged upstream version (JameH2 tip `64b64130`). The fork's creative-tab reversals (fuel plates, waste plates) live in `com/hbm/dbs/DBSItems.afterItemInit()`, called via `DBSFork.init()` from `MainRegistry.PreLoad` right after `ModItems.mainRegistry()`. This is not a rule: since 2026-09-25 the owner allows editing any file, so fork item changes may go inline in `ModItems`/`ModItemsArmor` or in `com/hbm/dbs/`. Leaving `ModItems` untouched only avoids merge conflicts if upstream merges continue.
- Load order for items added from fork code: `loadConfig` (MainRegistry:275, includes `ToolConfig`), the `Mats` init (L280), `ModBlocks.mainRegistry()` (L283) and `ModItems.mainRegistry()` (L284) run before the `DBSFork.init()` hook (L285); `CraftingManager.mainRegistry()` (L294), `HazardRegistry.registerItems()` (L296) and `OreDictManager` (L304-305) run after it. So such item constructors may reference `ModBlocks` fields and config flags, and crafting, hazard and ore-dict code can reference the new items. `ModItems.registerItem()` is private (L4906): items created outside it call `GameRegistry.registerItem` themselves.
- Not every field is assigned in `ModItems`: guns/ammo come from `items/weapon/sedna/factory/*`, syringes/IVs from `ItemSimpleConsumable.init()`, armor from `ModItemsArmor.init()` (there is no `ModItemsCrafting`; everything else is in `initializeItem()`/`initializeItem2()`).
- Naming families: by convention field = `setUnlocalizedName("<name>")` = texture `hbm:<name>` (exceptions exist, e.g. field `hat` / unlocalized "nossy_hat" (ModItemsArmor:33), `butter_sword` / texture `budder_sword` (ModItems:2344)). The registry name is `hbm:item.<name>`, because `getUnlocalizedName()` prepends `item.` and FML prefixes the mod id; that full string is what missing-mapping remaps and the recipe/armor/rad-resist JSON configs use. Choose the class by family: `Item` (plain), `ItemCustomLore` (lang `.desc` tooltip), `ItemEnumMulti(Enum.class, multiName, multiTexture)` (meta variants, icons `x.<enum_lower>`), `ItemGenericPart` (ItemEnumMulti of generic parts: pistons, LDE/HDE, polarized glass, with per-enum texture names), `ItemAutogen` (material-system shapes), `ItemSimpleConsumable`, `ArmorFSB*`/`ItemArmorMod`, `ItemToolAbility*`, `ItemGunBaseNT` (sedna), `ItemBlock*` for blocks. Tabs: `partsTab` parts/ingots/dusts; `controlTab` machine inputs, fuels, rods, upgrades; `templateTab` only blueprints, blueprint folder, fluid identifier, siren tracks, fluid ducts; `consumableTab` consumables and armor mods; `missileTab` missiles, satellites and sat chips; `weaponTab`/`nukeTab`; `machineTab`/`blockTab` for ItemBlocks. Some classes set the tab in their constructor (`ItemArmorMod` -> `consumableTab`, `ItemRBMKRod`/`ItemRBMKPellet` -> `controlTab`). Copy the tab of the nearest sibling item; `null` hides.
- Per-identity behaviour (`this == ModItems.x`) in `ItemDrop`, `ItemPill`, `ItemLemon`, `ArmorModel`, `ModArmor`, `ItemMachineUpgrade` tooltips.
- Armor: configure the helmet with fluent flags, then `new ArmorFSB(...).cloneStats((ArmorFSB) helmet)` for plate/legs/boots. `hides()` and `setFullSetForHide()` are per piece; hazard classes and the overlay are read only from the helmet slot, so set them on the helmet (B-112); the set bonus is read from the chestplate. Materials via `EnumHelper.addArmorMaterial("HBM_X", ...)` (two are both named `HBM_TRENCH`).
- Charge/fuel in NBT: `IBatteryItem` (`long charge`, missing = full), `IFillableItem` (`int fuel`).
- Self-registering static lists: `ItemRTGPellet.pelletList` (filled by the constructor; read by the RTG, DiFurnaceRTG and Radiolysis GUIs) and `ItemRBMKRod.craftableRods` (filled only by the `ItemRBMKRod(pellet)` constructor; consumed by `FuelPoolRecipes:46` and `RBMKRodDisassemblyHandler:26`). `FluidTank.noDualUnload` is filled by hand in ModItems (:2937, :2939, :4354-4356) and never read.
- Achievements: `new Achievement("achievement.<k>", "<k>", x, y, icon, parent).initIndependentStat().registerStat()` in `MainRegistry` L394+; must be added to the `AchievementPage` array at `MainRegistry:468`; icons via `DictFrame.fromOne(ModItems.achievement_icon, EnumAchievementType.X)`; crafting triggers in `AchievementHandler.register()`.

### How-to

- Rename/remove an item: the registry name is `hbm:item.<unloc>`, so renaming the unlocalized name orphans existing stacks. In `MainRegistry.handleMissingMappings` (~L800-1759), add `remapItems.put("hbm:item.<old>", ModItems.<new>)` for an ID remap, or `ignoreMappings.add("hbm:item.<old>")` to drop the stacks. Every missing `hbm:item.ammo_*` is ignored wholesale (L1742). For a rename that also changes meta, `ModItems.addRemap(oldUnloc, item, meta|Enum)` registers an `ItemRemap` placeholder under the old name. The placeholder shows the target's icon and converts itself only while in a player's inventory (onUpdate). It currently has no callers. Plain/enum/lore items: see the CLAUDE.md checklist; exemplars `special/ItemExpensive.java`, `ItemCustomLore.java`.
- FSB armor set: four fields (~L1836-2171); material via `EnumHelper.addArmorMaterial`; helmet with all flags in `ModItemsArmor.init()`, e.g. `x_helmet = new ArmorFSB(mat, 0, "hbm:textures/armor/x_1.png").setNoHelmet(false).setRadResist(20D).setSealed(true).setStep("hbm:step.x").setJump(..).setFall(..).setStepSize(1).setDashCount(1).setHasGeigerSound(true).setHasCustomGeiger(..).setHasHardLanding(..).enableVATS(..).enableThermalSight(..).addEffect(new PotionEffect(..)).setHazardClass(HazardClass.X, ..).hides(EnumPlayerPart.HEAD).setOverlay(path).setUnlocalizedName("x_helmet").setTextureName(RefStrings.MODID + ":x_helmet")`; then `x_plate = new ArmorFSB(mat, 1, "...x_1.png").cloneStats((ArmorFSB) x_helmet).setUnlocalizedName("x_plate").setTextureName(RefStrings.MODID + ":x_plate")` (legs use `_2.png`, slots 0-3 = helmet/chest/legs/boots). End each piece's chain with `setUnlocalizedName`/`setTextureName` AFTER `cloneStats` and every ArmorFSB setter: both return `Item`, and the ArmorFSB constructor presets the icon to `hbm:armor` (ArmorFSB:76), so a missing `setTextureName` silently shows the generic `armor.png` (see ModItemsArmor:43-51). `cloneStats` copies `effects` (shared list), `noHelmet`, `vats`, `thermal`, `geigerSound`, `customGeiger`, `hardLanding`, `dashCount`, `stepSize`, `step`/`jump`/`fall`, `canSeal` and re-runs `setRadResist`; it does NOT copy `setHazardClass`, `hides` or `setFullSetForHide`, nor `setOverlay`: set `hides`/`setFullSetForHide` per piece; hazard classes, like the overlay, are read only from the helmet slot, so set them on the helmet (B-112). The full-set bonus is read from the CHESTPLATE (`armorInventory[2]`): effects, step/jump/fall sounds, hardLanding, stepSize, dashCount, VATS, thermal and customGeiger. The subclass hooks `handleTick/handleAttack/handleHurt/handleJump/handleFall` are invoked on the chestplate item (ModEventHandler:996, 1067, 1084, 1139, 1158, 1358). Flags set on the helmet only take effect because `cloneStats` copies them to the plate. `setOverlay`/`handleOverlay` are helmet-only: Forge calls `renderHelmetOverlay` for armor slot 3 only, and ModEventHandlerClient:401-404 reads the helmet, so set the overlay on the helmet alone. Powered: `ArmorFSBPowered(mat, slot, texture, maxPower, chargeRate, consumption, drain)` (`IBatteryItem`, NBT `charge`); fueled: `ArmorFSBFueled(mat, slot, texture, fuelType, maxFuel, fillRate, consumption, drain)` (`IFillableItem`). Damage resistance is not a setter: `DamageResistanceHandler.initDefaults` / `config/hbmConfig/hbmArmor.json`. `initDefaults` runs only when `hbmArmor.json` is absent, and an existing `hbmRadResist.json` replaces every `setRadResist` value; delete both files on a test install to see a new set's stats. Register all four (~L6900-7040); icons `textures/items/`, layers `textures/armor/x_1.png`/`x_2.png` (the bismuth set passes `starmetal_2.png` to the plate and `starmetal_1.png` to the legs, ModItemsArmor:59-60; do not copy that). Construction must happen before `PostLoad` (in practice inside `ModItemsArmor.init()`, called from `ModItems` in PreLoad) because `ArmorUtil.register()` / `HazmatRegistry.registerHazmats()` (`MainRegistry` L600-601, PostLoad) fill the hazard-class and rad-resistance tables from the `ArmorUtil.external`/`HazmatRegistry.external` queues that `setHazardClass`/`setRadResist` append to (ArmorFSB:150, :160).
- Armor mod: `extends ItemArmorMod` (ctor `(slotConst, helmet, chest, legs, boots)`; sets maxStackSize 1 and consumableTab). Override `modUpdate` (every tick while worn), `modDamage` (LivingHurtEvent), `getModifiers`, `modRender` and `addDesc`. `getModifiers` returns attribute modifiers keyed `ArmorModHandler.UUIDs[armorType]`. They are applied only when the worn stack changes (item, damage or NBT) and removed via `getModifiers(prevStack)` (ModEventHandler:772-811), so keep it a pure function of the armor stack. Mods on the same piece share that UUID, so two of them must not modify the same attribute; `fixedUUIDs` is used by armor classes (`ArmorDesh`, `ArmorDiesel`, `ArmorLiquidator`), not by mods. Exemplar `ItemModServos.java`. `ItemModCladding` has no gameplay hook; it works only through a hard-coded check in `HazmatRegistry.getCladding`, which first honours a legacy float NBT `hfr_cladding` on the armor (HazmatRegistry:185-186). Note `ModEventHandlerClient.java:791` iterates `i < 8` while `MOD_SLOTS == 9` (the battery mod's `addDesc` never shows).
- Ability tool: instantiate in `initializeItem2()`: `new ItemToolAbility(dmg, movement, MainRegistry.tMatX, EnumToolType.PICKAXE).addAbility(IToolAreaAbility.HAMMER, 1)...`; levels 0-based (`AvailableAbilities` clamps with a warning; disallowed abilities are dropped). New tool ability: an anonymous constant in `IToolAreaAbility`/`IToolHarvestAbility` with `getName()` returning `tool.ability.x`, `levels()`, `sortOrder()` returning `SORT_ORDER_BASE + n` (area 0, harvest 100), and `isAllowed()` returning a new `ToolConfig` flag. The `IBaseAbility` default sort order is `hashCode()`, which leaves the preset order unstable. Append the constant to that interface's `abilities[]` (used by `getByName` when `ToolPreset` reads NBT). Add an `AbilityInfo(ability, u, v)` to `GUIScreenToolAbility.abilitiesArea`/`abilitiesHarvest`, or the preset GUI cannot select it. The harvest icon row at v=107 of `gui_tool_ability.png` is already full up to u=224, so a new harvest icon needs another spot in the atlas; the GUI widens itself. Give an area ability a HUD icon UV in `ItemToolAbility.abilityGui` (no entry means no crosshair icon), and add lang `tool.ability.x`. New weapon ability: a constant in `IWeaponAbility` (`SORT_ORDER_BASE` 200, lang `weapon.ability.x`), appended to its `abilities[]` for consistency (its `getByName` is currently unused). Weapon abilities have no `ToolConfig` flag and no GUI entry.
- RTG pellet / RBMK rod / machine upgrade: `ItemRTGPellet(heat).setDecays(...)` (~L3019), `ItemRBMKRod(pellet)` builder (~L3479), `ItemMachineUpgrade(UpgradeType, tier)` (~L4204). Hazards go into `HazardRegistry.registerItems()` (PreLoad, MainRegistry:296) through its private helpers: `registerRTGPellet(pellet, base, target[, hot[, blinding]])`, `registerRBMKPellet(pellet, base, dep[, linear[, blinding, digamma]])`, `registerRBMKRod(rod, base, dep[, blinding|linear])`, `registerPWRFuel(EnumPWRFuel, baseRad)`, `registerOtherFuel(fuel[, meta], base, target, blinding)`, and `registerOtherWaste`/`registerRadSourceWaste` (area 13). Code outside HazardRegistry uses `HazardSystem.register(item|stack, HazardData)`. RBMK rod crafting (empty rod + 8 billets): `crafting/RodRecipes.addRBMKRod(...)`.
- Held-item HUD/keybind/GUI: implement `IItemHUD.renderHUD` (called for every overlay ElementType; filter by type), `IKeybindReceiver` (existing `EnumKeybind`s only; `canHandleKeybind` is asked on each side; `handleKeybind` runs on the server, `handleKeybindClient` on the client), `IItemControlReceiver` (the client sends `NBTItemControlPacket`), and `IGUIProvider` + `player.openGui(MainRegistry.instance, 0, world, 0, 0, 0)`. Call openGui on the server (`!world.isRemote`) when `provideContainer` returns a Container (exemplar `tool/ItemLeadBox.java`). Call it on the client for container-less screens (exemplar `tool/ItemToolAbility.java`). No handler wiring is needed, but `GUIHandler` checks the TE and block at (x,y,z) before the held item.
- Simple consumable: follow `ItemSimpleConsumable.init()` (`setUseActionServer`, helpers `giveSoundAndDecrement`, `addPotionEffect`).

### Gotchas

- Instantiated but never registered (6): `med_schizophrenia` (ModItems:4089), `pch` (:4771), `ammo_misc` (:4050), `rbmk_pellet_lecf/mecf/hecf` (:3459-3461). (`rbmk_fuel_bk247` IS registered, at :6009; the call is written `registerItem( rbmk_fuel_bk247, ...)` with a leading space.) Declared but never assigned (null) (6): `remote` (its registration at :7067 is commented out), `flask_empty`, `ingot_pet`, `ingot_tetraneutronium`, `nugget_tetraneutronium`, `powder_tetraneutronium`. `telepad`, `coin_siege`, `source`, `satellite`, `gadget_explosive`, `man_explosive`, `turret_control` and `turret_biometry` are commented-out declarations (`//public static Item ...`), not fields; all except `satellite` are in `MainRegistry.handleMissingMappings` ignoreMappings.
- `ItemEnumMulti`/`ItemCustomLore.setUnlocalizedName` already set the texture name; a differing trailing `setTextureName` overrides it.
- `ItemEnumMulti.stackFromEnum` returns null when the enum constant has a body, because it compares `num.getClass() != theEnum` (ItemEnumMulti:85); avoid constant-specific bodies in item enums.
- `ItemLemon.java:40` spells the key `item.med_ipecac.desс` with a Cyrillic `с` (U+0441), and so do `en_US.lang:3614`, `uk_UA.lang:3376` and `zh_CN.lang:5966`/`:6142` (a duplicate). `ru_RU.lang:3087` uses the Latin `desc`, so Russian clients fall back to the English text. A fix changes the Java key, en_US, uk_UA and both zh_CN lines together; ru_RU then works as it is.
- `ArmorFSB.onArmorTick` geiger sound only on the chestplate; `HazmatRegistry` piece weights helmet 0.2 / chest 0.4 / legs 0.3 / boots 0.1.
- `ArmorFSBPowered.getCharge` and `ArmorFSBFueled.getFill` write a full-charge/full-fuel tag on the first read of a tag-less stack (ArmorFSBPowered:82-94, ArmorFSBFueled:34-42), so reading the charge mutates the stack.
- `ArmorModHandler.pryMods` mutates NBT (calls `removeMod` for every empty slot, ArmorModHandler:173) and also runs from the tooltip path (ModEventHandlerClient:789).
- `ItemMachineUpgrade` tooltips come from `IUpgradeInfoProvider` only when the open `GuiContainer`'s slot 0 belongs to an inventory implementing it (ItemMachineUpgrade:40-56); otherwise the per-identity fallback text is shown.
- `ItemToolAbility.handleKeybind` refuses to cycle presets when looking at a block that overrides `onBlockActivated` (reflection hack).
- `ModItemsArmor` instantiates `jackt`/`jackt2` twice; `ModItems.java:3185` TODO move syringes; `@Spaghetti` on `ItemStarterKit`, `ItemGlitch`, `ItemSyringe`, `ItemEnergy`, `ArmorModel`; orphan texture `achievement_icon.digammaunity.png`.

---

## 9. Weapons: sedna gun system, projectiles, missiles, grenades

### Purpose

`items/weapon/sedna/`: one item class `ItemGunBaseNT` driven by a config tree `GunConfig -> Receiver[] -> IMagazine -> BulletConfig[]` wired with lambdas and evaluated through `XWeaponModManager` (per-stack mod overrides). Guns are declared in `XFactory*` classes called from `GunFactory.init()` (both sides) and rendered/HUD-configured in `GunFactoryClient.init()` (client, via `proxy.registerGunCfg()`). Projectiles: `EntityBulletBaseMK4` (physical), `EntityBulletBaseMK4CL` (chunk-loading; only `XFactoryFolly.folly_nuke` uses it), `EntityBulletBeamBase` (hitscan). Legacy `ItemGunBase` is gone; `BulletConfiguration`/`BulletConfigSyncingUtil`/`EntityBulletBaseNT` (@Deprecated) survive for NPC attacks and the custom-missile TURBINE warhead. Missiles are `EntityMissileBaseNT` tiers plus `EntityMissileCustom` (`MissileStruct`); the Space fork adds `RocketStruct`/`ItemCustomRocket`/`EntityRideableRocket`. Grenades are one NBT-composed item (`ItemGrenadeUniversal`).

### Key files

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `sedna/ItemGunBaseNT.java` | `GunConfig[] configs_DNA` (akimbo = 2); `getConfig(stack, i)` via `XWeaponModManager.eval`; `onUpdate` state machine (`GunState DRAWING/IDLE/COOLDOWN/RELOADING/JAMMED`, timer, decider lambda); `handleKeybind` press/release lambdas; `renderHUD`; NBT state via static `getValue*/setValue*`: per-config keys are `KEY_*` + config index (`timer_`, `state_`, `mode_`, `wear_`, `mouse1_/2_/3_`, `reload_`, `lastanim_`, `animtimer_`), while `drawn`, `aiming`, `lockontarget`, `lockedon`, `cancel` and `eqipped` are stored once per stack and shared by all configs (both halves of an akimbo gun) (L92-107, accessors L367-409); `playAnimation` always sends receiverIndex 0; static client recoil/aiming fields. |
| `sedna/GunConfig.java`, `Receiver.java`, `BulletConfig.java` | Per-gun config (getters all go through `eval`; `setupStandardConfiguration()`), per-barrel config (`setupStandardFire`/`setupLockonFire`), ammo definition (global `configs` list, `id` = index in creation order; `clone()` re-registers; `pType BULLET/BULLET_CHUNKLOADING/BEAM`; `onUpdate/onImpact/onImpactBeam/onRicochet/onEntityHit`; `getDamage` names the source `dmgClass.name()` and sets a vanilla flag only for PHYSICAL/FIRE/EXPLOSIVE). |
| `sedna/factory/GunFactory.java`, `GunFactoryClient.java`, `Lego.java`, `LegoClient.java`, `GunStateDecider.java`, `Orchestras.java` | Entry point (ammo items, `EnumAmmo` append-only with `order` array, mod enums, ordered `XFactory*.init()` calls incl. `XFactoryFlamer`, `XFactoryDrill`, `XFactoryPA`); client registration (star-imports most factories but NOT Flamer/Drill/PA; flamer ammo gets no renderer); standard lambdas (`doStandardFire` spawns by `pType`); HUD components and `RENDER_*` lambdas; decider composition; 1754 lines of per-gun sound/casing/muzzle timing. |
| `sedna/factory/XFactory9mm.java`, `XFactory12ga.java`, `XFactoryRocket.java`, `XFactoryEnergy.java`, `XFactory40mm.java`, `XFactoryTurret.java`, `XFactoryPA.java`, `XFactoryTool.java`, `XFactoryDrill.java`, `XFactoryFlamer.java` | Compact exemplar; tube mags (`reloadSequential`, `reload(begin, cycle, end, cock)`); rocket templates (`clone()` per launcher, `rocket_ncrpa` and `rocket_ncrpa_steer`); beams; grenades/flares; turret ammo; power-armor delegates (standard decider); extinguisher + charge thrower; drill (`ItemGunDrill`, extra mod keys `D_REACH/F_DTNEG/F_PIERCE/I_AOE/I_HARVEST`); flamers (`MagazineFullReload`; only the chemthrower uses `MagazineFluid`). |
| `sedna/mags/IMagazine.java`, `MagazineSingleTypeBase.java`, `MagazineFullReload.java`, `MagazineSingleReload.java`, `MagazineBelt.java`, `MagazineFluid.java`, `MagazineInfinite.java`, `MagazineLiquidEngine.java`, `MagazineElectricEngine.java` | Magazine strategies; NBT keys `magcount<index>/magtype<index>` (belt uses un-indexed `magtype`); `standardReload(null inventory)` fills for free (NPC guns); `getAmount(null) = 1` for belts; the engine mags fuel the drill (`XFactoryDrill` L57), and `WeaponModEngine` (L13-16) swaps in shared static instances. |
| `sedna/mods/XWeaponModManager.java`, `WeaponModBase.java`, `WeaponModCaliber.java`, `WeaponModScope.java`, `WeaponModDrill*.java` | Mod registry (`init()` in `MainRegistry` after items; `WeaponModDefinition.addMod(gun, mod)`; `idToMod` HashBiMap: duplicate ids silently overwrite; id ranges 0-9 test, 100+ generic, 200+ special (drill 222-232), 300+ caliber; priorities SET > MULTIPLICATIVE > ADDITIVE > default 0 > MULT_FINAL, evaluated highest first (`modSorter` L383-389); `restoreMagState` receiver 0 only), mod base, caliber (shared static `DUMMY_*` mags mutated on eval), scope. Mods compare keys with `==` against the interned `static final` constants (`WeaponModDrill` uses `.equals`). The whole-config key `O_GUNCONFIG + index` (ItemGunBaseNT L123) is built at runtime, so matching it needs `equals`/`startsWith`. |
| `sedna/impl/ItemGunStinger.java`, `ItemGunChargeThrower.java`, `ItemGunChemthrower.java`, `ItemGunDrill.java` | Subclass exemplars (lock-on, grapple, `IFillableItem`). |
| `entity/projectile/EntityBulletBaseMK4.java`, `MK4CL.java`, `EntityBulletBeamBase.java`, `EntityThrowableNT.java`, `EntityThrowableInterp.java`, `EntityBulletBaseNT.java` (@Deprecated), `EntityBullet.java` (legacy) | Config-driven projectile (DataWatcher 3 = config id; lock-on server only; ct_hook special case), hitscan (250 blocks in the gun ctor; `onUpdate` still runs `config.onUpdate`; not persisted), throwable bases. |
| `entity/missile/EntityMissileBaseNT.java`, `EntityMissileTier1.java`, `EntityMissileCustom.java`, `EntityRideableRocket.java`, `handler/MissileStruct.java`, `RocketStruct.java`, `items/weapon/ItemCustomMissilePart.java`, `ItemCustomMissile.java`, `ItemCustomRocket.java`, `ItemMissile.java`, `tileentity/bomb/TileEntityLaunchPadBase.java` | Ballistic missile base (chunkload, radar tier from `ItemMissile.tier`), tier files with static inner concrete missiles, custom missile (`WarheadType` switch marked TODO; `SCHRAB`, `APOLLO`, `SATELLITE`, `CUSTOMn` without `impactCustom` do nothing; `CLUSTER` explicit no-op), rideable multi-stage rocket (`RocketStruct.setupDataWatcher` L392-398 reserves a fixed block of 2 + 2*MAX_STAGES ids from 11, i.e. 11-22 at `MAX_STAGES = 5`, which must stay the highest; vanilla `DataWatcher.addObject` rejects ids above 31, so MAX_STAGES <= 9), item->entity map `TileEntityLaunchPadBase.missiles` (L62), filled in `registerLaunchables()` L64-98 (called from `MainRegistry` L337). |

| `inventory/container/ContainerWeaponTable.java`, `entity/EntityMappings.java`, `crafting/WeaponRecipes.java`, `inventory/recipes/AmmoPressRecipes.java` | Only place mods get installed; entity registration (`entity_bullet_mk4` etc L102-106); gun recipes (L67); ammo press recipes (`DictFrame.fromOne(ModItems.ammo_standard, EnumAmmo.X, n)`). |

### Patterns

- Builder declaration: `new ItemGunBaseNT(WeaponQuality, new GunConfig().dura().draw().inspect().crosshair().smoke().rec(new Receiver(0).dmg().delay().spread().reload().jam().sound().mag(...).offset(f, u, s).setupStandardFire().recoil(...)).setupStandardConfiguration().anim(...).orchestra(...)).setDefaultAmmo(EnumAmmo.X, n).setUnlocalizedName("gun_x")`.
- Lambda types: `BiConsumer<ItemStack, LambdaContext>` (press/release/decider/orchestra/smoke/onFire/onRecoil), `BiFunction<ItemStack, LambdaContext, Boolean>` (canFire), `BiFunction<ItemStack, GunAnimation, BusAnimation>` (anims).
- Animation sync: server `playAnimation` -> `HbmAnimationPacket` + NBT `KEY_LASTANIM_/KEY_ANIMTIMER_`; `Orchestras` compare `getLastAnim/getAnimTimer` to tick offsets (anim millis / 50); client stores into `HbmAnimations.hotbar[slot][gunIndex]`; renderers apply the root bus unwrapped then push/pop per child part.
- Impact pipeline (MK4, server only, `EntityBulletBaseMK4.onImpact` L187-195): `onImpact`, then return if the bullet is now dead or `inGround`, then `onRicochet` (default `LAMBDA_STANDARD_RICOCHET`), then `onEntityHit` (default `LAMBDA_STANDARD_ENTITY_HIT`: `EntityDamageUtil.attackEntityFromNT` for living targets, `attackEntityFromIgnoreIFrame` otherwise). An `onImpact` that calls `setDead()` skips the other two. Beams call `onImpactBeam` (null by default; commonly `BulletConfig.LAMBDA_STANDARD_BEAM_HIT`) from `performHitscan`.
- Weapon quality (`ItemGunBaseNT` ctor L136-137): `A_SIDE` (core guns), `SPECIAL` (off-tier specials: double barrel, bolter, coilgun, NI4NI, Stinger) and `UTILITY` (tools: extinguisher, charge thrower, drill, PA melee/ranged) go into `weaponTab`. `B_SIDE` variants and `DEBUG` get no creative tab. `LEGENDARY` and `SECRET` get no tab and are added to `ItemGunBaseNT.secrets`, which `NEIConfig` L50 hides from NEI; most of them are crafted via `PedestalRecipes`.
- Other MK4 consumers: `TileEntityTurretBaseNT.spawnBullet`, `ModEventHandler` (~L1122 gauntlet), `ArmorNCRPARanged`, `ItemGrenadeFilling` submunitions, `TileEntityPileCore`, `TileEntityBatterySocket.discharge` (beam), `EntityAI*` NPC AIs, `EntityAIFireGun` (drives held guns with a null-inventory context).

### How-to

- New ammo: append to `EnumAmmo` (bottom) + insert into `EnumAmmo.order`; icon `textures/items/ammo_standard.<lower>.png`; lang `item.ammo_standard.<lower>.name`. In the caliber factory declare `public static BulletConfig p9_xxx;` and assign it inside `init()`: `p9_xxx = new BulletConfig().setItem(EnumAmmo.P9_XXX).setCasing(EnumCasingType.SMALL, 12).setCasing(casing9.clone().register("p9xxx"))...` (`casing9` is a local of `init()`; only `XFactoryBlackPowder` uses static initializers). Add it to every magazine's `addConfigs` and to the caliber tables at the bottom of `XWeaponModManager.init()` (~L171); `p9_xxx.setRenderer(LegoClient.RENDER_STANDARD_BULLET)` in `GunFactoryClient.init()` (invisible otherwise); `AmmoPressRecipes` entry. BulletConfig ids follow creation order and are stored in gun NBT (`magtype<index>`): a config created anywhere but at the end of the sequence shifts every later id, and loaded guns in existing saves can change ammo type. Exemplar `XFactory9mm.java`.
- New gun: `public static Item gun_foo;` in `ModItems` plus `GameRegistry.registerItem(gun_foo, gun_foo.getUnlocalizedName());` in `ModItems.registerItem()` next to the other guns (~L6372-6444); `GunFactory`/`XFactory*.init()` only assign the field, so without the registration line the gun is silently unobtainable. Builder in an `XFactory*.init()`; a new factory's `init()` must be called from `GunFactory.init()`, and one that creates BulletConfigs goes after `XFactoryPA.init()` at the end so existing ids do not shift; static-import it in `GunFactoryClient` if client code needs its statics. Anims lambda: `new BusAnimation().addBus("NAME", new BusAnimationSequence().addPos(...))` or `ResourceManager.<gun>_anim.get("<key>")`, where the key is whatever the exported JSON names (e.g. `lag_anim.get("Firing")`, `am180_anim.get("Fire")`). `Orchestras.ORCHESTRA_FOO`; `render/item/weapon/sedna/ItemRenderFoo extends ItemRenderWeaponBase`; `ResourceManager` model/texture; `MinecraftForgeClient.registerItemRenderer` + `getConfig(null, 0).hud(...)` in `GunFactoryClient` (`*_MIRROR` HUD components on config index 0 of akimbo guns; exceptions: `gun_fireext`'s renderer is registered in `ClientProxy` L654, and `gun_pa_ranged` has none (flat icon, `XFactoryPA` L43)); lang `item.gun_foo.name`; recipe in `WeaponRecipes` (`//SEDNA Guns`, L61-111), or `PedestalRecipes` for LEGENDARY/SECRET variants; add to `XWeaponModManager` material tables (a null gun there throws ClassCastException at `addMod`).
- New weapon mod: append the enum constant (item meta); texture `weapon_mod_<kind>.<lower>.png`, lang `item.weapon_mod_<kind>.<lower>.name`, recipe in `WeaponRecipes` (`//SEDNA Mods`, L119-165). `WeaponModFoo extends WeaponModBase`, calling `super(id, "SLOT")` (slots are mutex groups), with `eval(base, gun, key, parent)` comparing `key == Receiver.F_BASEDAMAGE` etc and returning `cast(...)`. Choose `setPriority`: mods are evaluated in descending priority (SET 1,000,000, MULTIPLICATIVE 1,000, ADDITIVE 500, default 0, MULT_FINAL -1; `WeaponModBase` L5-11), contrary to the `IWeaponMod` L7 javadoc. A mod that replaces the magazine calls `XWeaponModManager.changedMagState()` in `onInstall`/`onUninstall` (otherwise `restoreMagState` exits early, L285). Register with `new WeaponModDefinition(EnumModSpecial.FOO).addMod(guns, new WeaponModFoo(unusedId))` in `XWeaponModManager.init()`; grep ids first (no duplicate rejection). Exemplar `WeaponModCaliber.java`.
- Rocket ammo variant: append `EnumAmmo.ROCKET_X` (and add it to `order`); enlarge `rocket_template = new BulletConfig[5]` (XFactoryRocket L162) and add `rocket_template[n] = baseRocket.clone().setItem(EnumAmmo.ROCKET_X).setOnImpact(LAMBDA)`. The loop at L178-184 clones each template for the five launcher arrays, so one variant adds six BulletConfig ids mid-sequence. Impact lambdas skip entity hits while `ticksExisted < 3`, call `Lego.standardExplode(bullet, mop, range)` and end with `bullet.setDead()`; renderers via `setRendererBulk` (GunFactoryClient L215-219). 40 mm grenades are individual configs in `XFactory40mm`. Exemplar `XFactoryRocket.java`.
- Beam ammo: `.setBeam().setupDamageClass(DamageClass.LASER).setOnBeamImpact(...)` + `setRendererBeam`. Exemplar `XFactoryEnergy.java`.
- Custom warhead: `ModItems` field `new ItemCustomMissilePart().makeWarhead(WarheadType.CUSTOMn, punch, mass, PartSize.SIZE_15)...` plus its `GameRegistry.registerItem`. Register the part in both `MissilePart.registerAllParts()` (client, with model/texture; `ClientProxy` L909) and `MissilePart.registerAllPartsServer()` (`ServerProxy` L56): the assembler GUI/TESR, `RenderMissileCustom` and `MissileMultipart` resolve parts via `MissilePart.getPart`. Set `WarheadType.CUSTOMn.impactCustom` (server only), `updateCustom` (every tick, both sides) and `labelCustom` during init, directly or via `CompatExternal.setWarheadImpact/Update/Label` (L191-193). The hooks are fields on the enum constant, shared by every warhead of that CUSTOMn.
- Tiered missile: static inner class in the tier file with both ctors (the pad instantiates `(World, float, float, float, int, int)` reflectively, `TileEntityLaunchPadBase` L342, and swallows failures), `onMissileImpact`, `getDebrisRareDrop`, `getMissileItemForInfo`. An `addEntity(...)` line in `EntityMappings.writeMappings()` (network ids follow list position, mobs after all entities, L228-235; saves use the `hbm.<name>` string and only `addMob` entries get spawn-egg ids, so inserting an `addEntity` line changes no saved data). Entity renderer `RenderMissileGeneric/Strong/Huge/Nuclear` (`ClientProxy` ~710) plus an `instanceof` texture branch inside that renderer. Item `new ItemMissile(form, tier)` in `ModItems` plus its registration. `ItemRenderMissileGeneric` registration in `ClientProxy` (~587-614) and a `renderers.put(new ComparableStack(ModItems.missile_foo), generateStandard(tex, model))` line in `ItemRenderMissileGeneric.init()` (L129-168): the item renderer, launch-pad TESRs and pad GUI all read that map and render nothing without an entry. `missiles.put(...)` inside `TileEntityLaunchPadBase.registerLaunchables()` (L64-98). Exemplar `EntityMissileTier1.java`.
- Grenade shell/filling/fuze/extra: append the enum constant (filling/fuze/extra constants carry lambdas; `EnumGrenadeShell` takes only stack limit, draw time, bounce and throw force, ItemGrenadeShell L33-48). Ordinals are the item meta of the `grenade_*` parts and are stored as ints in `grenade_universal` NBT (ItemGrenadeUniversal L161-164). A filling lists its compatible shells in its enum constructor. Texture `grenade_<part>.<lower>.png`, lang `item.grenade_<part>.<lower>.name`. Submunition `BulletConfig`s are created in the `ItemGrenadeFilling` constructor (L57-63), which runs at ModItems L4067 before `GunFactory.init()`, so adding one there shifts every gun BulletConfig id; give it a renderer in `GunFactoryClient` (L251-252). Recipes in `crafting/handlers/GrenadeCraftingHandler`.

### Gotchas

- Positional ids everywhere. `BulletConfig` ids follow creation order: the `ItemGrenadeFilling` constructor (ModItems L4067) creates the first four, then the `GunFactory.init()` sequence runs. The only persisted copy is the gun NBT `magtype<index>` (belt: `magtype`); creating a config anywhere but at the end, or reordering init calls, remaps loaded ammo in existing saves (a mismatched id falls back to the magazine's first accepted config). Turrets rebuild `getAmmoList()` from `.id` at runtime and store no ids; projectiles only sync the id via DataWatcher 3. `EnumAmmo`/`EnumAmmoSecret`/`EnumMod*`/grenade enum ordinals (item meta, grenade NBT) and weapon-mod ids (gun NBT `KEY_MOD_LIST_<cfg>`) are persisted. `BulletConfigSyncingUtil` ids are sync-only (`EntityBulletBaseNT.writeToNBTOptional` returns false).
- Create BulletConfigs inside the `GunFactory.init()` sequence (appended at its end), not in `static {}` blocks of lazily loaded classes. `TileEntityPileCore.pile_debris` (L654-656) and `TileEntityBatterySocket.discharge` (L72-75) are initialised on the client by `GunFactoryClient.init()` (discharge at L228, then pile_debris at L254); on a dedicated server only when the classes are first used (TE creation, or `BlockPile.breakBlock` reading `TileEntityPileCore.meltingDown`). Their ids can therefore differ between server and client, and the DataWatcher-synced id resolves to the wrong config client-side (invisible debris or beam). Singleplayer is unaffected.
- NPC attacks mutate shared player ammo: `EntityBFAngel` L445/L465 (`energy_tesla_overcharge`) and L486 (`flame_balefire`), `EntityAIBehemothGun` L88 (`r762_ap`) and `EntitySiegeUFO` L138 (`energy_emerald_overcharge`) call `setKnockback(0)` on the global static (setters return `this`). It matters for `r762_ap` and `energy_emerald_overcharge`, whose hit lambdas pass `knockbackMult` on (`LAMBDA_STANDARD_ENTITY_HIT` `BulletConfig` L249, `LAMBDA_STANDARD_BEAM_HIT` L278): after the first NPC shot, player rounds of those types have no knockback. `flame_balefire` is already `setKnockback(0F)` (XFactoryFlamer L121) and `LAMBDA_LIGHTNING_HIT` (XFactoryEnergy L67) never reads the field, so the calls on those two configs (EntityBFAngel L445, L465, L486) change nothing. A per-NPC variant needs a `clone()` made inside the GunFactory sequence (clone registers a new id).
- `SpentCasing.register(name)` global map; always clone + unique name.
- `Lego.LAMBDA_STANDARD_CLICK_SECONDARY` reads `getMode(stack, 0)` but writes `ctx.configIndex` (akimbo inconsistency). `GunConfig.getReceivers(stack)[0]` is hard-wired into the standard reload/canFire/decider lambdas.
- `EntityBulletBeamBase`: only the 7-argument gun constructor aims and runs the 250-block hitscan; with the `(World|EntityLivingBase, BulletConfig, damage)` constructors the caller sets the position and calls `setRotationsFromVector` + `performHitscanExternal(range)`. Beams are never saved (`writeToNBTOptional` returns false). `EntityBulletBaseMK4.setDead()` sends a tracker teleport so 1-tick bullets render.
- `getBulletConfig` in `EntityBulletBaseMK4` (L116) and `EntityBulletBeamBase` (L118) tests `id > configs.size()`, so id == size throws IndexOutOfBoundsException instead of returning null; `MagazineBelt` L155 indexes `configs` unchecked. `EntityBulletBaseMK4` has no NBT code, so a bullet saved in flight reloads with id 0 (`ItemGrenadeFilling.fragmentation`, life 3) and expires.
- `ItemGunBaseNT.getShareTag` override is commented out ("nbt sync dupe fix, didn't work"); NPC guns reload for free and skip `EQUIP`.
- `XWeaponModManager.install()` keys by `new ComparableStack(stack)` while `modFromStack` uses `makeSingular()`; `recognizedMods` only filled by `addMod` with a non-null gun.
- `BulletConfig.getDamage` (L153-170) names the DamageSource `dmgClass.name()` and sets a vanilla flag only for PHYSICAL (projectile), FIRE (fire) and EXPLOSIVE (explosion). The other six classes (ELECTRIC, PLASMA, LASER, MICROWAVE, SUBATOMIC, OTHER) get none; the explicit ELECTRIC/LASER/SUBATOMIC cases are empty.
- `ItemGunBaseNT.handleKeybind` returns at once when `GeneralConfig.enableGuns` is false (L243), so every sedna gun goes inert. `onUpdate` also runs smoke handlers and orchestras on the client for the local player's held gun (L296-324). Most orchestras return at once when `worldObj.isRemote` (e.g. `ORCHESTRA_GREASEGUN` L202); `ORCHESTRA_FLAMER`/`STINGER`/`CHEMTHROWER`/`TAU`/`DRILL` use the client call for looped sounds (`ItemGunBaseNT.loopedSounds`), so a new orchestra has to check the side itself.
- Smells: `XWeaponModManager.java:277` TODO receiver-0-only mag restore; `GunFactoryClient.java:249` TODO sabots; `Lego.java:42` "this turned into fucking spaghetti"; `EntityMissileCustom.java:167` TODO demolish switch; `EntityBulletBaseMK4.java:159` ct_hook hack; `GunB92` @Spaghetti("destroy this class"); `GunRocketFactory` is legacy but live (`GunNPCFactory.getRocketUFOConfig()` L225 builds the `BulletConfigSyncingUtil.UFO_ROCKET` config that `EntityUFO.rocketAttack` L343 fires); typos preserved as identifiers (`ORCHESTRA_PANERSCHRECK`, `LAMBDA_CLICK_MELEE_SENONDARY`).

## 10. Recipes, ore dictionary, fluids, materials, item pools

### Purpose

JSON-configurable machine recipes (`SerializableRecipe` and the generic `GenericRecipes`/`GenericRecipe`), the `AStack` ingredient abstraction (`ComparableStack`/`NBTStack`/`OreDictStack`), ore-dict naming (`OreDictManager.DictFrame`/`DictGroup` + `MaterialShapes` prefixes), the material/quanta system (`Mats`/`NTMMaterial`/`MaterialShapes`/`MatDistribution`), the fluid registry with traits (`Fluids`/`FluidType`/`FluidTrait` + `FluidContainerRegistry`), crafting-table recipes (`CraftingManager` + `com/hbm/crafting/*`) and weighted loot pools (`ItemPool*`). Recipe JSON lives in `config/hbmRecipes/`; fluid/item-pool/custom-machine JSON in `config/hbmConfig/`.

### Key files

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `inventory/recipes/loader/SerializableRecipe.java` | Base of all JSON recipe sets. `registerAllHandlers()` ordered list (called once in PostLoad); `initialize()`: `clearPools`, per handler `deleteRecipes` -> (first a server-synced stream in `recipeSyncHandlers`, else `config/hbmRecipes/<file>`, else `registerDefaults()` + `IRecipeRegisterListener` + `_<file>` template) -> `registerPost()`; `modified` flag. No per-handler error isolation. Helpers `readAStack/writeAStack` (`["item", name, size?, meta?]`, `["dict", name, size?]`, `["nbt", name, size, meta, nbt]`; NBT stacks lose meta on read), `readItemStack` (`[name, size?, meta?, nbt?]`), `readFluidStack` (`[name, mB, pressure?]`), `matchesIngredients`. Unparseable stacks degrade to `ModItems.nothing`. |
| `loader/GenericRecipes.java`, `GenericRecipe.java` | Generic set (`*Limit()` abstract methods, `instantiateRecipe`, `readExtraData`/`writeExtraData`, `recipeOrderedList`, `recipeNameMap`, static `blueprintPools`/`nameToRecipeGlobal` (cross-set name collisions silently overwrite), `autoSwitchGroups`, `ChanceOutput`/`ChanceOutputMulti`); recipe builders (`setup`, `setupNamed`, `inputItems` (throws if size > max stack), `inputItemsEx`/`inputFluidsEx` (expensive-mode replacements: they replace the whole input list only when `enableExpensiveMode` is set; chain them AFTER `inputItems`/`inputFluids`, which assign unconditionally), `setPools` (throws on `528.` when 528 off), `setPools528` (applied only in 528 mode), `setGroup`, `setIcon`). |
| `inventory/RecipesCommon.java` | `AStack` (`matchesRecipe`, `compareTo` NBT > Comparable > OreDict), `ComparableStack` (equals treats WILDCARD as any but hashCode includes meta), `NBTStack`, `OreDictStack`; `ComparableStack(Item)` substitutes `ModItems.nothing` for null. |
| `inventory/OreDictManager.java` | `DictFrame` constants (`U`, `STEEL`, ...; `U` is named `Uraninite` under GT6), `DictGroup` (`ANY_PLASTIC`...), `registerOres()` (fluent registrations, autogen loop L631-654, fragment 9-to-1, `registerCompatShapes`, `compensateMojangSpaghettiBullshit`), `registerGroups()`, `@SubscribeEvent onRegisterOre` (re-registers group aliases, fills `arcSmeltable`). Ingots also registered under the bare material name (NuclearCraft compat; TODO config). |
| `inventory/material/MaterialShapes.java`, `NTMMaterial.java`, `Mats.java`, `MatDistribution.java` | Shapes with quanta (`NUGGET 8`, `INGOT 72`, `BLOCK 648`, `QUART 162`; prefixes incl. `FRAGMENT = bedrockorefragment`, `PIPE = ntmpipe`, `CASTPLATE = plateTriple`, `WELDEDPLATE = plateSextuple`); materials (id = autogen item meta; scheme `_VS` 0-29, `_AS` 30-99, `_ES` 20000+, `_EX` 24000+, elements Z*100+mass); `Mats` constants + `materialEntries`/`materialOreEntries`; crucible smelting JSON (must precede `ArcFurnaceRecipes` in `registerAllHandlers`). |
| `inventory/fluid/Fluids.java`, `FluidType.java`, `trait/FluidTrait.java`, `FluidTraitSimple.java`, `FT_Gaseous.java`, `FT_Combustible.java`, `FT_Rocket.java` | Registry (`init()` declaration-order IDs, `//ADD NEW FLUIDS HERE` ~L545, `metaOrder` size check at L887, `hbmFluidTypes.json` custom fluids with explicit ids, `reloadFluids()` preserves instances via `fluidMigration`, `readTraits` rebuilds a fluid's traits reflectively from `hbmFluidTraits.json`); fluid (`hbmfluid.<name>`, `getDict(mB)` = `(enableFluidContainerCompat ? "container" : "ntmcontainer") + mB + name-without-underscores-lowercase`, `getNetworkProvider()`); trait base (`traitNameMap` = JSON keys); tag traits; gas trait with atmosphere helpers; data trait exemplar; Space rocket trait (no no-arg ctor, so it cannot be instantiated from JSON). |
| `inventory/FluidContainerRegistry.java`, `FluidContainer.java`, `FluidStack.java`, `fluid/tank/FluidTank.java` | Container generation from `CD_*` descriptors/traits (loop from index 1 uses `Fluids.fromID(i)` for disperser/gland, wrong for custom ids), lookups, `clearRegistry()`; POJOs; machine tank with `loadingHandlers`. |
| `main/CraftingManager.java`, `crafting/PowderRecipes.java`, `MineralRecipes.java`, `handlers/ScrapsCraftingHandler.java` | `addRecipeAuto`/`addShapelessAuto` (String ingredient -> ore recipe; shaped detection needs a String after the pattern rows), `IRecipe` handlers + `RecipeSorter`, `ContainerUpgradeCraftingHandler` instantiated per crate in `AddCraftingRec`. |
| `itempool/ItemPool.java`, `ItemPoolsC130.java`, `config/ItemPoolConfigJSON.java` | Named weighted pools (`getStack(name, rand)`, `backupPool` fallback); JSON replaces the whole map, template written only when the live file is absent. |
| `inventory/recipes/PressRecipes.java`, `CentrifugeRecipes.java`, `ShredderRecipes.java`, `ChemicalPlantRecipes.java`, `AssemblyMachineRecipes.java`, `BlastFurnaceRecipesNT.java`, `BlastFurnaceRecipes.java` (@Deprecated, still used by DiFurnace tiles and their NEI handler; file `hbmBlastFurnaceLegacy.json`), `FusionRecipes.java`, `PrecAssRecipes.java`, `CrucibleRecipes.java`, `ArcFurnaceRecipes.java`, `CustomMachineRecipes.java`, `anvil/AnvilRecipes.java`, `AtmosphereRecipes.java`, `CryoRecipes.java`, `MachineRecipes.java` (@Spaghetti), `SILEXRecipes.java` | Classic and generic exemplars. Only `ShredderRecipes`, `CentrifugeRecipes` and `FusionRecipes` override `registerPost()`. `ShredderRecipes.registerPost()` auto-generates ore-dict shredding (ingot/plate/gem/crystal/ore/block/dust names) through `setRecipe`, which puts only if the key is absent, so JSON (and `registerDefaults`) entries win for the same input, but JSON cannot remove generated entries (the file's own `getComment` says they cannot be changed). `CentrifugeRecipes.registerPost()` merges `IMCCentrifuge.buffer` over the set (overriding JSON entries with the same input) and then clears the buffer, so IMC centrifuge recipes are lost at the next `initialize()` (`/ntmreload`, a received server sync, or disconnecting after one). `FusionRecipes.registerPost()` only recomputes `maxInput`. `ArcFurnaceRecipes` has no `registerPost`: its material/bedrock-ore/furnace autogen runs inside `registerDefaults()`, so a live `hbmArcFurnace.json` replaces all of it, and the `_hbmArcFurnace.json` template contains the generated entries. The legacy `BlastFurnaceRecipes` drains `IMCBlastFurnace.buffer` inside `registerDefaults()`, so IMC blast recipes apply only on the no-JSON path, and only at the first init. Anvil smithing is static (not JSON), construction is `hbmAnvil.json`; `AtmosphereRecipes` has no-op read/write. |
| `module/machine/ModuleMachineBase.java`, `handler/nei/NEIGenericRecipeHandler.java`, `util/CompatRecipeRegistry.java`, `api/hbm/recipe/package-info.java`, `packet/toclient/SerializableRecipePacket.java`, `commands/CommandReloadRecipes.java` | Consumer, NEI base, addon API (@Untested), addon guide, server->client sync, `/ntmreload`. |

### Patterns

- Handler order matters only where code reads another set: `MatDistribution` before `ArcFurnaceRecipes`. The `//AFTER Assembler` comment above `AnvilRecipes` is stale (Assembler is added later and Anvil does not reference it). `CrucibleRecipes.getSmeltingRecipes()` is computed lazily for NEI.
- Template format: `{"comment": ..., "recipes": [...]}`; `getRecipeObject()` must be a Collection or HashMap.
- Generic recipe names use a machine prefix (`chem.`, `ass.`, `purex.`, `fus.`, `plsm.`, `precass.`, `blast.`, `crucible.`); the name doubles as lang key with `setNamed`.
- Ore dict: `STEEL.ingot()` getter = `MaterialShapes.INGOT.name() + "Steel"`; setters `STEEL.ingot(items...)` register and apply hazards; `.rad()/.hot()/...` must be chained BEFORE the shape setters (hazards snapshot at registration; shape order among themselves does not matter). `DictGroup.addPrefix` + `onRegisterOre` re-register under shape prefix + group name (e.g. `ingotAnyPlastic`, read back via `ANY_PLASTIC.ingot()`); `registerGroups` must precede `registerOres`. Only registrations made after the handler is registered and `registerGroups()` has run (MainRegistry PreLoad L302-304) are aliased: Forge's vanilla entries (e.g. `ingotIron`) and anything registered earlier in PreLoad are not.
- Autogen: `NTMMaterial.setAutogen(shapes)` only has an effect for `ItemAutogen` shapes: subitems, plus ore dict for BOLT, INGOT->ingot_raw, SHELL, PIPE, FRAGMENT, WIRE, barrels/receivers/mechanism/stock/grip, and CASTPLATE/WELDEDPLATE/DENSEWIRE when SMELTABLE. It also generates recipes: WIRE gives a press wire-stamp recipe (8 per ingot), tier-4 anvil construction and, under LBSM simple crafting, 3 ingots -> 24 wires; BOLT gives 2 ingots -> 16 bolts crafting; SHELL gives anvil construction (4 plates); PIPE gives anvil construction (3 plates, or ingots); FRAGMENT gives 9-to-1 crafting. DUST/PLATE/BLOCK/NUGGET/BILLET in `setAutogen` are inert. Crucible/arc smelting autogen iterate all non-`noAutogen` prefixes present in the ore dict regardless of `setAutogen` (crucible: SMELTABLE or ADDITIVE; arc: SMELTABLE).
- Fluids: `new FluidType(name, color, p, f, r, EnumSymbol)` registers itself with id = current size; custom/foreign fluids use `Fluids.register(fluid, id)` (overwrites blindly). Trait queries `type.hasTrait(FT_X.class)`/`getTrait`.
- Fluid traits (`inventory/fluid/trait/`): data traits `FT_Combustible(FuelGrade, energyPerBucket)` (combustion engine, diesel, turbofan, gas turbine...), `FT_Flammable` (oil burners, wood burner, drains/tanks catching fire), `FT_Corrosive` (the rating drives chemical spray/mist damage (`EntityChemical`/`EntityMist`), and `isHighlyCorrosive()` drives the fluid-tank block (`TileEntityMachineFluidTank`, `RenderFluidTank`); presence alone is checked by plastic barrels, the pipette, `PneumoTube` and atmosphere corrosion (`ChunkAtmosphereHandler`); `FluidTank` does not read it), `FT_Heatable`/`FT_Coolable` (heat exchanger, boiler and turbine tables: heat boiler, fusion boiler, PWR, Watz, steam engine, turbines), `FT_Polluting` (release type -> `PollutionHandler`: emitters, blast furnace, engines), `FT_VentRadiation`/`FT_Poison`/`FT_Toxin`/`FT_Pheromone`/`FT_Terraformer` (`EntityChemical`/`EntityMist` cloud effects), `FT_Rocket` (Space: thrust/isp for HTR3/HTRF4, xenon thruster, stations), `FT_PWRModerator`; tag traits in `FluidTraitSimple`: `FT_Gaseous_ART` (`EVAP`, key `gaseous_art`, gaseous at room temperature), `FT_Liquid`, `FT_Viscous`, `FT_Plasma` (@Deprecated), `FT_Amat`, `FT_LeadContainer`, `FT_Delicious`, `FT_EXPLOSIVE`, `FT_ULTRAKILL`, `FT_Unsiphonable`, `FT_NoID`, `FT_NoContainer`, and `FT_Leaded`. `FT_Leaded` is unused and NOT registered in `FluidTrait`'s static block: attaching it to a fluid crashes `Fluids.init` (NPE in `writeDefaultTraits`) on installs without a live `hbmFluidTraits.json`. `FT_Gaseous` (key `gaseous`) is a separate class, `trait/FT_Gaseous.java`: its static `release`/`capture` move gas into and out of `CelestialBody` atmospheres (atmospheric emitter/compressor, drain, intake, Dyson anatmogenesis converter, atmosphere editor, `CelestialBody.reactAtmosphere`). Traits are keyed by exact class, so gas checks test `FT_Gaseous` and `FT_Gaseous_ART` separately (air pump, gas flare, fluid tank, mist, pneumatic tube). Query with `type.hasTrait(FT_X.class)`/`getTrait`.
- Containers: `.addContainers(new CD_Canister(color), new CD_Gastank(bottleColor, labelColor))` on the `FluidType` (both are inner classes of `Fluids`). `FluidContainerRegistry.register()` (PostLoad ~L574 and `/ntmreload`) loops `Fluids.getAll()` from index 1. It registers `canister_full`/`gas_full` at meta = fluid id (1000 mB; empties `canister_empty`/`gas_empty`) when the descriptor is present, then skips `FT_NoContainer` fluids. For the rest it adds `disperser_canister` (2000 mB) and `glyphid_gland` (4000 mB) if `isDispersable()` (not AMAT/NOCON/VISCOUS; by loop index, B-137), and `fluid_tank_lead_full` (1000 mB). Unless the fluid has `FT_LeadContainer`, it also adds `fluid_tank_full` (1000 mB) and `fluid_barrel_full` (16000 mB). Every container is also ore-dicted as `type.getDict(mB)`. The items take their icon and name from the fluid (`hbmfluid.<name>`).
- Config flags read by recipe defaults: `GeneralConfig.enable528`, `enable528PressurizedRecipes`, `enableExpensiveMode` (read directly, e.g. by `inputItemsEx`/`inputFluidsEx`, `AnvilRecipes`, `ExposureChamberRecipes`, `PrecAssRecipes`), `enableLBSM*`, `enableServerRecipeSync`. `trueExp()` (= expensive && `!PrecAssRecipes.INSTANCE.modified`) only drives the HUD badge in `RenderScreenOverlay` and gates no recipe.
- Addon contract: `IRecipeRegisterListener.onRecipeLoad` fires only in the defaults branch; `IFluidRegisterListener` fires in `init` and `reloadFluids`.

### How-to

- Generic recipe / classic recipe / new GenericRecipes set (`INSTANCE`, `*Limit()`, `getFileName` `hbmMyMachine.json`, `instantiateRecipe`, `registerDefaults`; add to `registerAllHandlers()` `//GENERIC` block after any set it reads; `NEIGenericRecipeHandler` subclass + `NEIRegistry.listAllHandlers()`; consume via `ModuleMachineBase.getRecipeSet()` or `recipeNameMap`) / new classic set (extends `SerializableRecipe`: `getFileName`, `registerDefaults`, `getRecipeObject` (Collection or HashMap), `deleteRecipes`, `readRecipe`, `writeRecipe`; optional `getComment`/`registerPost`/`allowEmptyRecipeList` (the last is required if the default list can be empty, otherwise no template is written); then `recipeHandlers.add(new X())` in `registerAllHandlers()` after any set it reads; without that line the set never loads): exemplars `ChemicalPlantRecipes.java`, `PressRecipes.java`, `BlastFurnaceRecipesNT.java` (plain set with power 0; it does NOT override `hasPower()`; a JSON entry missing `power`/`duration` NPEs unless you override `hasPower`/`hasDuration`), `CryoRecipes.java`.
- New fluid: field in `inventory/fluid/Fluids.java`; define at the END of `init()` directly above `//ADD NEW FLUIDS HERE` (~L545; ID = declaration index, persisted in saves) as `X = new FluidType("X", 0xRRGGBB, p, f, r, EnumSymbol.NONE).addTraits(LIQUID, new FT_Combustible(FuelGrade.MEDIUM, 200_000L), ...).addContainers(new CD_Canister(0xRRGGBB), new CD_Gastank(...))`; `metaOrder.add(X);` (a missing entry crashes `Fluids.init` with "MetaOrder and Mappings are inconsistent", checked at ~L887); texture `textures/gui/fluids/<lowercase>.png`; lang `hbmfluid.<lowercase>`; crafting-table references use `Fluids.X.getDict(1000)`, which only matches if a 1000 mB container is registered: a `CD_*` descriptor, or the lead/steel fluid tank that every non-`FT_NoContainer` fluid gets. New trait: public no-arg ctor; `registerTrait("name", Class)` in `FluidTrait`'s static block (the name is the `hbmFluidTraits.json` key). An unregistered trait on any fluid crashes `Fluids.init`/`reloadFluids` with an NPE in `writeDefaultTraits` whenever no live `hbmFluidTraits.json` exists. Data traits must override `serializeJSON`/`deserializeJSON`, or a live `hbmFluidTraits.json` that lists the fluid resets them to the no-arg defaults. Exemplars `Fluids.java`, `trait/FT_Combustible.java`.
- New material: `DictFrame` constant; `Mats.MAT_X = makeSmeltable(uniqueId, FRAME, light, dark, molten).setAutogen(...).m()`; `registerOres()` line for hand-made items; `CrucibleRecipes`/`MatDistribution` entries for alloys; lang `hbmmat.x`; `ItemAutogen.aot` texture override if needed. Exemplar `Mats.java`.
- Ore-dict group: declare `public static final DictGroup ANY_X = new DictGroup("AnyX", FRAME_A, FRAME_B);` in `OreDictManager` and add `ANY_X.addPrefix(INGOT, true)` in `registerGroups()`. Every `ingot<Mat>` registration of the frames' names is then re-registered as `ingotAnyX` (prefix + group name); consume it with `ANY_X.ingot()`. With `addPrefix(shape, false)` the input is the bare mat name (e.g. `ANY_TAR` = group `Tar` -> `anyTar`). Only registrations made after `registerGroups()` (MainRegistry PreLoad ~L304) are aliased. Forge's vanilla entries (e.g. `ingotIron`) and anything registered earlier in PreLoad are not.
- Crafting recipe: `CraftingManager.addRecipeAuto(new ItemStack(out, n), new Object[]{"ABC", ..., 'A', STEEL.plate(), 'D', Fluids.WATER.getDict(1000)})`; `MineralRecipes.add1To9Pair`; smelting in `crafting/SmeltingRecipes.java` (no ore dict); custom `IRecipe` + `RecipeSorter.register("hbm:name", ...)`.
- Loot pool: `new ItemPool(POOL_X) {{ this.pool = new WeightedRandomChestContent[]{ weighted(item, meta, min, max, weight) }; }}` in an `ItemPools*.init()`; a new `ItemPools*` class must be added to `ItemPool.initialize()`. Consume with `ItemPool.getStack`/`getPool`. Installs with a live `hbmItemPools.json` do not see new code pools until the entry is added to that file: they silently get `backupPool`, and the `_` template is not rewritten while the live file exists.
- Fluid container item: `FluidContainerRegistry.registerContainer(new FluidContainer(full, emptyOrNull, Fluids.X, mB))` before the `getAll()` loop.
- Anvil: construction `constructionRecipes.add(new AnvilConstructionRecipe(inputs, outputs).setTier(n))`; smithing `smithingRecipes.add(new AnvilSmithingRecipe(tier, out, left, right))` (static, PostLoad).
- Fork recipe: either inline in the set's `registerDefaults()` (as above) or in `com/hbm/dbs/DBSRecipes.java`, an `IRecipeRegisterListener` registered by `DBSFork.init()`; both behave the same (JSON override, `/ntmreload`, server sync). `DBSRecipes` never conflicts on an upstream merge; inline is simpler to read. `onRecipeLoad(className)` dispatches on the set's simple class name (`AssemblyMachineRecipes` -> `registerAssembly(AssemblyMachineRecipes.INSTANCE)`, `AnvilRecipes` -> `registerAnvilConstruction()`); for another set add a branch and a method. The listener fires inside `SerializableRecipe.initialize()` after `registerDefaults()` and before the template is written, only on the no-JSON path, so semantics equal an inline default and the recipe lands at the end of the set's list. No hook in any recipe class. `onRecipeLoad` catches and logs exceptions (`DBSRecipes.java:42-49`): a duplicate id throws in `GenericRecipes.register` after the recipe was appended to `recipeOrderedList` (`GenericRecipes.java:99-100`), so the duplicate stays in the ordered list (and NEI) and the rest of that branch is skipped. `tools/check-fork.sh` checks the wiring, the class names and that the restored recipe ids are defined only in `DBSRecipes` after merges; update those checks if the restored recipes move inline.

### Gotchas

- Everything registered outside `initialize()` is wiped by `deleteRecipes()` on init, `/ntmreload` and server sync; addons must use the listener.
- `GenericRecipes.register` appends to `recipeOrderedList` BEFORE the duplicate check; `writeTemplateFile` swallows exceptions (truncated templates possible).
- A typo in a recipe ingredient is not reported: an unknown item name in an `item` stack becomes `ModItems.nothing` (`ComparableStack(Item)` null substitution, `RecipesCommon.java:113-116`) and an unknown fluid name becomes `Fluids.NONE` (`Fluids.fromName`, `Fluids.java:1196-1203`). `readAStack`/`readFluidStack` log `Error reading stack array`/`Error reading fluid array` only on structural errors; `readItemStack` (used for outputs, and for the inputs of `ShredderRecipes`/`FuelPoolRecipes` and the `particle` input of `CyclotronRecipes`) does log an unknown item name before substituting `ModItems.nothing` (`SerializableRecipe.java:333-340`; `readItemStackChance` likewise, L343-356).
- Client recipe sync (`enableServerRecipeSync`; sent only by a dedicated server, `ModEventHandler.java:247`) runs `SerializableRecipe.initialize()` on the client main thread (`SerializableRecipePacket.java:65`; `FMLProxyPacket` is queued for `processReceivedPackets`, see area 16 Patterns), rebuilding every recipe set between client ticks. The reset on disconnect is different: `ModEventHandler.java:272` calls `SerializableRecipe.clearReceivedRecipes`, which re-runs `initialize()` when synced files were held, but FML posts `ClientDisconnectionFromServerEvent` from `NetworkDispatcher.disconnect`/`close`, Netty outbound operations that run on the channel's event-loop thread, so that rebuild runs off the main thread while client ticks and NEI may read the maps.
- `Fluids.readTraits` clears a fluid's traits first, then instantiates each listed trait; `FT_Rocket` fails (`InstantiationException` printed, trait lost). Foreign (`CompatFluidRegistry`) fluids are absent from `metaOrder` during trait read/write.
- Custom fluids from `hbmFluidTypes.json` are registered after the built-ins with their explicit ids (`readCustomFluids`, `Fluids.java:549`; `Fluids.register` overwrites, L1181-1185), while a built-in takes id = `idMapping.size()` (L1173-1178). A new built-in whose index equals an existing custom fluid's id is replaced in `idMapping`, and `Fluids.init` then throws at the MetaOrder size check (L887).
- `FluidContainerRegistry.clearRegistry()` (L27-30) does not undo the `OreDictionary.registerOre` calls of `registerContainer` (L115). Forge ignores a re-registration of the same item/meta under the same name (`OreDictionary.registerOreImpl`), so `/ntmreload` adds no duplicates, but container ore names that a reload no longer produces (a custom fluid removed or re-traited) stay registered until restart.
- `CraftingManager.mainRegistry()` (MainRegistry.java:294) runs before `OreDictManager.registerOres()` (L305) and `FluidContainerRegistry.register()` (L574). Ore-dict ingredients still resolve because Forge's `OreDictionary.getOres(String)` returns the live list, but code that tests `doesOreNameExist`/`getOres(...).isEmpty()` when it builds recipes (the `PressRecipes`/`AnvilRecipes` autogen) must run after `registerOres()`.
- `ComparableStack`-keyed HashMap lookups cannot find WILDCARD entries; use `makeSingular()` and retry with WILDCARD (`ShredderRecipes.getShredderResult`) or normalise to 0 (`ArcFurnaceRecipes.register`, which silently drops the whole recipe, including its unoccupied variants, if any variant of its input is already in `occupiedSolid`/`occupiedLiquid` for the output kind it produces; B-144).
- `RadiolysisRecipes.registerRadiolysis` throws if `CrackingRecipes` is empty. It runs only in PostLoad (MainRegistry.java:591): `/ntmreload` (`CommandReloadRecipes.java:33-42`: fluids, containers, recipe sets, item pools, damage resistance, logic-block actions/conditions/interactions) does not re-run it, so radiolysis keeps the startup cracking recipes; it also skips `CustomMachineConfigJSON` and anvil smithing. Owner's pack: EnviroMine injects at the HEAD of `registerRadiolysis()` and `@Shadow`s `private static Map radiolysis` (L21; required mixin config) to add five `RADIOACTIVE_*_WATER` -> `WATER` entries, so a `clear()` at the start of that method would erase them (B-365's fix therefore clears in the caller, the `CrackingRecipes.registerPost` override it adds, before that calls `registerRadiolysis`), and renaming or retyping the field or the method crashes at class load.
- Owner's pack: bobfluidtranslator registers a Forge fluid `<name>_fluid` plus a `bobfluidtranslator:<name>_fluid_block` block and item for every `FluidType` in `Fluids.getAll()` (skipping blacklisted and mapped types and names that already exist as Forge fluids), and those registry names persist in the world's id map (206 fluid blocks remapped in the latest log). Renaming or removing a fluid, or adding a fork fluid and removing it later, leaves missing mappings on world load, so `FluidType` names are save-relevant there. EnviroMine's 20 HBM fluid types (explicit ids 7732-7751) are not bridged, because EnviroMine registers same-named Forge fluids itself, but they occupy those ids.
- `CustomMachineConfigJSON.initialize()` runs before `SerializableRecipe.initialize()` in PostLoad; `registerAllHandlers()` is not idempotent.
- `SILEXRecipes` registers `ingot_cm_mix` twice; `ItemPoolsSingle` registers `POOL_BLUEPRINTS` twice; `MachineRecipes.java:19` TODO/@Spaghetti; `CrucibleRecipes.java:220` TODO buffer lookups; `SerializableRecipe.java:194` stale "currently unused" javadoc on `deleteRecipes`.

---

## 11. Containers, GUIs, NEI

### Purpose

`inventory/container/` (187 files), `inventory/gui/` (234 files incl. `element/`), `handler/nei/` (80 files), plus `NEIRegistry`, `NEIConfig`, `GUIHandler`. There is no GUI-ID table: one `IGuiHandler` (`GUIHandler`) resolves an `IGUIProvider` from the TE, then Block (13 blocks implement it directly), then held Item, then Entity with id == x; the int ID is passed through unchanged (0 by convention). NEI is a list of `TemplateRecipeHandler`s built once in `NEIRegistry.listAllHandlers()` and registered by `NEIConfig.loadConfig()` (found by NEI's classpath scan for `NEI*Config` implementing `IConfigureNEI`; the class name is load-bearing), plus a GTNH-NEI IMC path (`IMCHandlerNHNEI`).

### Key files

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `inventory/container/ContainerBase.java` | Preferred container base (29 direct subclasses incl. `ContainerCrateBase` + 8 crate containers): `public IInventory tile`, `canInteractWith` via `tile.isUseableByPlayer`, generic `transferStackInSlot` splitting at `tile.getSizeInventory()` (tile slots must be added first and completely), `playerInv`, `addSlots`, `addOutputSlots`, `addTakeOnlySlots`, `mergeItemStack` honouring `Slot.isItemValid` and, when merging into the tile, `tile.getInventoryStackLimit()` (L141-142). It does not honour per-slot `Slot.getSlotStackLimit()`, so an empty limit-1 `SlotPattern` in the default shift-click range would keep 1 item and delete the rest of the stack (L188-194). For such slots override `transferStackInSlot` (every current `ContainerBase` with a `SlotPattern` does) or use `InventoryUtil.mergeItemStack`, which honours `getSlotStackLimit` (`InventoryUtil.java:523,565`). |
| `container/ContainerNT.java`, `ICustomPayloadReceiver.java` | Dead alternative base (0 subclasses); `acceptData(Side, windowId, nbt)` for `ContainerNBTCommsPacket` (only `ContainerPneumoStorageAccess`). |
| `container/ContainerMachineArcWelder.java`, `ContainerMachineReactorBreeding.java`, `ContainerMachineChemicalPlant.java` | Raw-Container exemplar (147 concrete raw containers; `index <= 7` for 8 slots is correctly bounded), minimal raw exemplar (has an off-by-one: `index <= 2` for 2 tile slots), ContainerBase-style exemplar mixing `ContainerBase.mergeItemStack` and `InventoryUtil.mergeItemStack`. |
| `inventory/gui/GuiInfoContainer.java`, `GuiInfoContainerLayered.java`, `element/GUIElements.java` | Preferred GUI base (153 direct + 11 via `GUITurretBase` + 2 layered): `drawElectricityInfo`, `drawCustomInfoStat`, `drawInfoPanel` (types 0-11 from `gui_utility.png`), `getUpgradeInfo`, `checkClick`/`clickSendFlag` (`NBTControlPacket`), scissor helpers, NEI drag-and-drop into `SlotPattern` (requires the container to be a `ContainerBase`); layered GUIs (`SlotLayer` + `GuiLayerPacket`); hover text/gauge helpers. |
| `gui/GUIMachineReactorBreeding.java`, `GUIMachineArcWelder.java`, `GUIScreenRecipeSelector.java` | Minimal GUI (`public static ResourceLocation texture` for NEI), rich GUI (`FluidTank.renderTank`/`renderTankInfo`), recipe picker for GenericRecipes machines. |
| `inventory/SlotNonRetarded.java`, `SlotCraftingOutput.java`, `SlotTakeOnly.java`, `SlotUpgrade.java`, `SlotPattern.java`, `SlotLayer.java` (also `SlotDeprecated`, `SlotRocket`, `SlotSmelting`) | Slot types. `SlotNonRetarded` (created by `ContainerBase.playerInv` and `addSlots`; `addOutputSlots`/`addTakeOnlySlots` create `SlotCraftingOutput`/`SlotTakeOnly`) validates with `inventory.isItemValidForSlot(this.slotNumber, ...)` (`SlotNonRetarded.java:25`). That is the slot's position in the container, not its inventory index (`getSlotIndex()`), so tile slot k must be the k-th slot added. Player slots are unaffected only because `InventoryPlayer.isItemValidForSlot` always returns true. NEI drag-and-drop sends `slot.slotNumber` as the inventory index too (`GuiInfoContainer.java:365`). `SlotTakeOnly`/`SlotCraftingOutput` reject inserts, `SlotUpgrade` accepts any `ItemMachineUpgrade`, and `SlotPattern` accepts anything (limit 1 and `putStack` truncates to 1, unless `allowStackSize()`); none of them consult the TE. |
| `main/NEIRegistry.java`, `NEIConfig.java` | Ordered handlers (`BreederRecipeHandler` at L36; `OreSlopperHandler` before acidizing; `FluidRecipeHandler` last; `RTGRecipeHandler` if `VersatileConfig.rtgDecay()`); plugin (`registerHandler`, `AnvilOverlayHandler`, `CustomMachineHandler` per JSON machine via `registerHandlerBypass`, `API.hideItem`, `registerHighlightIdentifier` for plushies). |
| `handler/nei/NEIUniversalHandler.java`, `NEIGenericRecipeHandler.java`, `NEICelestialHandler.java`, `BreederRecipeHandler.java`, `FusionBreederHandler.java`, `BlastFurnaceHandler.java`, `CustomMachineHandler.java`, `AnvilOverlayHandler.java`, `AlloyFurnaceRecipeHandler.java` | Universal base (48 direct subclasses; all but `GrenadeRecipeHandler` pass HashMaps to the @Deprecated ctors, so ordering is non-deterministic; `InventoryUtil.extractObject` accepts ItemStack/ItemStack[]/[][]/AStack/AStack[]/Object[], no FluidStack), generic base (6), celestial variant (4; only item-usage lookup is a no-op), hand-rolled exemplar (fork-added; compares literal `"breeding"` in five places), smallest universal/generic exemplars, JSON-machine handler (no `ICompatNHNEI`, `gui_nei_custom.png`), anvil overlay, unregistered dead handler. |
| `handler/imc/ICompatNHNEI.java`, `IMCHandlerNHNEI.java` | GTNH NEI catalysts (hard-coded 166x65, 3 per page). |
| `packet/toserver/NBTControlPacket.java`, `interfaces/IControlReceiver.java`, `tileentity/IControlReceiverFilter.java` (also extends `ICopiable`; needs `nextMode`/`getFilterSlots`), `packet/GuiLayerPacket.java`, `packet/toclient/ContainerNBTCommsPacket.java` | Control plumbing. |

### Patterns

- Container/GUI naming `ContainerX`/`GUIX` (older `Gui*`); ctor `(InventoryPlayer, TileEntityX)`; GUI `super(new ContainerX(invPlayer, tile))`, `xSize`/`ySize`; textures `RefStrings.MODID + ":textures/gui/<category>/gui_<name>.png"` (`public static` when NEI needs it).
- Draw lifecycle: `drawScreen` -> super, tooltips (`renderTankInfo`, `drawElectricityInfo`, `drawCustomInfoStat`); `drawGuiContainerForegroundLayer` name (`0x404040`) + `container.inventory` at `ySize - 96 + 2`; `drawGuiContainerBackgroundLayer` glColor, bindTexture, background, bars, `drawInfoPanel`, `renderTank(guiLeft + x, guiTop + bottomY, zLevel, w, h)` (y = bottom edge; `renderTankInfo` y = top).
- Slot layout: tile slots 0..n-1, then 27 main, then 9 hotbar (`playerInv(invPlayer, 8, y)`, hotbar at y+58).
- GUIs read TE fields directly; those arrive via the TE's `networkPackNT`/`serialize`/`deserialize`, not the Container (only 6 containers override `detectAndSendChanges`; 9 files reference it). A new GUI needs the TE to serialize every field it draws.
- `drawInfoPanel(x, y, w, h, type)` draws an icon from `gui_utility.png`: 0/1 small (8x8) blue/green "i", 2/3 large (16x16) blue/green "i", 4/5 small red/yellow "!", 6/7 large red/yellow "!", 8/9 small blue/grey "*", 10/11 large blue/grey "*" (2, 8, 3 and 6 are the common ones); pair it with `drawCustomInfoStat` hover text on the same rect. It binds `gui_utility.png` (`GuiInfoContainer.java:106`) and leaves it bound, so rebind the GUI texture before drawing more of its sprites after the call.
- NEI layout (`NEIUniversalHandler`/`NEIGenericRecipeHandler`): `PositionedStack` coordinates are relative to the 166x65 recipe area; machine icon at (75, 31) (with a template: template (75, 10), machine (75, 38)); 18x18 slot frames come from texture (5, 87), drawn at `pos - 1`. The arrow is the (59, 87) 18x36 sprite drawn at (74, 14); for a pooled `GenericRecipe` (template shown) it is the (77, 87) 18x50 sprite drawn at (74, 7) (`NEIGenericRecipeHandler.java:317-321`). `NEIGenericRecipeHandler` adds `getMachineXOffset(recipe)` to the arrow, machine and template x. Subclasses do not pass slot positions; they are derived from the input/output count. `NEIUniversalHandler` uses the static `getInputCoords`/`getOutputCoords(count)`: fixed layouts for 1-9 inputs and 1-8 outputs, and a 4-wide grid beyond that. `NEIGenericRecipeHandler` uses the overridable `getInputSlotPositions`/`getOutputSlotPositions(count)` plus the `getInputXOffset`/`getOutputXOffset`/`getMachineXOffset` hooks (only `AssemblyMachineRecipeHandler` overrides the offsets).
- GUI IDs that are not plain 0: `TileEntityMachineRadarNT` uses 0 for a client-opened GuiScreen (from `MachineRadar`) and 1 for the container GUI, opened by `receiveControl` key `"gui1"` (L447). `TileEntityElectrolyser`: `MachineElectrolyser` passes -1, meaning the last selected GUI; 0 is fluid, 1 is metal. `TileEntityPneumoTube`: `PneumoTube`/`PneumoTubePaintableBlock` open with 0 for a compressor tube and 1 for an endpoint tube (a plain tube opens nothing; `PneumoTube.java:122,127`), which `provideGUI` reads only as the boolean `ID == 1` (L265). `BlockMachineBase.guiID` is 0 in all 8 subclasses (-1 = no GUI). 14 dummyables pass the clicked face (0-5) as the ID: the five PA parts (`BlockPADetector/Dipole/Quadrupole/RFC/Source`), `MachineAnnihilator`, `MachineCatalyticReformer`, `MachineCoker`, `MachineHydrotreater`, `MachineMilkReformer`, `MachineOreSlopper`, `MachineVacuumDistill`, `MachineBatteryREDD` and `MachineBatterySocket`. Their TEs ignore it; only the three TEs above branch on ID.
- NEI hand-rolled shape: inner `CachedRecipe`, four `load*` overloads guarded by `outputId.equals(getRecipeID()) && getClass() == X.class`, `getGuiTexture()` = GUI's `texture.toString()`, `getGuiClass()`, `loadTransferRects()`, `drawExtras`.

### How-to

- Container + GUI for a machine: `ContainerMachineFoo extends ContainerBase`. Add the tile slots first, in inventory-index order (see `SlotNonRetarded` above), then `playerInv`. Override `transferStackInSlot` if routing differs; `ContainerMachineChemicalPlant` is the ContainerBase exemplar. `GUIMachineFoo extends GuiInfoContainer`, using the lifecycle above but with `I18nUtil.resolveKey` where the older GUIs use `I18n.format` (fork rule; `GUIMachineChemicalPlant` already does). The TE implements `IGUIProvider`, with `@SideOnly(Side.CLIENT)` on `provideGUI` (+ `IControlReceiver` for buttons). The block opens with ID 0 through `standardOpenBehavior(..., 0)`, which calls `openGui` only on the server (`BlockDummyable.java:449-464`). Screen-only GUI: `provideContainer` returns null and `provideGUI` returns a `GuiScreen`. Here the block must call `FMLNetworkHandler.openGui` itself on the client (`if(world.isRemote)`, as `MachineRadar`/`RadioTorchBase` do), because FML's server path sends nothing when there is no container. GUI exemplar: `GUIMachineArcWelder.java` (its container is a raw `Container`).
- Hand-rolled NEI handler: `extends TemplateRecipeHandler implements ICompatNHNEI`; use `getRecipeID()` consistently; `handlers.add(new FooRecipeHandler())` in `NEIRegistry.listAllHandlers()` before `FluidRecipeHandler`. Exemplar `BreederRecipeHandler.java`.
- Universal handler: `super(ModBlocks.foo.getLocalizedName(), ModBlocks.foo, FooRecipes.getRecipes())` + `getKey()` (ids conventionally `ntmFoo`); prefer the `List<Pair<Object,Object>>` ctor. Exemplar `FusionBreederHandler.java`.
- Generic handler: `super(name, FooRecipesNT.INSTANCE, ModBlocks.foo)` + `getRecipeID()`. Exemplar `BlastFurnaceHandler.java`.
- GUI button: `mouseClicked` -> `checkClick(x, y, left, top, w, h)` -> `NBTControlPacket`, or `clickSendFlag(tile, x, y, left, top, w, h, "toggle")`.

### Gotchas

- GTNH-NEI init order: `MainRegistry.load` (L544-548) calls `proxy.handleNHNEICompat()` (ClientProxy only, and only when the NotEnoughItems version string contains `GTNH`, L545) -> `IMCHandlerNHNEI.IMCSender()` -> `NEIRegistry.listAllHandlers()`. Every handler is therefore constructed during init, before `SerializableRecipe.initialize()` (PostLoad, L585), and the memoised list is what `NEIConfig.loadConfig` registers later. Recipe display is not stale because of this. NEI uses registered handlers only as prototypes and builds a fresh instance for every lookup via `newInstance()` (1.0.3.74: `getClass().newInstance()`; GTNH 2.8: `getClass().getConstructor().newInstance()`). That re-runs the ctor, which re-reads `FooRecipes.getRecipes()`, and `NEIGenericRecipeHandler` reads `recipeSet.recipeOrderedList` at lookup time anyway. Only the IMC data (`getRecipeID()`, `getMachinesForRecipe()`) comes from the early instances. Consequences: a handler ctor must be public and no-arg, it runs once per handler per lookup (keep it cheap), and it must be safe before recipes load. A handler whose ctor takes arguments must override `newInstance()`, as `CustomMachineHandler` does. The owner's pack runs GTNH NEI 2.8.146, so this IMC path is live there (the log shows 74 `registerHandlerInfo` messages from hbm, exactly the `listAllHandlers()` set, and 118 added catalysts). GTNH NEI runs the lookups on its ForkJoin worker pool (`RecipeHandlerQuery.getRecipeHandlersParallel`; the instance's `config/NEI/serialhandlers.cfg` lists no hbm handler), so handler ctors and lookups run off the client thread and must not mutate shared statics (B-369).
- GTNH NEI 2.8.146 keying: IMC handler info is keyed by the `handler` class name, and a catalyst by its `handlerID` string, which must equal the lookup key `firstNonNull(getOverlayIdentifier(), getHandlerId())` (`getHandlerId()` defaults to the class name; `TemplateRecipeHandler.getOverlayIdentifier()` is null). NEI ignores the `handlerID` extra that `IMCHandlerNHNEI` adds to `registerHandlerInfo` (L37) and the `catalystHandlerID` extra (L52), so `getRecipeID()` has no effect through IMC; it still matters inside NTM code, where `NEIGenericRecipeHandler` uses it as the transfer-rect id and the "all recipes" id (L235, L261-262, L304). Consequence: catalysts sent under the class name of a handler that has an overlay id are never shown; `AnvilRecipeHandler` (overlay id `ntmAnvil`, also the `AnvilOverlayHandler` key at `NEIConfig.java:43`) shows none of its 12 anvil catalysts.
- IMC catalyst names are `"hbm:" + getUnlocalizedName()` (`IMCHandlerNHNEI.java:20,24`), valid only for NTM blocks/items registered under their unlocalized name. `GrenadeRecipeHandler` and `RBMKRodDisassemblyHandler` use `Blocks.crafting_table` and send `hbm:tile.workbench`, which is not a registry name (the table is `minecraft:crafting_table`); the owner's log shows `Cannot find item hbm:tile.workbench` twice per start (B-373). GTNH NEI 2.8.146 resolves item names as `modid:name[:meta]` (`NEIServerUtils.getModdedItem`).
- NEI drag-and-drop into a `SlotPattern` (`GuiInfoContainer.handleDragNDrop`) works only when the container is a `ContainerBase` whose `tile` is a TileEntity (cast at `GuiInfoContainer.java:371`). That TE must implement `IControlReceiver` and handle the `slot`/`stack` keys; `IControlReceiverFilter`'s default `receiveControl` does this, and every current filter TE uses it. It silently does nothing for the raw containers `ContainerMachineCustom` and `ItemRebarPlacer.ContainerRebar` (an item inventory with a `GuiInfoContainer` GUI). It also does nothing for `ContainerCartDestroyer`, whose `GUICartDestroyer` is a plain `GuiContainer`, so the handler never runs.
- Classic NEI 1.0.3.74 allows one handler per class; GTNH NEI 2.8.146 one per `getHandlerId()` (default: the class name). Extra instances need `registerHandlerBypass` (or, on GTNH only, a distinct `getHandlerId()`) and a `newInstance()` override (as `CustomMachineHandler`). The owner's instance defines one custom machine (the `paperPress` demo in `hbmCustomMachines.json`), so its bypass-registered handler gets no GTNH handler info or catalysts there (B-154).
- `GUIHandler.getGUIProvider` (L29-43) has no ID namespace. Item GUIs open at (0, 0, 0), so an `IGUIProvider` TE or block at the world origin takes them over; entity GUIs pass the entity id as x with y = z = 0, so a held `IGUIProvider` item takes over the entity GUI (the item check runs first).
- `ContainerOrbitalStationComputer`/`ContainerRadiobox` do not override `transferStackInSlot` but have no slots (safe until slots are added).
- `GUIMachineReactorBreeding` comments on "dud" TEs after block-state swaps (client GUI keeps an invalidated TE).
- NEI is a hard compile dependency (`build.gradle` `implementation`), tolerated at runtime through `@Optional` in `GuiInfoContainer`.
- Smells: `ContainerMachineCustom.java:77` TODO Mojang; `GUIMachineDiFurnaceRTG.java:36` and `PressRecipeHandler.java:29` @Untested; `GUIPneumoStorageAccess.java:97` and `GUIScreenRadioTorchLogic.java:99` TODO localization; `VacuumCircuitHandler`/`SolderingStationHandler:42` TODO output-only matching; `OilExtractionHandler:38,79` hard-coded; hard-coded English in several GUIs/handlers; 169 `inventory/gui` files call `I18n.format("container.inventory")` (170 with `GUIFurnaceBrick`'s `new Object[0]` form) against the fork's `I18nUtil` rule; only `GUIMachineChemicalPlant` (L67) uses `I18nUtil.resolveKey("container.inventory")`.

## 12. Entities, mobs, explosions

### Purpose

`com/hbm/entity/` (top-level, mob/, effect/, item/, logic/, cart/, train/, particle/, pathfinder/) and `com/hbm/explosion/`. Registration in `EntityMappings.writeMappings()` via `ModEntityList`; renderers in `ClientProxy`. Explosions: deprecated vanilla-subclass `ExplosionNT` (+ `ExplosionNukeSmall` mini-nukes), the composable `ExplosionVNT` pipeline (`vanillant/`), and progressive nuke drivers (`EntityNukeExplosionMK5` + `IExplosionRay`, `EntityNukeExplosionMK3` + spiral column algorithms, `EntityBalefire`, `EntityTomBlast`); only MK5 (unless `statFacNoRad`) spawns `EntityFalloutRain` in practice (MK3 only in its unused waste mode). Space adds celestial fauna, `CBT_Invasion` siege waves and atmosphere-aware `EntityNukeTorex`.
