### Patterns

- Packet class shape: fields, a public no-arg ctor, `fromBytes`/`toBytes`, and `public static class Handler implements IMessageHandler<X, IMessage>` returning null. In 1.7.10 both decoding and handlers run on the main thread: vanilla `NetworkManager` queues the non-priority `FMLProxyPacket`, and `processReceivedPackets` feeds it to the embedded channel. World access in a handler is therefore safe, and no scheduling is needed (unlike 1.8+). Client handlers: `@SideOnly(Side.CLIENT)` and null-check `theWorld`. Several existing handlers deviate and are not exemplars for this: `BufPacket`/`EntityBufPacket`/`AuxParticlePacketNT` lack @SideOnly, and `TESiren`/`TEVault`/`TEFF`/`TEMissileMultipart`/`MuzzleFlash` skip the null check. Server handlers use `ctx.getServerHandler().playerEntity` and must validate every client value (index bounds, distance, open container).
- Threaded tiers: plain `IMessage` (serialized where written), `ThreadedPacket` (lazy compile on the worker; immutable data only), `PrecompiledPacket` (compiled on the main thread by `preparePacket`; still recompiled once more on the worker after the send, because the codec's `writeBytes(compiledBuffer)` consumes the buffer (NetworkHandler.java:60) and `getCompiledBuffer()` recompiles an empty one (ThreadedPacket.java:26-30) inside the `getCompiledBuffer().release()` call (PacketThreading.java:97/123); B-100).
- Per-tick barrier: `PacketThreading.waitUntilThreadFinished()` then `NetworkHandler.flush()` at `ServerTickEvent` END (ModEventHandler L1573-1579). Despite NetworkHandler's class comment (L31), packets are NOT batched. The embedded channel's `FMLOutboundHandler` hands each encoded packet straight to `NetworkDispatcher.sendProxy` -> `NetworkManager.scheduleOutboundPacket` (`writeAndFlush`), so a packet leaves when it is written: on the main thread, or on the worker for threaded packets. `flush()` is effectively a no-op. The wait is the only end-of-tick guarantee, and it guarantees only that queued threaded packets have been written.
- TE sync / control / container payload / particle / HUD message: see areas 5, 7, 15; container payloads via `ICustomPayloadReceiver.acceptData(side, windowId, nbt)` + `ContainerNBTCommsPacket` (registered on both sides).
- wiaj pipeline: `Jars.initJars()` (ClientProxy) -> tooltip hint `cannery.f1` -> Shift+`HbmKeybinds.qmaw` opens `GuiWorldInAJar(cannery.createScript(), name, icon, seeAlso)`; `JarScript.run()` -> actors `updateActor` -> `JarScene.tick()` -> `IJarAction.act()`; camera state lives on the script.

### How-to

- New packet: class in `packet/toclient/` or `packet/toserver/` implementing `IMessage`. A packet passed to `PacketThreading.createAllAroundThreadedPacket`/`createSendToThreadedPacket` (the only two threaded send helpers) MUST extend `ThreadedPacket` (immutable data; serialized on the worker) or `PrecompiledPacket` (mutable server state; serialized on the main thread); any other `IMessage` is logged as 'Invalid packet class' and never sent (PacketThreading.java:74-77). Public no-arg ctor; `fromBytes`/`toBytes` in matching order (`BufferUtil` helpers); nested `public static class Handler implements IMessageHandler<X, IMessage>` returning null and releasing stored ByteBufs in `finally`. Give every packet its own `Handler` class: the handler's class name is its Netty pipeline name (NetworkHandler.java:121), and a duplicate on one side throws. APPEND `wrapper.registerMessage(X.Handler.class, X.class, i++, Side.CLIENT|SERVER);` at the END of `PacketDispatcher.registerPackets()` (discriminators are positional; an unregistered packet is silently sent as discriminator 0). Prefer the generic paths first: TE state via `serialize`/`deserialize` + `networkPackNT`, GUI input via `IControlReceiver` + `NBTControlPacket`, particles via `IParticleCreator`. Exemplar `packet/toclient/ExplosionKnockbackPacket.java`.
- TE sync: area 5 (`serialize`/`deserialize` + `networkPackNT(range)`). Exemplar `tileentity/machine/TileEntityMachineRadarScreen.java`.
- GUI control: the TE `implements IControlReceiver`. Implement `hasPermission(player)`, which is the ONLY server-side validation (the packet carries client-supplied coordinates), so check distance there (Diesel: `getDistance(...) < 25`). Implement the abstract `receiveControl(NBTTagCompound)`. Override the default `receiveControl(EntityPlayer, NBTTagCompound)` only when you need the player, and then leave the one-arg version empty: the handler calls both, two-arg first (NBTControlPacket.java:86-87). Validate every value read from the NBT. The GUI sends `PacketDispatcher.wrapper.sendToServer(new NBTControlPacket(nbt, x, y, z))` with the core TE's coordinates. Exemplar `tileentity/machine/TileEntityMachineDiesel.java`.
- Item control (GUI opened from a held item): item `implements IItemControlReceiver` (`receiveControl(player, stack, data)`); the GUI sends `new NBTItemControlPacket(data)` and the handler applies it to the sender's held stack without any other check (NBTItemControlPacket.java:64-69), so validate in `receiveControl`. Exemplars `items/tool/ItemRTTYPager.java`, `inventory/gui/GUIScreenFluid.java`.
- HUD message: `ChatBuilder` text + `ServerProxy.ID_*` slot + `PlayerInformPacket(component, id, millis)` via `wrapper.sendTo`. Exemplar `util/ArmorUtil.java`.
- Container payload: the container implements `ICustomPayloadReceiver.acceptData(side, windowId, nbt)`. It can be a `ContainerBase` subclass for tile GUIs (tile slots first and completely, then `playerInv`; `canInteractWith` delegates to `tile.isUseableByPlayer`, 128 squared distance) or a plain `Container`, like the exemplar. `acceptData` must return early when `windowId != this.windowId`, because the shared handler hands the packet to whatever `player.openContainer` is. On the server it must also validate the client-supplied data. Send `new ContainerNBTCommsPacket(this.windowId, nbt)` with `sendToServer`, or `(playerMP.currentWindowId, nbt)` with `sendTo`. The packet is registered on both sides; outbound uses discriminator 28. `detectAndSendChanges` is rarely overridden (6 overrides): GUI state normally arrives through the TE sync. Exemplar and only implementor: `inventory/container/ContainerPneumoStorageAccess.java` (extends `Container`).
- PermaSync field: insert it at the SAME position in `PermaSyncHandler.writePacket` and `readPacket`. Never append it after the trailing CBT_War projectile loop (write L162-170, read L291-302). That tail has no count, and the reader sizes it from the client's own CBT_War copy, which is refreshed only in the every-5-ticks CBT block, so anything after it misaligns whenever the server's projectile list has changed. Put it before the CBT block (write L77, read L197): the CBT catch returns early (L247) and skips everything after it. Use a leading boolean for optional data and keep it small (one stream per player per tick). A mismatch fails silently because `PermaSyncPacket.Handler` swallows every exception (PermaSyncPacket.java:47). Exemplar `packet/PermaSyncHandler.java`.
- New cannery: `CanneryXxx extends CanneryBase` (`getIcon`, `getName` -> `cannery.xxx`, `createScript()` building `WorldInAJar`, `JarScript`, `JarScene`s with `ActionSetZoom` first, `ActionSetBlock`/`ActionWait`, `ActionCreateActor(id, new ActorTileEntity(new RenderXxx(), nbt))`, `ActionUpdateActor`, `ActorFancyPanel(font, x, y, new Object[][]{{I18nUtil.resolveKey("cannery.xxx.0")}}, 250).setColors(colorCopper).setOrientation(Orientation.BOTTOM)`, `ActionRotateBy`/`ActionOffsetBy`); `Dummies.JarDummyConnector` tiles so cables render; reset mutable actor values with `ActionUpdateActor` at scene start (rewind reuses NBT instances: `ActionCreateActor.act` puts the same actor object back, ActionCreateActor.java:24; see CanneryStirling L77-85); `canneries.put(new ComparableStack(ModBlocks.xxx), new CanneryXxx())` in `Jars.initJars()`; lang keys. Exemplar `wiaj/cannery/CanneryStirling.java`.

### Gotchas

- Never insert a `registerMessage` line mid-list; `ContainerNBTCommsPacket` is registered twice (27/28) and outbound uses 28.
- `ThreadedPacket` instances must not be reused on the threaded path (released buffer -> `IllegalReferenceCountException`).
- `PacketThreading.init()` only via `/ntmpackets`; validation inverted; single worker with unbounded queue.
- `PermaSyncPacket` is one contiguous stream; a write/read mismatch desyncs everything after it.
- `I18nUtil` server sentinel; `EnumUtil.grabEnumSafely` silently remaps bad ordinals. Nine client handlers catch `Exception` and drop it without logging: `HbmAnimationPacket` (L88), `PlayerInformPacket` (L87), `PermaSyncPacket` (L47, so any PermaSync misread or underflow is invisible), `HeldItemNBTPacket` (L64), `SerializableRecipePacket` (L71; its server-side `SerializableRecipePacket(File)` constructor also has an empty `IOException` catch, L29), `ParticleBurstPacket` (L57), `TransporterLinkerPacket` (L88), `TEVaultPacket` (L72), `TEFFPacket` (L92). `BufPacket`/`EntityBufPacket` log a warning instead, and the PermaSync CBT catch logs via `logger.catching`.
- `AnvilCraftPacket` sends an index into `AnvilRecipes.getConstruction()` (L23/L53), so the client and server lists must be in the same order. Server recipe JSONs reach clients only on a dedicated server with `GeneralConfig.enableServerRecipeSync` (default false; ModEventHandler L247-265); with a server-only anvil JSON the server crafts its own recipe at the clicked index, which can differ from the one the player clicked (tier and input checks at L55/L62 still apply).
- `ArmorUtil` static initializer throws `AssertionError` when Fisk's Superheroes is present but not reflectable.
- `BiomeSyncPacket.Handler`'s EndlessIDs branch (L106-115) copies only 255 of the 256 biome entries (`i < 255`, L112) and calls `markBlockRangeForRenderUpdate` inside the loop (L114). The (x=15, z=15) column of every fully synced chunk therefore keeps its old biome on the client until the chunk is resent (grass, foliage and water colour, F3 biome), and each packet queues 255 identical render updates; server data is correct. The owner's pack (EndlessIDs, crater biomes on) hits it on every fallout biome change.
- Owner's pack: hodgepodge raises the server-to-client custom-payload (S3F) limit to 256 MiB, so B-408's 1048577-2097050-byte failure band does not happen there; the zero padding and the client-to-server C17 32767-byte failure remain, and B-275 is unchanged (hodgepodge's codec fix does not reach NTM's codec). hodgepodge also processes received packets within a 5 ms time budget instead of vanilla's 1001-packet cap.
- wiaj: `JarScript.ffwTarget`/`freeRun` are static (one fast-forward at a time; harmless, since `ffw()` sets and clears `freeRun` inside one synchronous client-thread call and nothing outside `JarScript` reads either field, L126-148). `ActorFancyPanel` creates a `RenderItem` and fetches the `TextureManager` in field initializers (L30-31), and canneries read `Minecraft.getMinecraft().fontRenderer` inside `createScript()` (e.g. CanneryStirling L89), so wiaj scripts and panels may only be built on the client. `ActorBasicPanel` touches client classes only while drawing, and nothing uses it (its only reference is commented out). The `GuiWorldInAJar` ctor carries a large commented-out test script.
- Smells: `PermaSyncHandler.boykissers` / `/// SHITTY MEMES ///`; `AuxButtonPacket` still constructed in 19 files; `CompatEnergyControl` deprecated key constants; `EntityDamageUtil` deprecated overloads; `ActorFancyPanel.java:340` TODO scaled stacks; `Calculator.java:167` TODO BigDecimal; `ModEventHandler.java:1563-1572` comment documents the packet-thread race and its fix.

## 17. Resources, localization, build, tooling

### Purpose

Everything outside Java that a change must touch: the Gradle build (`build.gradle`, `gradle.properties`, wrapper 4.4.1, ForgeGradle 1.2 anatawa12, JDK 8), the access transformer, and `src/main/resources/assets/hbm/`: 10 `.lang` files (`en_US` 7377 lines / 7199 unique keys / 23 duplicates), 194 QMAW manual pages, 130 NBT structures, 588 model files, ~6.9k textures, 591 OGG sounds (594 files under `sounds/`, counting a stray `.mp3`, `.wav` and `desktop.ini`) + `sounds.json`, GLSL shaders, one OC floppy. `tools/` holds Blender add-ons for the animation JSON and the fork's `check-fork.sh` post-merge check (the index is all LF since `27811a59`; `.gitattributes` pins 17 text extensions plus `gradlew` to LF and `*.bat` to CRLF, and its leading `* text=auto eol=lf` catch-all (2026-09-26) makes extension-less or odd text files such as `changelog`, `LICENSE*`, `.gitignore`, `.editorconfig`, `curseforge.properties.example`, `models/doors/seal.dae` and `models/weapons/tom_flame.hmf` LF too).

### Key files

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `build.gradle` | ForgeGradle plugin (dynamic `1.2-1.0.+`), `minecraft { version = "1.7.10-10.13.4.1614-1.7.10"; runDir = "eclipse" }`, Java 1.8, UTF-8; version `version_name = mod_version + "_X" + mod_build_number + "_H261"` (just `mod_version` when the build number is empty, i.e. a release), then the fork suffix `"_DBS" + REVISION`, parsed by regex from `com/hbm/dbs/DBSVersion.java` (fork line, `// DBS fix B-008`), and `project.version = "[" + version_name + "]"` (bracketed jar name `HBM-NTM-[1.0.27_X5778_H261_DBS1].jar`; unbracketed when the build number is empty); `mcmod.info` gets `version_name`; repos `maven.ntmr.dev/proxy`, `modmaven.dev`, `gregtech.mechaenetia.com`, `jitpack.io`, `cursemaven.com`; deps CodeChickenCore/Lib/NEI (dev `implementation` + src `compileOnly`, `transitive = false`), InventoryTweaks, OpenComputers API (`com.github.MightyPirates:OpenComputers:1.7.10-forge~1.8.9:api`), AE2 GTNH; `processResources` expands `${version}`/`${credits}` in `mcmod.info` only; `jar`/`sourceJar`/`devJar` with `FMLAT: HBM_at.cfg` (`devJar dependsOn reobf` hack); conditional `curse {}` (task `curse`; rotates `changelog` -> `changelog.bak`) and `publishing {}` (`maven.properties`, repo "Nuggies" at `https://maven.ntmr.dev/releases`). |

### Patterns

- Version: `V T (X)` = next release, build type, days since 2010-10-10; CI seds both `RefStrings.VERSION` and `mod_build_number`; local releases bump both by hand. The `_H261` suffix is NTM: Space's fork identifier (added by George Paton in `47614cbc`, 2024-09-19, "add space fork identifier to version"; the number itself is unexplained). DBS adds its own `_DBS<REVISION>` suffix from `com/hbm/dbs/DBSVersion.java` (area 1, update check) and leaves `RefStrings.VERSION` at upstream's value, so CI and JameH2 merges never touch the fork's identity.
- Lang namespaces (en_US unique keys): item 3426, tile 1589, hbmfluid 266, container 221, desc 182, achievement 135, hbmmat 134, gun 126, book_lore 108, cannery 94, book 92, death 77, trait 52, gui 52, entity 45, body 32, armor 30, and smaller. `$` = line break (consumed by `resolveKeyArray`/`autoBreakWithParagraphs`; a literal `$` cannot be shown through them), `§` colour codes; `%s` args (vanilla rewrites `%d`/`%.Nf` in lang values to `%s` at load, so width and precision are lost; format numbers in code); `%%` for a literal `%` only in keys resolved through a formatting call (`I18nUtil`/`I18n.format`, `translateToLocalFormatted`, `ChatComponentTranslation`); `.name` keys shown via `StatCollector.translateToLocal` (`Item`/`ItemBlockBase.getItemStackDisplayName`) are not formatted, so `%%` there displays verbatim; `#` comments.
- Lang key families: `item.<unloc>.name` and `item.<unloc>.<enum_lower>.name` (`ItemEnumMulti`), `item.<unloc>.desc` (`ItemCustomLore`, `$` line break, `.desc.P11` variant), `tile.<name>.name`/`.desc` and `tile.<name>.<enum_lower>.name` (`BlockEnumMulti`), `container.<name>`, `hbmfluid.<name>`, `hbmmat.<name>`, `hbmpseudofluid.<name>`, `entity.hbm.<name>.name`, `hbm.key.<name>`, `potion.hbm_<name>`, `itemGroup.tab<Name>`, `achievement.<k>`, `cannery.<name>[.N]`, `trait.<name>`, `desc.item.<name>`, `gun.<name>`, `book_lore.<name>`, `death.<name>`, `gui.<name>`, `body.<name>`, `armor.<name>`, `commands.<cmd>.<msg>`, `bomb.<code>`, `tool.ability.<name>`.
- Texture naming: items `setTextureName(RefStrings.MODID + ":x")` -> `textures/items/x.png`; blocks `setBlockTextureName` -> `textures/blocks/x.png`; models under `textures/models/<category>/` mirroring `models/<category>/`; GUIs `textures/gui/<category>/gui_<name>.png`.
- Model registration: `HFRWavefrontObject(...).asVBO()` for new models; `AdvancedModelLoader.loadModel` is legacy (and the only way to load `.hmf`); Collada and JSON animations via `ColladaLoader.load`/`AnimationLoader.load`.
- Sound registration is data-only (`<group>.<camelName>` -> `sounds/<group>/<file>.ogg`; categories player/block/record/hostile/ambient/neutral/music; `stream` for long loops).
- Structures: `public static final NBTStructure x = new NBTStructure(new ResourceLocation(RefStrings.MODID, "structures/<sub>/<file>.nbt"))`.
- Line endings: the index is all LF since `27811a59` (`.gitattributes` catch-all plus 17 text extensions and `gradlew`, see Purpose; upstream lang files arrive CRLF and are normalised on commit). A working tree checked out with `core.autocrlf=true` before the attributes existed keeps CRLF copies until they are re-checked-out (`git ls-files --eol` shows `i/lf w/crlf`). The owner's clone had 4810 such files on 2026-09-25; it was refreshed to LF and set to `core.autocrlf=false` on 2026-09-26 (only `*.bat` is CRLF on disk now). Another clone can be refreshed the same way, on a clean tree with nothing uncommitted: `git rm -r --cached -q . && git reset --hard`.

### How-to

- Localized name/tooltip: see CLAUDE.md; per-variant item names via `getUnlocalizedName(ItemStack)` (`ItemStampBook` L38-41); per-meta block names via `new BlockEnumMulti(mat, Enum.class, true /*multiName*/, multiTexture)` (keys `tile.<name>.<enum_lower>.name`; with `false`, as on `laythe_coral_block`, every meta gets the plain name) or an `IBlockMulti` that overrides `getUnlocalizedName(ItemStack)` (the default returns the plain block name). Either works only through `ItemBlockBase`, i.e. `register(x)` or `register(x, <ItemBlockBase subclass>.class)` in `ModBlocks`.
- QMAW page: `manual/<category>/<slug>.json` copying `manual/machine/assembler.json`; include `"trigger": []` when there are no triggers; content per STYLEGUIDE; dev run picks it up on F3+T (watch for `[QMAW] Error reading manual`).
- NBT structure: build it in-world, mark two corners with the `wand_s` item (it places a `wand_structure` block below the lower corner), name and save it from that block's GUI (`TileEntityWandStructure.saveStructure`, `BlockWandStructure.java:190` -> `NBTStructure.quickSaveArea`, written to `<mcDataDir>/structures/<name>.nbt`, i.e. `eclipse/structures/` in dev; uses `Minecraft.getMinecraft()`, so client/singleplayer only), copy the file to `src/main/resources/assets/hbm/structures/<sub>/`, add the `StructureManager` static, check the log for `NBT Structure not found`, wire into worldgen (area 14).
- Sound: OGG under `sounds/<group>/`, `sounds.json` entry, play with `"hbm:<group>.<event>"`.
- OBJ model: export triangulated, with normals, to `models/<category>/<name>.obj`; texture `textures/models/<category>/<name>.png`; `ResourceManager` static `new HFRWavefrontObject(new ResourceLocation(RefStrings.MODID, "models/<category>/<name>.obj")).asVBO()` (`.asVBO()` runs during static init and assumes 3 vertices with a normal each per face, so quads or faces without `vn` crash the client; see area 15). Do not create new `.hmf`.
- Weapon animation JSON: see area 15.
- OC floppy: `disks/<sanitized>/...` + `disks.put("Name", new FloppyDisk("Name", OCColors.X.ordinal()))` in `CompatHandler.init()` (the `FloppyDisk` constructor is package-private, `CompatHandler.java:99`) + recipe after the `oc:floppy` check (item exists only after `registerFloppy`; the recipe line dereferences `disk.item` even when loading failed).
- Access transformer: append `public net.minecraft.pkg.Class field_x # mcpName` for a field or `public net.minecraft.pkg.Class func_x(Largs;)Lret; # mcpName` for a method (SRG name plus JVM descriptor; `*` = all fields, `*()` = all methods), then `./gradlew clean setupDecompWorkspace` and refresh the IDE project.
- Version bump: `mod_build_number=<days>` in `gradle.properties` and `VERSION = "1.0.27 BETA (<days>)"` in `RefStrings`; for a new release also change `mod_version` and the hard-coded `1.0.27 BETA` in the sed line of `.github/workflows/build.yml` (otherwise CI builds re-stamp the old version); `./gradlew build` (JDK 8). A fork build that should supersede older DBS jars bumps `REVISION` in `com/hbm/dbs/DBSVersion.java` instead (area 1, update check). Publish: `curseforge.properties` from the example, notes in `changelog` (`## Changed`/`## Fixed`), `./gradlew curse`; maven: `maven.properties` (`username`/`password`), `./gradlew publish`.
- Compile-time mod dependency: `compileOnly("group:Artifact:version:<dev|api|deobf>") { transitive = false }` (prefer a deobfuscated artifact, since FG 1.2 has no `deobfCompile`; add a repository only if not already listed); guard usage with `Loader.isModLoaded`/`@Optional`; refresh the IDE project (`./gradlew eclipse` or a Gradle re-import). `setupDecompWorkspace` only rebuilds decompiled Minecraft and is not needed. `runClient`/`runServer` use `runtimeClasspath`, which excludes `compileOnly` (InventoryTweaks, OC and AE2 are absent from the dev run); to test with the mod, put its jar in `eclipse/mods/` (CodeChickenCore's dev-time deobfuscation handles release jars) or add a `runtimeOnly` dev artifact. The owner runtime-tests the built jar in their own game instead (a MultiMC instance with the mod pack, played solo; no `eclipse/` dir exists yet).

### Gotchas

- The Gradle project version is bracketed (`[1.0.27_X5778_H261_DBS1]`); the maven publication and `mcmod.info` use the unbracketed `version_name`. The `_DBS` regex in `build.gradle` (`[0][1]` on the match) fails the Gradle configuration if `DBSVersion.java` no longer contains `String REVISION = "..."`.
- Owner's pack: hodgepodge `hideTextureErrors=true` replaces FML's per-icon missing-texture report with a one-line summary (`497 missing textures ...`), so missing `hbm:` block and item icons (stitched into the atlas) cannot be audited from the owner's logs; launch once with it off and grep the TEXTURE ERRORS block for `hbm`. Textures bound through `TextureManager` (GUI images, model textures such as B-257's `ResourceManager` paths) still log `Failed to load texture` in `latest.log`.
- ForgeGradle 1.2 + Gradle 4.4.1 need JDK 8; the plugin coordinate is dynamic (`build.gradle:15`, `changing = true`), so builds are not reproducible over time. The owner's Gradle cache resolves it to `1.2-1.0.12`; pinning that version and dropping `changing = true` would make it reproducible.
- `en_US.lang` has 23 duplicate keys (last wins; e.g. `hbmfluid.blood`, `item.powder_zinc.name`, `commands.station.*`); translations carry stale keys never flagged.
- `QMAWLoader.registerJson` NPEs on a page without `trigger` (caught, page skipped); a page with empty `content` strings still registers. A page with `"content": {}` is not registered (`QMAWLoader.java:224`), but its triggers are already stored (L216), so the trigger hotkey opens a page that is in no index and shows "Missing Localization!".
- `processResources` only filters `mcmod.info`; `credits` comes verbatim from `gradle.properties`, which is UTF-8 on disk but read by Gradle 4.4.1 as ISO-8859-1. L19 already contains a literal U+FFFD (bytes EF BF BD) in place of the 'æ' of 'Vær', so it shows as mojibake and the letter is lost. Fix it by writing `V\\u00e6r` (two backslashes, so `Properties.load` leaves the JSON escape `\u00e6` for Gson to decode from `mcmod.info`), never a raw UTF-8 'æ'. L26 has a doubled paren, L44 and L73 lack commas, L87 ends in a trailing comma, and `mikkerlo` appears at L71 and L82 (B-287, D4).
- `HmfModelLoader` is @Deprecated but registered; `StructureManager.excavator` points at a missing file; `models/weapons/.obj` is unparseable.
- Smells: `build.gradle` L53 codechicken eclipse hack and L166 reobf hack; `build.gradle:126` declares `inputs.property "mcversion"` although `mcmod.info` hard-codes `1.7.10` and the `expand` map has no `mcversion`; `CompatHandler.java:192` creates its own `LogManager.getLogger("HBM")` instead of using `MainRegistry.logger`; three hand-maintained Blender scripts; `en_US.lang:373-404` commented-out `#book.rbmk.*` block.

### Open questions

- Whether the remaining unreferenced `sounds.json` keys (those not built at runtime, see Key files) and the 35 unreferenced models (B-299) are dead; purpose of `my_hecking_realism.png`/`ABC123.png`; whether `soundCategory.ntmMachines` is planned; whether `maven.ntmr.dev` credentials exist for this fork.
- Owner decisions: whether the upstream `curse {}`/`publishing {}` blocks (`build.gradle:185-244`; display name "Hbm's Nuclear Tech Mod ...", repo "Nuggies" at `maven.ntmr.dev`) stay, are retargeted or are removed; whether `manual/concepts/fluidhandling.json` is deleted or finished.

## 18. OpenComputers integration

### Purpose

~64 tile entities expose OC components through one contract, `CompatHandler.OCComponent` (extends OC `SimpleComponent`, `SidedComponent`, `ManagedPeripheral`; `@Optional.InterfaceList` + `@SimpleComponent.SkipInjection`), each machine adding `@Callback`-annotated `Object[] name(Context, Arguments)` methods, with `TileEntityProxyCombo` ports forwarding calls to the multiblock core. `CompatHandler.init()` (PostLoad, `MainRegistry` L615) registers read-only floppies from `assets/hbm/disks/` and their recipes; `BlockOpenComputersCablePaintable` is a colour-matched OC cable. OC's API is a `compileOnly` dependency; everything is soft-gated with `@Optional` and `Loader.isModLoaded("OpenComputers")`. HBM uses only `li.cil.oc.api.*` (no `Machine`/`Architecture`/`Driver`), so OC-LuaJIT (a replacement Lua VM behind OC's unchanged `Machine`) inherits OC's component marshalling untouched.

### Component registry (name -> class)

`ntm_null` default; `ntm_launch_pad` LaunchPadBase; `ntm_rocket_pad` LaunchPadRocket; `ntm_custom_launch_pad` LaunchTable; `reactor_control`, `research_reactor`, `breeding_reactor`, `zirnox_reactor`, `watz_reactor`, `ntm_icf_reactor`, `ntm_pwr_control`; `dfc_emitter/receiver/stabilizer/injector` Core*; `ntm_geiger`; `microwave`; `ntm_radar`; `ntm_stardar`; `ntm_atmospheric_vent` AirPump; `ntm_combustion_engine`; `ntm_gas_turbine`; `ntm_turbine` (MachineTurbine, LargeTurbine, IndustrialTurbine (different method set), Chungus); `ntm_coker`; `ntm_pa_dipole/quad/rfc/detector/source`; `ntm_fusion_breeder/boiler/klystron/torus/mhdt`; `ntm_fluid_tank` (FluidTank, Barrel); `ntm_energy_storage` (BatteryBase, REDD, Socket with differing `getEnergyInfo`); `ntm_energy_storage_legacy` MachineBattery; `rbmk_console/crane/lever/terminal/keypad/gauge/graph/indicator/numitron/fuel_rod/control_rod/boiler/heater/cooler/outgasser`; `ntm_turret`; `ntm_artillery`; `ntm_fluid_counter_valve`; `ntm_telex`; `radio_torch`; `capacitor`; `ntm_fluid_pump`; `ntm_power_gauge`; `ntm_fluid_gauge`.

### Patterns

- Class shape: `@Optional.InterfaceList({@Optional.Interface(iface = "li.cil.oc.api.network.SimpleComponent", modid = "OpenComputers")}) class X ... implements SimpleComponent, CompatHandler.OCComponent`. The direct `SimpleComponent` is REQUIRED; inheriting it via `OCComponent` does not trigger injection. MightyPirates OC injects the node/Environment only when the class's own interface list names it. GTNH OC, which the owner's pack runs (1.12.62) and OC-LuaJIT targets, injects when gtnhlib's `ClassConstantPoolParser` finds a `CONSTANT_Utf8` exactly equal (by length and bytes) to `li/cil/oc/api/network/SimpleComponent` (`common/asm/ClassTransformer.java:71` in the 1.12.55 sources, bytecode offsets 185-197 in 1.12.62); descriptors (`L...;`) and dotted annotation strings do not match. So under GTNH a `SimpleComponent` cast, `instanceof` or class literal in any non-TE class would also trigger it (HBM has none today), and in a subclass of an injected TE it injects twice (see Gotchas). The owner's log shows 62 injected HBM classes, including all seven lowercase-modid classes (`TileEntityProxyCombo` among them), and no injection failure. `OCComponent` carries `@SimpleComponent.SkipInjection` because it names `SimpleComponent` itself but is not a tile entity. Without it, injection throws, `hadSimpleComponentErrors` is set, and (GTNH `EventHandler.scala:203`) every player gets a warning chat message on login.
- Callback shape: `@Callback(direct = true[, limit = N][, doc = "..."]) @Optional.Method(modid = "OpenComputers") public Object[] name(Context context, Arguments args)`. Counts (382 total): 275 plain `direct = true`, 13 `direct = true, doc = ...`, 35 `limit = 4` (7 of them with `doc`), 38 `limit = 2`, 1 `limit = 3`, 1 `limit = 1`, 17 bare `@Callback` (non-direct), 1 getter, 1 setter. `Context` is never used. Arguments via `args.checkInteger` (89 calls on 88 lines), `checkString` (30), `checkBoolean` (28), `checkDouble` (23 calls on 15 lines), `checkTable` (1), `checkAny` (1), `optInteger` (1).
- Dispatch semantics (OC `Callbacks.scala`; the same structure in the 1.12.62 bytecode): every HBM component is a `ManagedPeripheral`, so OC registers every name from `methods()` as a `PeripheralCallback` with a synthetic annotation `direct = true, limit = 100, doc = ""`, on BOTH direct wiring and proxy ports, and only then adds reflected `@Callback` methods whose names are not already listed. Consequences: annotations on listed names are ignored; a callback that must stay non-direct or rate-limited must be left OUT of `methods()` (still reachable by reflection when a cable touches the core, but not through ports); OC skips its per-class cache for `ManagedPeripheral` hosts, but each component node memoises the result (`server/network/Component.scala:25`, `private lazy val callbacks = Callbacks(host)`), so `methods()` and the reflected list are read once per node at first use, not per call, and a changed `methods()` result only takes effect when the node is recreated (chunk reload, re-placement).
- Returns: `new Object[] {}` void; `{true}/{false}`; `{null, "message"}` error tuple; aggregate `getInfo`; `getEnergyInfo` = `{power, max}`; `getPos` = `{x, y, z}`; tables as `LinkedHashMap<String, Object>` or `String[]`; any boxed Number passes through.
- Proxy forwarding requires the port dummies to be `TileEntityProxyCombo().power()` or `.fluid()` and metadata 6..11; `canConnectNode` is consulted on the core too.
- Node lifecycle (GTNH OC 1.12.55 sources; the 1.12.62 injector wraps the same five methods through `*_OpenComputers` delegators): the injected `node()` (`common/asm/template/StaticSimpleEnvironment.java:25-47`) re-reads `getComponentName()` on every call and creates the node the first time the name is non-empty. It never renames an existing node, and removes it only on a null/empty name, `invalidate`, `onChunkUnload` or server stop. For a loaded tile the first call is the wrapped `readFromNBT` (L72-78, after the original, before `worldObj` is set), hence the proxy's `ocname` cache (a missing key reads as `""` and creates no node yet). Otherwise it is `Network.joinOrCreateNetwork`, which `validate()` schedules for the next server tick START, or a neighbour's join; both call `node()` only on sides where `canConnectNode` is true. A proxy that answers `ntm_null` at that first creation keeps that name until invalidate or chunk unload, and its method list is memoised per node (`server/network/Component.scala:25`).
- Floppies: `disks.put(name, new FloppyDisk(name, OCColors.X.ordinal()))`; `fromClass(MainRegistry.class, RefStrings.MODID, "disks/" + sanitizeName(name))`; only `PWRangler` (cyan) ships.
- OC API stability: `Items.registerFloppy`, `FileSystem.fromClass`/`asReadOnly` and `SimpleComponent.SkipInjection` (RUNTIME) are identical in the MightyPirates `1.7.10-forge~1.8.9` api jar and the GTNH `1.12.58-GTNH-dev` jar. Against the owner's runtime, GTNH OC 1.12.62, there is no API incompatibility: all 22 member refs and 19 class refs the fork jar makes into `li/cil/oc` resolve with identical descriptors and access, the `@Callback` element defaults are identical, and every OC interface the fork implements is complete. The only differences across the 191 api classes are `TextBuffer.dropFile` (runtime only) and the prefab `TileEntityEnvironment`/`TileEntitySidedEnvironment` methods (MCP-named in the api jar, SRG-named at runtime); the fork uses neither, so the MightyPirates api jar stays a safe compile target. GTNH OC 1.12.55 (sources, api, dev) and 1.12.58 (dev) jars are in the local Gradle cache (`~/.gradle/caches/modules-2/files-2.1/com.github.GTNewHorizons/OpenComputers/`) for further checks.
- OC-LuaJIT relation: `Machine.add(LuaJITArchitecture.class)` (`OCLuaJIT.java:67`). A `NativeLuaArchitecture` subclass owning the VM factory, persistence and a kernel swap in `initialize()`: its patched `machine.lua` changes the deadline hook, `_ENV` binding, `__persist` and the iteration of `component.list`/`componentProxy.__pairs`. Native component invocation (`ComponentAPI` -> `ArgumentsImpl`), argument boxing and return marshalling (`Registry.convert`) stay OC's. HBM emits no OC signals. Only three HBM behaviours depend on marshalling details (`Map.containsKey(Integer)` in `setCustomMapValues`, `checkAny == null` in Telex, mixed boxed numeric returns), all inherited unchanged.
- `checkTable` (native architectures, GTNH OC 1.12.58 bytecode; in 1.12.62 `ExtendedLuaState.toSimpleJavaObject` turns a Lua table into `toJavaObject(index, Map.class)`) returns JNLua's live `AbstractTableMap` proxy. Its `containsKey` pushes the Java key into Lua (`pushJavaObject` + `getTable`), so boxed Integer keys match, and `setCustomMapValues` works. This holds under OC-LuaJIT too (verified 2026-09-26: `LuaStateLuaJIT extends LuaState` and uses OC's native argument path unchanged, same converter). On the LuaJ architecture, which the owner's instance registers (`registerLuaJArchitecture=true`; default CPUs are Lua 5.3), OC builds a Scala map: integer keys still match through Scala's numeric equality, but string values arrive as `byte[]`, so `setCustomMapValues` sets nothing (B-328).

### How-to

- Single-block component: annotations + `implements SimpleComponent, CompatHandler.OCComponent`; `getComponentName()` unique `ntm_*`; `getX` callbacks `direct = true`; setters clamp/validate, write fields only and return `{}` or an error tuple. To persist from a direct callback use `markChanged()` (`TileEntityLoadedBase.java:42-44`, chunk-modified flag only; exemplar `TileEntityPWRController.setLevel` L636-641), not vanilla `markDirty()`, which also reads block metadata and fires `onNeighborChange` on the horizontal neighbours (43 existing direct callbacks, mostly RBMK panels, still do this). No world mutation in direct callbacks: anything that spawns entities, sets blocks or notifies neighbours must be a bare (non-direct) `@Callback` kept out of `methods()`. Add `getInfo`. Exemplar `TileEntityGeiger.java`.
- Multiblock component: everything above plus `methods()` (`String[]` of names) and `invoke(String, Context, Arguments)` (`switch` + `throw new NoSuchMethodException()`); keep both in sync (nothing checks); leave non-direct callbacks out of the list. Exemplar `TileEntityMachineFluidTank.java`.
- Subclass callbacks: add annotated methods; if the base has `methods()`/`invoke()`, override both re-listing the FULL set (`TileEntityTurretArty` is the only genuine re-listing exemplar and it drops `getPos`); to change a return shape, override with the same annotations. Never mention `SimpleComponent` in the subclass (double injection, see Gotchas); give it its own name by overriding `getComponentName()`.
- Lua table / error / optional args: `LinkedHashMap` + `new Object[] {map}`; `{null, "reason"}`; `args.checkTable(0)` with boxed Integer keys 1..N; `args.optInteger(i, default)`; for optional strings use `args.count()`/`args.isString(i)`/`optString` (`checkAny` throws "value expected, got no value" when fewer arguments are passed; it returns null only for an explicit nil).
- Restrict sides: override `@Optional.Method public boolean canConnectNode(ForgeDirection side)`. Exemplar `TileEntityTurretBaseNT`.
- ROR (Redstone-over-Radio) endpoint: tile `implements IRORValueProvider` (`provideRORValue(String)` answering `VAL:<name>` queries) and/or `IRORInteractive` (`runRORFunction(String name, String[] params)` for `FUN:<name>!<param>` commands; `NAME_SEPARATOR = "!"`, `PARAM_SEPARATOR = ":"`, helpers `getCommand`/`getParams`/`parseInt`); `getFunctionInfo()` lists them for the reader/logic GUIs, and `TileEntityRadioTorchReader` lowercases the name before lookup, so compare lowercase. 42 providers / 27 interactives exist; `TileEntityProxyCombo` forwards both to the core.
- Addon or compat listener: `CompatExternal.registerRecipeRegisterListener(IRecipeRegisterListener)` (fires only in the defaults branch of `SerializableRecipe.initialize`) and `registerFluidRegisterListener(IFluidRegisterListener)` (fires in `Fluids.init` and `reloadFluids`). A new soft dependency follows `CompatHandler`/`AE2CompatHandler`: static `init()` called from `MainRegistry.PostLoad` behind `Loader.isModLoaded(modid)`, `@Optional.Method`/`@Optional.Interface` on every member touching the foreign API, `Compat.tryLoadItem(modid, name)` for items, and both gates (`Loader.isModLoaded` at init, `Compat.MOD_X` at registration) for conditional blocks/TEs.
- PermaSync field: area 16 how-to.
- Floppy disk: see area 17. If programs should run under OC-LuaJIT, keep them 5.2-safe: no 5.3 features (`//`, bitwise operators, `utf8`, `string.pack`, `math.type`/`tointeger`/`maxinteger`, reliance on the integer subtype), and no lexical `local _ENV = ...` rebinding (the kernel only emulates `_ENV` as a table field). `goto` and `bit32` are fine: OC-LuaJIT ships a real 5.2 `bit32` (`native/lj52shim.c`); LuaJIT's own `bit` is not exposed in the sandbox. `PWRangler.lua` currently uses `//` (L207/213/217/252/256) and would need `math.floor(a / b)` rewrites; the owner's instance defaults new CPUs to Lua 5.3 (`defaultLua53=true`), so it fails there only on CPUs switched to Lua 5.2, LuaJ or OC-LuaJIT (B-317).

### Gotchas

- `TileEntityWatz` and `TileEntityLaunchTable` implement `OCComponent` without a direct `SimpleComponent`, so OC never injects a node into the core. Watz still works through its ports (`Watz.java:33` fluid ProxyCombos plus its own `methods()`/`invoke()`; the listed `getComponentName` throws `NoSuchMethodException`). LaunchTable is dead as a component: its ports are legacy `TileEntityDummy` blocks (`LaunchTable.java:93-142`).
- 8 sites use `modid = "opencomputers"` (`TileEntityProxyCombo` x2 from upstream 6e5b689e; `TileEntityMachineFluidTank`, `TileEntityMachineBattery`, `TileEntityBatteryBase`, `TileEntityBarrel`, `TileEntityMachineCoker`, `TileEntityRBMKHeater` from other upstream commits). FML's `Loader.isModLoaded`/`ModAPIManager.hasAPI` are exact-match `containsKey` lookups, so the direct `li.cil.oc.api.network.SimpleComponent` is stripped from those 7 classes even with OC present. This is harmless. `ModClassLoader.addModAPITransformer` registers `ModAPITransformer` at mod discovery, and `LaunchClassLoader.registerTransformer` appends it after OC's coremod `ClassTransformer`, so OC has already injected its Environment implementation. `SimpleComponent` also stays inherited through `OCComponent`. The proxy's other entry (`iface = "com.hbm.handler.CompatHandler.OCComponent"`) never matches: `stripInterface` only does `replace('.', '/')`, and the nested interface is `CompatHandler$OCComponent`. So `OCComponent` always stays on the proxy and ports work. Normalising the `SimpleComponent` strings to `OpenComputers` and deleting the dead `OCComponent` entry changes no behaviour.
- `direct = true` callbacks, and every name listed in `methods()`, run on OC's worker threads. That includes real world mutations: `ntm_launch_pad.launch` (`TileEntityLaunchPadBase.java:522`, bare `@Callback` but listed) and `ntm_rocket_pad.launch` (`TileEntityLaunchPadRocket.java:616`) call `worldObj.spawnEntityInWorld` off-thread (L361 / L272). `TileEntityTurretArty.addCoords` mutates `targetQueue` (an `ArrayList`, `TileEntityTurretBaseArtillery.java:20`, that the server tick reads and removes from). 43 direct callbacks call vanilla `markDirty()`, which runs neighbour `onNeighborChange` updates. RBMK console/control, PWR, the Telex getters and `clearAll`, and the radio torch (reflection-only classes) also run there. The Telex's bare `setChannels`/`setSendingText`/`printMessage`/`sendMessage` run on the server thread. `worldObj.isRemote` checks in callbacks are dead code (`TileEntityCraneConsole.move`).
- Double injection: under GTNH OC (the constant-pool trigger above), a subclass of an already-injected HBM TE that mentions `SimpleComponent` in any way (implements, cast, `instanceof`, class literal, interface call) is injected a second time. The child's `*_OpenComputers` delegators `invokespecial` into the parent's injected wrapper, which dispatches back to the child, so `validate`, `invalidate`, `onChunkUnload`, `readFromNBT` and `writeToNBT` recurse into a `StackOverflowError` (chunk loading crashes for every tile of that class). Nothing triggers it today: 29 subclasses of 10 injected parents exist (TurretBaseNT 14, Barrel 3, BatteryBase, LaunchPadBase, RBMKControl, RadioTorchBase 2 each, MachineBattery, RadarNT, RBMKRod, ProxyCombo 1 each) and none references `SimpleComponent`. Put `implements SimpleComponent` only on the topmost component TE of a hierarchy.
- `args.checkInteger` truncates Lua doubles and HBM narrows further (`(short)` in `setModeLow`).
- `steamTypeToInt` returns `Object[]`; unwrap `[0]` when composing.
- `TileEntityTurretBaseArtillery.getCurrentTarget` (L87) does `targetQueue.get(0)` without an empty check.
- `TileEntityTurretBaseNT.removeWhitelist` (L948-956) dereferences `getWhitelist()` without the null check `addWhitelist` has (L939); `getWhitelist()` (L383-396) returns null when no turret chip is inserted or the chip holds no names (`ItemTurretBiometry.getNames` L38-51 returns null for a chip without NBT or with `playercount` 0), so the call throws an NPE.
- `@Optional.Method` also strips `getComponentName()`/`canConnectNode()` without OC; never call them from non-OC code.
- `TileEntityMicrowave` ships test callbacks (`test`, `variableget`, `variableset`).
- Component-name reuse with divergent APIs (`ntm_turbine` x4, `ntm_energy_storage` x3, `ntm_artillery` x2: through ports Arty exposes 14 names without `getPos` and HIMARS the base 12 with `getPos`; wired to the core both expose the same 15, but Arty's `addCoords` runs direct and HIMARS's does not).
- Smells: `// :vomit:` at `TileEntityTurretBaseNT.java:1013`/`TileEntityTurretArty.java:472`; `TileEntityProxyCombo.java:47-48` early-name-lookup rant and L501 `// please work`; `CompatHandler.java:251` SkipInjection comment; `TileEntityCraneConsole` "if this doesnt work im going to die"; `TileEntityRadioTelex.java:299`; 20 of 69 callback files use the `// do some opencomputer stuff` marker; `limit = 4` on setters is inconsistent (some setters plain direct, FluidPump limits getters too); 22 of the 35 `limit = 4` and 8 of the 17 bare `@Callback` annotations are inert because their names are listed in `methods()` (`limit = 4`: FluidPump x7, TurbineGas x4, CombustionEngine x3, TurretBaseNT x2, RadarNT, Zirnox, FusionKlystron, LaunchPadRocket, Chungus, LargeTurbine; bare: LaunchPadBase `launch`, LaunchTable x6, TurretArty `addCoords`); `CompatHandler.init()` logs through `LogManager.getLogger("HBM")` (L192) instead of `MainRegistry.logger`; `getComponentName` also lacks `@Override` in `TileEntityFluidCounterValve.java:87` and `TileEntityRBMKCooler.java:149`.

### Open questions

The owner's four latest client logs (2026-09-21/22) show no OC error naming HBM.
